children.text: Śrī Śrī-nivāsāya námaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to <s>Śrī Śrīnivāsa</s>.

children.text:
Śrī-vaikhānasa-mantra-praśnāṣṭake
Pañcama praśna prārambhaḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śrī Vaikhānasa Mantra Praśna</s>, the collection of eight sections: Beginning of the Fifth Section.

children.text:
5.1.1.1 hariḥ oṃ
príyátāṃ bhágavān viṣṇus sarvá-deveśvaró hariḥ
śrīvatsāṅkás[*1] sahasrākṣas sahásra-caraṇás tathā
5.1.1.2 jitán te puṇḍarīkākṣa namás te viśva-bhā́vana
námas te 'stú hr̥ṣīkeśa mahā́-puruṣa pū́rva-ja
5.1.1.3 bhávantu sárvāḥ[*2] puṇyākhyā nimíttāś śobhanā́nvitāḥ
tvat-prasādā́d vayaṃ viṣṇo tavá dāsās samā́gatāḥ
5.1.1.4 sādhayāmó vimānaṃ te prasā́daṃ kuru nó bhavān
sāhāyyáṃ sárva-bhr̥tyās te kurvántu tava śā́sanāt
5.1.1.5 śāntá-vīśā́ri-bhūtādīn[*3] visŕ̥jāsmābhir éva tu
anapāyī́ prayātv agre chitvā́ vighnaṃ punáḥ-punaḥ
[*1] Irregular bahu-vrīhi accentuation. cf. A Vedic Grammar for Students, A.A. MacDonell, page 455a.
[*2] Underlined syllables receive a “double svarita,” two parallel vertical lines above the syllable, in the published text.
[*3] cf. Kāśyapa Jñāna Kāṇḍaḥ, chapter 34, vīśa-hīne ripu-vr̥ddhiḥ.
children.translated_text: (5.1.1.1) <s>Hariḥ Oṃ</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> be pleased — <s>Hari</s>, lord of all the gods, bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, thousand-eyed, and likewise thousand-footed. (5.1.1.2) Victory to you, O Lotus-eyed One! Obeisance to you, O Creator of the universe! Obeisance to you, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (Lord of the senses), O Great Being, O Primeval One! (5.1.1.3) May all auspicious omens arise, accompanied by good fortune. By your grace, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, we, your servants, have assembled. (5.1.1.4) We shall construct your temple (<s>vimāna</s>) — bestow your grace upon us, O Lord! May all your servants render assistance at your command. (5.1.1.5) Having pacified the spirits — <s>vīśāri</s>-demons, <s>bhūtas</s>, and others — we ourselves [shall proceed]. May the Imperishable One go forth at the head, cutting down obstacles again and again. [Footnotes: *1 Irregular <s>bahuvrīhi</s> accentuation. *2 Double <s>svarita</s> marking. *3 Cf. <s>Kāśyapa Jñāna Kāṇḍa</s>, ch. 34.]

children.text:
5.1.2.1 pŕ̥ṣṭhe ca nándako yātu gadā́ vāmaṃ surákṣatu
śaṅkha-śaktītáre pārśve yatétāṃ kārya-síddhaye
5.1.2.2 śéṣā gacchántu cāsmābhiḥ prasā́dāt tava sárvaśaḥ
tvat-prasādā́d vayaṃ vīra karíṣyāmó gr̥háṃ tava
5.1.2.3 yáthopaláṃ dahat sūrya-tanúm uṣṇatvam ā́śritaḥ[*4]
táthā vayáṃ hi tvad-vīryā́c chuśrū́ṣām anupālaya
5.1.2.4 asti cét káruṇā tvattáś cāsmā́kaṃ dāsa-kármaṇām
anumantā́ bhava prītas sarvé yācāmahé vayam
5.1.2.5 índraś śatá-kratur vīrás sarvá-rājaś śacī́-patiḥ
príyátā́ṃ bhágavān viṣṇuḥ sarvá-loka-śubhá-pradaḥ
[*4] The published text gives the following variant which I have translated in the English: yáthopaláṃ dáhyate sūryād anúṣṇám uṣṇatvam ā́śritam.
children.translated_text: (5.1.2.1) And may <s>Nandaka</s> (the sword) go behind; may the <s>gadā</s> (mace) protect the left. May the conch and <s>śakti</s> (spear) strive on the other two sides for the accomplishment of the task. (5.1.2.2) And may the rest go with us, by your grace, in every direction. By your grace, O hero, we shall build your dwelling. (5.1.2.3) Just as the sun, having assumed the nature of heat, burns stone, so we too, by your valor, carry out devoted service. (5.1.2.4) If there be compassion from you toward us who perform the service of servants, be pleased and consent — we all beseech you. (5.1.2.5) May <s>Indra</s>, the hundred-sacrificed hero, king of all, lord of <s>Śacī</s>, be pleased. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the bestower of auspiciousness to all worlds, [be pleased]. [Footnote: *4 Variant reading translated in the English: 'Just as a stone is burned by the sun — though not hot itself, having acquired heat.']

children.text:
5.1.3.1 agnir agryáḥ pavitrāṇāṃ devā́nām agra-gó hariḥ
príyátā́ṃ bhágavān viṣṇus sarvá-bhoktā sukhā́vahaḥ
5.1.3.2 sarva-lokódbhavo viṣṇúr yamó yama-karáḥ prajāḥ
príyátā́ṃ dáṇḍa-bhr̥n netā dharmā́tmā dharma-pā́lakaḥ
5.1.3.3 prájā rakṣan vinighnan vai yātúdhānān ajáḥ prabhuḥ
nírŕ̥tíḥ príyatāṃ nīlo nīlótpala-dalá[*5]-prabhaḥ
5.1.3.4 várúṇáḥ prácetā bhagavān vikrámī yajña-pā́lakaḥ
ráktāmbará-dharo vīraḥ priyátām prabhur ávyayaḥ
5.1.3.5 vā́yus sarvā́tmako bhadra udā́no javanó marut
príyátā́ṃ bhágavān prāṇaś śacī́-pati-sakhā́ prabhuḥ
5.1.3.6 rāja-rājó dhanādhyakṣaḥ kubéro viśravás-sutaḥ
príyátā́ṃ nídhí-sáṃyukta īśvárasya sakhā́ prabhuḥ
5.1.3.7 īśas tri-lócanaś śūlī vr̥ṣábha-dhvaja-vā́hanaḥ
príyátā́ṃ gáṇa-bhr̥n nityaṃ try-ambáko 'mbara-sánnibhaḥ
5.1.3.8 bráhmā pitā́maho vīro vedá-vaktā vr̥ṣā́-kapiḥ
príyátā́ṃ pádma-garbhābho viṣṇú-putro virā́ṭ svarāṭ
5.1.3.9 diṅ-nāgā́ nā́ga-saṅghāś ca sarvā́ś cāntara-dévatāḥ
rávy-ādayó grahā bhūtā r̥ṣáyas siddha-cā́raṇāḥ príyátā́ṃ gáṇa-saṃyuktā́ḥ kurvántu ca sahā́yatām
[*5] Text: daḷá
children.translated_text: (5.1.3.1) <s>Agni</s> is the foremost among purifiers; <s>Hari</s> is the chief among the gods. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the enjoyer of all offerings and the bringer of happiness, be pleased. (5.1.3.2) <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the origin of all worlds, is <s>Yama</s>, the subduer of creatures. May the bearer of the rod, the guide, the righteous soul, the protector of <s>dharma</s>, be pleased. (5.1.3.3) Protecting creatures and destroying <s>Yātudhānas</s> (demons), the Unborn Lord — may <s>Nirṛti</s> be pleased, the dark one, radiant as a blue lotus petal. (5.1.3.4) <s>Varuṇa</s>, the wise <s>Bhagavān</s>, the valiant protector of sacrifice, wearing red garments, the hero — may the imperishable Lord be pleased. (5.1.3.5) <s>Vāyu</s>, the all-pervading, the auspicious, the upward-breath, the swift wind — may the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Prāṇa</s> (Life-breath), friend of the lord of <s>Śacī</s>, the Lord, be pleased. (5.1.3.6) <s>Kubera</s>, king of kings, lord of wealth, son of <s>Viśravas</s> — may the one joined with treasures, friend of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), the master, be pleased. (5.1.3.7) <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva), the three-eyed, the trident-bearer, whose vehicle is the bull — may the lord of <s>Gaṇas</s>, the eternal <s>Tryambaka</s>, radiant as the sky, be pleased. (5.1.3.8) <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather, the hero, the speaker of the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Vṛṣākapī</s> — may the one radiant as a lotus-interior, the son of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Universal Sovereign, the Self-Sovereign, be pleased. (5.1.3.9) The guardian elephants of the directions, the hosts of <s>Nāgas</s>, all the intermediate deities, the planets beginning with the Sun, the beings, the <s>Ṛṣis</s>, the <s>Siddhas</s>, and the <s>Cāraṇas</s> — may they be pleased together with their hosts and render assistance. [Footnote: *5 Text: daḷá]

children.text: 5.1.0.1 punáḥ punaś śubhá-pradaḥ prabhur náva ca
children.translated_text: (5.1.0.1) [Rubric:] Again and again the auspicious Lord and the nine [offerings].

5.1.4.1 rudráṃ bhūtám índraṃ yamám mātr̥̄s sómaṃ vīrám rudrám índraṃ yamáṃ vr̥kṣéndrān
5.1.4.2 vánas-pátibhyo námaḥ
5.1.4.3 kumārī́bhyo námaḥ
5.1.4.4 vr̥kṣa-rājébhyo námaḥ
5.1.4.5 sarva-kāma-pradébhyo námaḥ
5.1.4.6 agnáye svā́hā
5.1.4.7 vana-rājā́ya svā́hā
5.1.4.8 sómāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: (5.1.4.1) [To] <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Bhūta</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the <s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers), <s>Soma</s>, the Hero, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the lords of trees — (5.1.4.2) Obeisance to the lords of the forest! (5.1.4.3) Obeisance to the maidens! (5.1.4.4) Obeisance to the lords of trees! (5.1.4.5) Obeisance to the bestowers of all desires! (5.1.4.6) To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.4.7) To the King of the Forest, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.4.8) To <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

5.1.5.2 śākhā́ya svā́hā
5.1.5.3 sthūla-lākṣā́ya svā́hā
5.1.5.4 vyādhā́ya svā́hā
5.1.5.5 mr̥ga-rūpíṇe svā́hā
5.1.5.6 vánas-pátibhyas svā́hā
5.1.5.7 kumārī́bhyas svā́hā
5.1.5.8 vallī́bhyas svā́hā
5.1.5.9 kusumā́ya svā́hā
5.1.5.10 śalā́ṭave svā́hā
children.translated_text: (5.1.5.1) To <s>Yama</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.2) To the Branch, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.3) To the Thick-resinous One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.4) To the Hunter, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.5) To the One in Deer Form, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.6) To the Lords of the Forest, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.7) To the Maidens, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.8) To the Creepers, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.9) To the Flower, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.5.10) To the Unripe Fruit, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
5.1.6.1 br̥hat-váce svā́hā
5.1.6.2 puṇyā́ya svā́hā
5.1.6.3 amita-tejáse svā́hā
5.1.6.4 sū́ryāya svā́hā
5.1.6.5 sūrya-rūpā́ya svā́hā
5.1.6.6 śr̥ṅgíṇe svā́hā
5.1.6.7 bhūta-rūpíṇe svā́hā
5.1.6.8 nāga-hastā́ya svā́hā
5.1.6.9 divyā́ya svā́hā
5.1.6.10 tri-hastā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: (5.1.6.1) To the Great-voiced One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.2) To the Meritorious One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.3) To the One of Immeasurable Radiance, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.4) To <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.5) To the One in the Form of the Sun, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.6) To the Horned One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.7) To the One in the Form of a Being, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.8) To the Elephant-trunked One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.9) To the Divine One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.6.10) To the Three-handed One, <s>svāhā</s>!

5.1.7.1 vighnā́ya svā́hā
5.1.7.2 vighná-rūpā́ya svā́hā
5.1.7.3 vināyakā́ya svā́hā
5.1.7.4 prasā́ríṇe svā́hā
5.1.7.5 muruṇḍā́ya svā́hā

5.1.7.7 nāgébhyas svā́hā
5.1.7.8 bhūta-rājébhyas svā́hā
5.1.7.9 cāraṇébhyas svā́hā
5.1.7.10 divā-carébhyas svā́hā
children.translated_text: (5.1.7.1) To the Obstacle, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.2) To the One in the Form of Obstacles, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.3) To <s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.4) To the One Who Extends, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.5) To <s>Muruṇḍa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.6) To <s>Nyarṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.7) To the <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.8) To the Lords of Beings, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.9) To the <s>Cāraṇas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.7.10) To the Day-wanderers, <s>svāhā</s>!

5.1.8.3 sandhyā́-carébhyas svā́hā

5.1.8.13 sthāna-devébhyas svā́hā
5.1.8.14 vidyādharébhyas svā́hā

children.translated_text: (5.1.8.1) To the Night-wanderers, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.2) To the Twilights, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.3) To the Twilight-wanderers, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.4) To the <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.5) To the <s>Yakṣīs</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.6) To the Maidens, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.7) To the <s>Āsurī</s> (demonesses), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.8) To the <s>Rākṣasīs</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.9) To the <s>Piśācīs</s> (female ghouls), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.10) To the Forest, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.11) To the Ground-wanderer, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.12) To the Tree-gods, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.13) To the Place-gods, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.14) To the <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.15) To the Form-bearers, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.16) To the Pairs, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.17) To the Pleasures, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.8.18) To the Earth, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 5.1.0.2 sómāya svā́hā śalā́táve svā́hā tri-hastā́ya svā́hā divā-carébhyas svā́hā vanā́ya svā́hā áṣṭaú ca
children.translated_text: (5.1.0.2) [Rubric:] To <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to the Unripe Fruit, <s>svāhā</s>; to the Three-handed One, <s>svāhā</s>; to the Day-wanderers, <s>svāhā</s>; to the Forest, <s>svāhā</s> — [these are] the eight [concluding offerings of each group].

children.text:
5.1.9.1 nírdagdha(g)ṃ rákṣaḥ
5.1.9.2 sarveśvarā́ya svā́hā
5.1.9.3 jagannāthā́ya svā́hā
5.1.9.4 cāmuṇḍā́ya svā́hā
5.1.9.5 sarvataś-carā́ya svā́hā
5.1.9.6 brahmā́ṇyai svā́hā
5.1.9.7 piṅgalā́yai[*6] svā́hā
5.1.9.8 gaúryai svā́hā
5.1.9.9 sárváto-mukhyai svā́hā
5.1.9.10 sarit-priyā́yai svā́hā
[*6] Text: piṅgaḷā́yai
children.translated_text: (5.1.9.1) May the <s>Rākṣas</s> (demon) be burned up! (5.1.9.2) To the Lord of All, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.3) To the Lord of the World, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.4) To <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.5) To the All-wanderer, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.6) To <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.7) To <s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.8) To <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.9) To the All-faced One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.9.10) To the River-loving One, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnote: *6 Text: piṅgaḷāyai]

children.text:

5.1.10.2 ugrā́yai svā́hā
5.1.10.3 gaṇeśvaryai svā́hā
5.1.10.4 vaiśākhínyai svā́hā
5.1.10.5 śikhaṇḍínyai svā́hā
5.1.10.6 gāyátryai svā́hā
5.1.10.7 ṣaṇ-múkhyai svā́hā
5.1.10.8 viśva-garbhā́yai svā́hā
5.1.10.9 viṣórmiṇyai svā́hā
5.1.10.10 kr̥ṣṇā́yai svā́hā
children.translated_text: (5.1.10.1) To the One of Universal Form, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.2) To the Fierce One (<s>Ugrā</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.3) To the Lady of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.4) To <s>Vaiśākhinī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.5) To <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> (the Crested One), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.6) To <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.7) To the Six-faced One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.8) To the One Bearing the Universe in Her Womb, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.9) To <s>Viṣūrmiṇī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.10.10) To <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (the Dark One), <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:

children.translated_text: (5.1.11.1) To <s>Druhiṇī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.2) To <s>Vārāhī</s> (the Boar Goddess), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.3) To the Boon-giver, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.4) To the Vast One (<s>Urvī</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.5) To the Diamond-fanged One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.6) To the Victorious One (<s>Jayantī</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.7) To <s>Kauśikī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.8) To <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.9) To <s>Ghanāghanā</s> (Cloud upon Cloud), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.10) To <s>Kālī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.11) To the Lotus-fanged One, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.12) To <s>Vṛṣabhā</s> (the Bull Goddess), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.13) To the Bearer of the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.14) To the Curved-trunked One (<s>Vakratuṇḍa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.15) To the Single-tusked One (<s>Ekadaṃṣṭra</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.16) To the Formidable One (<s>Vikaṭa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.17) To <s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.11.18) To the Earth, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes: *7 Text: kāḷyai. *8 Text: nāḷīka. *9 1926 ed.: vṛṣabhāyai; 1946, 1984 eds.: vṛṣahāyai]

children.text:
5.1.0.3 sarit-priyā́yai svā́hā kr̥ṣṇā́yai svā́hā kālyai[*10] svā́hā aṣṭāú ca

children.translated_text: (5.1.0.3) [Rubric:] To the River-loving One, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Kālī</s>, <s>svāhā</s> — [these are] the eight [concluding offerings]. [Footnote: *10 Text: kāḷyai]

children.text:

5.1.12.2 dhārāsu saptású

svasti-dā́ viśás pátiḥ[*12]
5.1.12.4 nārāyaṇā́ya
5.1.12.5 oṃ śéṣam ā́vāhayāmi
5.1.12.6 medínīm ā́vāhayāmi
5.1.12.7 jyéṣṭhām ā́vāhayāmi
5.1.12.8 vā́yum ā́vāhayāmi
5.1.12.9 índram ā́vāhayāmi
5.1.12.10 marúta ā́vāhayāmi

children.translated_text: 5.1.12.1 Pure are these animals. 5.1.12.2 In the seven streams. 5.1.12.3 May he measure out well-being for us; the lord of the people, the giver of well-being. 5.1.12.4 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. 5.1.12.5 <s>Oṃ</s>, I invoke <s>Śeṣa</s>. 5.1.12.6 I invoke <s>Medinī</s> (the Earth). 5.1.12.7 I invoke <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (the Eldest). 5.1.12.8 I invoke <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind). 5.1.12.9 I invoke <s>Indra</s>. 5.1.12.10 I invoke the <s>Maruts</s>. [Footnote 11: RV 5.51.11. Also ŚŚ 10.8.17, 12.8.9, 14.3.12; ŚG 1.4.2, 1.15.12, 2.6.2; AŚ 8.1.23, 9.5.5; MG 2.15.6.] [Footnote 12: RV 10.152.2a. Also found in RV 10.152.2; AV 1.21.1, 8.5.22; ŚB 5.1; AdB 1; TB 3.7.11.4; TA 10.1.9; TAA 10.55; Mahān U 20.5; ApŚ 3.12.1; VHDh 8.43.]

children.text:
5.1.13.1 ápā́ṃ pátim ā́vāhayāmi yámam ā́vāhayāmi sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānam[*13] sómam ā́vāhayāmi[*14]
5.1.13.2 sárva-jít sárva-śatru-ghno 'mogho 'pratima-vī́ryavān
āyā́tú bhágavāṃś cakras sarvá-saṃhāra-vártakaḥ
5.1.13.3 oṃ bhū́r bhúvas súvas su-bhū́ svayam-bhū́ḥ
5.1.13.4 vainateyó mahā-vīryaḥ kāśyápo 'gni-samá-prabhaḥ
āyā́tú bhágavān rājā sarpá-jid viṣṇu-vā́hanaḥ
5.1.13.5 astv āsanám..
5.1.13.6 svāgatáṃ pákṣi-rājāya sarpā́śe viśva-kármaṇe
aṇḍa-jānā́ṃ variṣṭhāya viṣṇúnā sama-téjase
5.1.13.7 anumantā́ bhava prītas tavá bhártúḥ kriyā́ṃ prati
svayá(g)ṃ[*15] sarvám ánujñānair gr̥hyátām idam ávyayaḥ
5.1.13.8 yóge-yoge[*16]
5.1.13.9 āpo hí ṣṭhā́ mayo-bhúvas[*17] tát[*18] savitúḥ
5.1.13.10 cit-pátis tvā tejovát syāvaḥ
5.1.13.11 ihá púṣṭiṃ púṣṭi-patir dadhātv ihá prajā́(g)ṃ ramayatu[*19]
5.1.13.12 prajā́-pataye puṣṭi-pátáye 'gni-patáye ráyi-pataye kā́māyānnā́dyāya[*20]
[*13] somaṃ rājānam (pratīka): KhG 3.2.20; Svidh 2.3.2; Vāit 15.16. Cf. ViDh 56.17, 56.24; VāDh 28.13ñ14; LAtDh 3.12; VAtDh 3.12.
[*14] somam ā vaha: TS 2.5.9.4; KB 8.8; ŚB 1.4.2.16, 2.6.1.22; TB 3.5.3.2; ŚŚ 1.5.2, 5.11.4.
[*15] The consonant g is occasionally inserted into the text to indicate an anusvāra.
[*16] RV 1.30.7. The RV phrase yóge-yoge tavástaraṃ is also given in AV 10.24.7, 20.26.1; SV 1.163, 2.93; VS 11.14; TS 4.1.2.1, 5.1.2.1; MS 2.7.2: 75.5, 3.1.3: 3.21; KS 16.1, 10.2; PB 9.2.20; ŚB 6.3.2.4; AS 6.4.10; Vait 26.12; ApŚ 16.2.3; MŚ 6.1.1; ApMB 1.6.3, 2.4.1; ApG 2.5.20, 4.11.6; HG 1.4.11.
[*17] RV 10.9.1. The words ā́po hí ṣṭhā mayo-bhúvaḥ are also found in: AV 1.5.1; SV 2.1187; VS 11.50, 36.14; TS 4.1.5.1, 5.6.1.4, 7.4.19.4; MS 2.7.5: 79.16, 3.1.6: 8.10, 4.9.27: 139.3; KS 16.4, 19.5, 35.3; ŚB 6.5.1.2; TB 3.9.7.5; TA 4.42.4, 10.1.11; ApŚ 7.21.6, 9.12.2. 9.18.8, 13.15.13, 14.18.1, 16.4.1; etc.
[*18] Text: tátth
[*19] VS (K) 3.2.5.
[*20] This is a paraphrase of VS (K) 3.2.5, agnáye gr̥há-pataye rayimáte púṣṭi-pataye svā́hā. agnáye 'nnādā́yā́nna-pataye svā́hā.
children.translated_text: 5.1.13.1 I invoke the Lord of the Waters; I invoke <s>Yama</s>; King <s>Soma</s>; I invoke <s>Soma</s>. 5.1.13.2 The all-conquering, all-enemy-slaying, infallible, of incomparable valor — may the blessed <s>Cakra</s> (Discus), the agent of total annihilation, come. 5.1.13.3 <s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvas su-bhūḥ svayam-bhūḥ</s> (the Self-existent). 5.1.13.4 <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), of great valor, descendant of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, of splendor equal to fire — may the blessed king come, the conqueror of serpents, the vehicle of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. 5.1.13.5 Let there be a seat. 5.1.13.6 Welcome to the king of birds, the devourer of serpents, the maker of all, the foremost among the egg-born, of splendor equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s. 5.1.13.7 Be an approver, pleased, regarding the ritual of your master; you yourself, imperishable, by all your permissions — let this be accepted. 5.1.13.8 In every <s>yoga</s> (union). 5.1.13.9 For waters, indeed, you are the givers of joy; that of <s>Savitṛ</s>. 5.1.13.10 <s>Cit-pati</s> (Lord of Consciousness), may [the seat] be for you, radiant, dark. 5.1.13.11 May <s>Puṣṭi-pati</s> (Lord of Nourishment) bestow nourishment here; may he make progeny delightful here. 5.1.13.12 To <s>Prajā-pati</s> (Lord of Progeny), to <s>Puṣṭi-pati</s> (Lord of Nourishment), to <s>Agni-pati</s> (Lord of Fire), to <s>Rayi-pati</s> (Lord of Wealth), for desire, for food. [Footnotes 13-20 contain extensive cross-references to RV, TS, VS, ŚB, TB, and other Vedic texts.]

children.text: 5.1.0.4 marúṭa āvāyahayāmy astv āsanáṃ náva ca
children.translated_text: 5.1.0.4 [Catch-words:] 'I invoke the <s>Maruts</s>; let there be a seat' — and nine [mantras in this section].

children.text:
5.1.14.1 āyā́tú bhágavān divyo dāntáś śānto[*21] janá-priyaḥ
várṣíṣṭhás sárva-bhaktānāṃ sarvá-dā dhana-dó varaḥ[*22]
5.1.14.2 dhārāsu saptasú
5.1.14.3 áto devā́ kánikradaj janúṣam
5.1.14.4 priyatā́ṃ[*23] medínī devī́ yená śr̥ṅgeṇa códdhr̥tā
vīra-patnī́ viśālākṣī tasyā́yaṃ sthāna-nírṇaye
ávighnenaíva tam pātvā sādháyemaṃ varā́nane
5.1.14.5 medínī devī́
5.1.14.6 námo váruṇaḥ
5.1.14.7 akṣaír mā́ dīvyaḥ kr̥ṣim ít kŕ̥ṣásvá vitté rámasva bahu mányamānaḥ[*24]
[*21] The 1946 published edition gives the variant reading śānto dānto.
[*22] Compare the unusual accents here with 5.1.1.1, príyátāṃ bhágavān viṣṇus.
[*23] Here priyatā́ṃ has only one accent.
[*24] RV 10.34.13ab
children.translated_text: 5.1.14.1 May the blessed divine one come — tamed, peaceful, dear to people, most generous of all devotees, the best, the giver of wealth always. 5.1.14.2 In the seven streams. 5.1.14.3 Then the god, crying aloud, from birth... 5.1.14.4 May the beloved goddess <s>Medinī</s> (Earth) be pleased — she by whose horn she was lifted up, the wife of a hero, wide-eyed — for her, in this determination of place, without obstacle, having protected that, let us accomplish this, O fair-faced one. 5.1.14.5 The goddess <s>Medinī</s>. 5.1.14.6 Obeisance to <s>Varuṇa</s>. 5.1.14.7 Do not play with dice; do farming indeed; rejoice in wealth, esteeming it highly. [Footnotes 21-24 contain variant readings and cross-references to RV 10.34.13ab and other texts.]

children.text:
5.1.15.1 tátra gā́vaḥ kítava tátra jā́yā tán me ví caṣṭe savitā́yam áryaḥ[*25]
5.1.15.2 tváṃ vr̥ṣabhas tváṃ purātanas tváṃ vai paurāṇikás tváṃ vaídikas tváṃ cátuś-śr̥ṅgaḥ[*26]
5.1.15.3 tvā́ṃ evā́ha mánu[r] yokṣye váhasva[*27] devārthaṃ vī́ra dhuráṃ vī́ras tvám
5.1.15.4 śaúrabheya suréśa-vāhana vī́śasyāṃśa vī́śa-sakha gópate
5.1.15.5 víṣṇor imā́ṃ bhū́miṃ bhavanārthaṃ kr̥ṣasva
5.1.15.6 yúgaṃ yúga-śr̥ṅgaṃ yúñjāmi yógārtham[*28]
5.1.15.7 ŕ̥ṣiṃ gr̥hṇāmi kraṣṭúṃ múnīnā́ṃ śā́sanāt[*29]
5.1.15.8 víṣṇur mā́ṃ rakṣatu
5.1.15.9 yé 'smin deśé jīvantáḥ prā́ṇino rakṣā(g)ṃsi bhū́tāḥ. píśācinyo 'nya-devá-yutāś śruṇudhva(g)ṃ sárveśasyedáṃ sthā́naṃ bhávanāya kálpitam
5.1.15.10 gácchantu yathéṣṭam asmā́d rámaṇīyam anyad bhadráṃ vo astu svastí bhavatu
5.1.15.11 hála-kr̥ṣṭā́ diváṃ gacchantu márditā vāyú-lokam. śramā́rtā amártyatām
5.1.15.12 yathā́vac cāhared vīryam
5.1.15.13 sárveṣāṃ cákṣur ādityáḥ príyatā(g)ṃ śubhā́ny eva kriyatā́m daítyārir bhágavān itáḥ
[*25] RV 10.34.13cd Our text differs from the RV in the accentuation of the following words: kitava, jāyā, āyam, and aryaḥ.
[*26] cf. RV 4.58.2; BhP 5.20.15
[*27] cj RV 8.26.23
[*28] Text: yógārdham
[*29] The published text gives here as an additional reading at the bottom of the page: (rudram anyaṃ try-ambakam iti marīciḥ). The words “the published text” indicate both the 1946 and 1984 editions.
children.translated_text: 5.1.15.1 There are the cows, O gambler; there the wife — this noble <s>Savitṛ</s> shows to me. 5.1.15.2 You are the bull; you are the ancient one; you are indeed the <s>Purāṇic</s> one; you are the Vedic one; you are the four-horned one. 5.1.15.3 You alone <s>Manu</s> yokes: 'Carry, O hero, the burden for the sake of the gods; you are a hero.' 5.1.15.4 O son of <s>Surabhī</s>, O vehicle of the Lord of the gods, O portion of the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, O friend of the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, O lord of cows — 5.1.15.5 plough this earth of <s>Viṣṇu</s> for the purpose of a dwelling. 5.1.15.6 I join the yoke and the yoke-horn for the purpose of yoking. 5.1.15.7 I seize the sage (the plough) to plough, by the command of the sages. 5.1.15.8 May <s>Viṣṇu</s> protect me. 5.1.15.9 Those living beings — <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Piśācinīs</s>, and those joined with other deities — who live in this place, hear! This place has been designated as a dwelling for the Lord of all. 5.1.15.10 Let them go as they please from this place; another pleasant place [awaits] — may good fortune be upon you; may there be well-being. 5.1.15.11 Those ploughed [by the plough] go to heaven; those crushed go to the world of <s>Vāyu</s>; those fatigued with toil [attain] immortality. 5.1.15.12 And he should bring valor as is proper. 5.1.15.13 The sun is the eye of all; may the blessed enemy of the <s>Daityas</s> be pleased; may auspicious things alone be done from here. [Footnotes 25-29 contain cross-references to RV 10.34.13cd, RV 4.58.2, RV 8.26.23, and variant readings.]

children.text: 5.1.0.5 mányamāno bhávanāya kálpita(g)ṃ sapta ca
children.translated_text: 5.1.0.5 [Catch-words:] 'esteeming it highly; designated for a dwelling' — and seven [mantras in this section].

children.text:
5.1.16.1 imé bījā́ vrī́hi-yavā́ ruhantūṣṇā́ṃśu-prasādā́t
sómenā́rpitā grahaír nirvyā́dhikāś śuddhā́ś śubhā́ bhavantu
5.1.16.2 prároha-bījā́n nírvapāmi bhūmaú yé brahma-sr̥ṣṭā́ dáśa sapta caíva. té vardhitā vr̥ṣṭi-váśena sárve saṃpā́lyamānā hy amŕ̥tena lokā́n
5.1.16.3 saptá grāmyās sáptá cāraṇyakā́ś ca yé gharma-naṣṭā́ himá-varṣa-sr̥ṣṭā́s té vr̥ṣṭi-bhūtā́ hy amŕ̥taṃ rakṣantu
5.1.16.4 dīrṇā́rdra-saṃśuṣká-vivárdhamānā mū́laiḥ phalaíś śā́kais sámr̥ddha[*30]-rūpaíḥ
annéná martyānāṃ[*31] havíṣā surāṇā́n té vai ruhantā́ṃ tr̥ṇávat paśúbhyaḥ
5.1.16.5 tā́n bhūmi-śuddhyaí nírvapāmi bījā́n devá-sthiti-kā́raṇāya
5.1.16.6 yé vyoma-bhūmy-agni[*32]-jalásya vāyós sáṃyoga-bhūtā́ḥ práruhanti sárve
tā́n daivike śuddhi-kárāya bījā́n nírvapāmi devá-sthiti-kā́raṇāya
[*30] 1946 edition shows the incorrect reading pamr̥ddhaiḥ which was corrected in the 1984 edition. In Telegu script, pa and sa are very similar.
[*31] 1946 text reads martyānṃ. The 1984 text reads martyān, assuming that what appears to be a second r is actually a symbol for final n with one loop broken off. Otherwise as it stands, the 1984 edition would read marrtyā. I have corrected all these unintelligible forms to martyānāṃ, which combined with annena provides an intelligible reading parallel to haviṣā surāṇān.
[*32] The text places an anudatta under the ū of bhūmy and then a svarita over the a in agni, seemingly an impossible feat of recitation.
children.translated_text: (5.1.16.1) May these seeds — rice and barley — grow by the grace of the hot-rayed one [the Sun], offered to <s>Soma</s>, free from affliction by the planets, pure and auspicious. (5.1.16.2) I cast sprouting seeds upon the earth — those seventeen created by <s>Brahmā</s>. May they all, nourished by rain, protected by the immortal [nectar], [sustain] the worlds. (5.1.16.3) Seven domestic and seven wild [grains], those destroyed by heat and produced by snow and rain — may they, becoming rain, protect the immortal [nectar]. (5.1.16.4) Split, moist, dried, and growing — with roots, fruits, and vegetables of abundant forms — with food for mortals, with oblations for the gods — may they grow like grass for cattle. (5.1.16.5) For the purification of the earth I cast these seeds, for the establishment of the gods. (5.1.16.6) Those born from the combination of sky, earth, fire, water, and wind — all that sprout — those seeds for divine purification I cast, for the establishment of the gods. [Editorial notes: corrections to readings in 1946 and 1984 editions regarding Telugu script confusions of pa/sa, martyānāṃ, and accent placement.]

children.text:
5.1.17.1 yád bīja-bhūtám idám antárikṣaṃ, yád bījáṃ cāgníḥ pr̥thivī́ rásaś ca tád bīja-rohā́ya váhantu vā́tās, saṃvárdhamānā rúhantāṃ praróhāḥ
5.1.17.2 nírītikās te bahávo rúhantas saṃpā́lyamānā hy amŕ̥tá-vāyunā cá
kā́lena bījā́ḥ práruhanti coptā́ bījā́d aháṃ prácariṣyāmi dhármam
5.1.17.3 éte bījā́ rasá-bhūtā vahantu sómena sr̥ṣṭā́ amŕ̥távat paśúbhyaḥ
etā́n prárohān rasá-bhūta-jātā́n dattā́n me bhúktvā prácarantu gā́vaḥ
5.1.17.4 tásmān mámaitā́n právapāmi gehé té me paśūnām amŕ̥tā vahantu
etáṃ stutā́ me právahantv amútra té puṇya-loké máma dehá-bhūtāḥ
5.1.17.5 samudrávátī śŕ̥ṅge-śr̥ṅge
5.1.17.6 deví tvayi vā́payāmy amū́n kuruṣva tva(g)ṃ sasyá-sáṃpattim
children.translated_text: (5.1.17.1) That which is seed-essence in the atmosphere, and fire and earth and moisture are seed — may the winds carry them for the sprouting of seeds; may the growing sprouts grow. (5.1.17.2) Free from <s>Nirṛti</s> (destruction), may these many sprouting [seeds], protected by the immortal wind, [flourish]. In time, the sown seeds sprout — from the seed I shall propagate <s>dharma</s>. (5.1.17.3) May these seeds, rich in moisture, carry [nourishment], created by <s>Soma</s>, like the immortal [nectar] for cattle. These sprouts born from moisture — given to me, may the cows, having eaten them, move about. (5.1.17.4) Therefore I sow these in my house; may they carry the immortal [essence] for my cattle. May they, praised, carry [merit] to the other world — they who are born of my body in the meritorious world. (5.1.17.5) Like the ocean, at every peak. (5.1.17.6) O Goddess, I sow these in you; may you produce the abundance of grain.

children.text:
5.1.18.1 kā́ma-dúhe duhā́mi tvāṃ kā́ma-dúhe sasyá-vatse dhána-rā́śiṃ prápūraya
5.1.18.2 duhatā́ṃ[*33] dívam índraḥ
5.1.18.3 dharā sā yā[*34] púrā yena dhŕ̥tā yā śóbhanaṃ padám
káriṣyāmy ásya sā́ prītā́ bháva tva(g)ṃ śubha-lákṣaṇe

kartúm árhasi nítye tu vídye vaí tvát-prasādataḥ
5.1.18.5 sasyā́ imé su-havíṣas su-śuddhā yáthā́ cā́hutír yajñá-mukhé sámr̥ddhāḥ
śuddhā́mr̥tās sūríbhir agra-peyā́s sárvāṅga-devā́ áváyavaiś śubhā́nām
5.1.18.6 śúbhā bhavantu prábhavantu púṣṭyai
5.1.18.7 śuddhā́ imé paśáva éṣā(g)ṃ śŕ̥ṅgā́v índrā-viṣṇū bráhmā śíraḥ
5.1.19.1 pr̥ṣṭhó rudrá ŕ̥ṣayo rómā́ṇy uró gúhas tī́rthā lāṅgū́lam
kúkṣir médinī cákṣuṣī cándrādityaú vā́lā vidyā́dharāḥ
5.1.19.2 ū́dhas sāgarā́ḥ[*35] stanā́ nadyó gā́traṃ bhū́-dharāḥ
ásthīni párvatā rúdhiraṃ mitrā́-váruṇau māṃsam agnír jā́hnavī mūtrám
5.1.19.3 khurá úragā jyeṣṭhā́[*36] nā́síkā dántā marutáḥ
jíhvā sarasvatī́ karṇáḥ kavī́ndraś śakŕ̥t púṇya-déśam[*37]
5.1.19.4 etā́s sa-vátsā gā́vas sá-vŕ̥ṣāḥ
yathā-sukháṃ cárantu kāmáṃ carantām
yathā-sukháṃ vrajantu kāmáṃ vrajantām
yathā-sukháṃ mudantu kāmáṃ mudantām
5.1.19.5 gā́vo hi me mātáras santu sárvā mé gó-vr̥ṣāḥ pitáraḥ santu sárve
vatsā́ máma bhrātára eva santu tasmād iḷā́ śuddhi-karā́ bhavantu
5.1.19.6 imā́ṃ siñcāmīmā́m ánugacchāmīmā́ṃ śodhayāmīmā́ṃ mudantu devā́ vítatā vareśā́m[*38]
5.1.19.7 bhuñjántu dattáṃ bálim adya vīrā́ś
śvaḥ śrā́vaye[*39] yūyám aśeṣam asmā́d
gácchadhvam āryā́s su-mánasā ca yúktāḥ
[*33] Normal accent dúhatā́ṃ.
[*34] I read this as dharā sā yā. In his English translation of the KJK, Goudriaan (p. 319) lists an alternative reading dhārāyāsāya from a group of manuscripts which he calls L. Goudriaan is unable to translate these letters either as dhārāsāyā (which he incorrectly lists as dhārāsāya) or as dhārāyāsāya.
[*35] I have added visarga to correct the text.
[*36] The 1946 edition correctly gives jyeṣṭhā, however the 1984 edition has corrupted the word to jeṣṭhā.
[*37] The older edition correctly gives puṇya-, however the 1984 edition of the text has corrupted it to r̥uṇya-. In Telegu script, p and r̥, when following a consonant, are similar.
[*38] The text gives the unintelligible vareḷā́m, which I have changed to vareśā́m, to the (female) lord of boons. I chose this over the possible vareṣā́m since in the Telegu script ḷ is very similar to ś. Also the reading of vareśām gives provides a referent for the four occurrences in this text of imām.
[*39] I have corrected śvaśrā́vaye to śvaḥ śrā́vaye. Thus the word śvaḥ, “tomorrow” follows the word adya, “today” in the previous line, a common sequence. cf. RV 6.56.6d.
children.translated_text: (5.1.18.1) O <s>Kāmadhenu</s> (wish-fulfilling cow), I milk you; O <s>Kāmadhenu</s>, with your grain-calf, fill the heap of wealth. (5.1.18.2) May <s>Indra</s> milk heaven. (5.1.18.3) That earth which was formerly upheld by whom, which is the beautiful abode — I shall make it [thus]; be pleased, O auspicious-marked one. (5.1.18.4) In the divine purification, it is proper to perform [the rite] here with cows, O Lord; you deserve to perform it always; indeed, the sciences [are attained] by your grace. (5.1.18.5) These crops, with excellent oblations, pure — as offerings abundant at the mouth of sacrifice, pure and immortal, to be drunk first by the wise, with all limbs divine, with parts of the auspicious. (5.1.18.6) May they be auspicious; may they produce nourishment. (5.1.18.7) These cattle are pure; their two horns are <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>; <s>Brahmā</s> is the head. (5.1.19.1) <s>Rudra</s> is the back; the <s>Ṛṣis</s> are the hairs; <s>Guha</s> [<s>Skanda</s>] is the chest; the <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords) are the tail; the belly is the earth (<s>Medinī</s>); the two eyes are the Moon and the Sun; the tail-hairs are the <s>Vidyādharas</s>. (5.1.19.2) The udder is the oceans; the teats are the rivers; the body is the mountains; the bones are the mountains; the blood is <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>; the flesh is <s>Agni</s>; <s>Jāhnavī</s> [the Ganges] is the urine. (5.1.19.3) The hooves are the serpents; <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> is the nostrils; the teeth are the <s>Maruts</s>; the tongue is <s>Sarasvatī</s>; the ear is the lord of poets [<s>Bṛhaspati</s>]; the dung is the holy ground. (5.1.19.4) These cows with their calves and their bulls — may they graze as they please, may they roam as they wish, may they go as they please, may they rejoice as they wish. (5.1.19.5) May the cows all be my mothers; may all the bull-cows be my fathers; may the calves be my very brothers; therefore may the libation (<s>iḷā</s>) be purifying. (5.1.19.6) I sprinkle this one, I follow this one, I purify this one — may the gods delight in this one, extending [grace] to the lady of boons. (5.1.19.7) May the heroes enjoy the offering (<s>bali</s>) given today; tomorrow may I hear all the rest from you; go, O noble ones, with good minds and well-disposed. [Editorial notes: corrections to readings involving visarga, Telugu script confusions of jyeṣṭhā/jeṣṭhā, puṇya/ṛuṇya, ḷ/ś, and accent patterns.]

children.translated_text: 5.1.29.1 I invoke <s>Vetra-sāra</s> (Reed-essence). 5.1.29.2 I invoke <s>Kapotaka</s> (the Pigeon). 5.1.29.3 I invoke the Equal-speaker (<s>Tulya-vādin</s>). 5.1.29.4 I invoke <s>Phullā</s> (the Blossoming). 5.1.29.5 I invoke <s>Phulla-rūpa</s> (of Blossoming Form). 5.1.29.6 I invoke the Obstacle (<s>Vighna</s>). 5.1.29.7 I invoke the Obstacle-maker (<s>Vighna-kārin</s>). 5.1.29.8 I invoke the All-bearer (<s>Sarva-vāhana</s>). 5.1.29.9 I invoke <s>Kiṣkindha</s>. 5.1.29.10 I invoke the sacred ford (<s>Tīrtha</s>). 5.1.29.11 I invoke the Enchanter (<s>Mohana</s>). 5.1.29.12 I invoke the Staff-bearer (<s>Daṇḍin</s>). 5.1.29.13 I invoke the Warrior (<s>Yūdhaka</s>). 5.1.29.14 I invoke the Ender (<s>Antaka</s>). 5.1.29.15 I invoke the Rivalry-destroyer (<s>Spardha-ghna</s>). 5.1.29.16 I invoke the Striker (<s>Nighna</s>). 5.1.29.17 I invoke the Bliss-giver (<s>Sukha-da</s>). 5.1.29.18 I invoke the Benefit-giver (<s>Hita-da</s>). [Note: These eight hundred named deities are according to <s>Kaśyapa</s>.]

children.text: 5.1.0.7 rúdram ā́vāhayāmi bhŕ̥śam ā́vāhayāmi nírŕ̥tim ā́vāhayāmi múkhyam ā́vāhayāmi nā́gam ā́vāhayāmi múrúṇḍam ā́vāhayāmi tā́pásam ā́vāhayāmi gárbham ā́vāhayāmi vétram ā́vāhayāmi tī́rtham ā́vāhayāmy aṣṭāú ca.
children.translated_text: 5.1.0.7 I invoke <s>Rudra</s>; I invoke <s>Bhṛśa</s> (the Mighty); I invoke <s>Nirṛti</s>; I invoke <s>Mukhya</s> (the Chief); I invoke the <s>Nāga</s>; I invoke <s>Muruṇḍa</s>; I invoke the Ascetic (<s>Tāpasa</s>); I invoke the Embryo (<s>Garbha</s>); I invoke the Reed (<s>Vetra</s>); I invoke the sacred ford (<s>Tīrtha</s>) — and the eight [additional ones].

children.text:
5.1.30.1 yó 'jaḥ purā́ vī́ra-váro váreṇyo bhūtādhipó bhū́ta-sámasta-vāhaḥ
yó vr̥tra-hr̥d vīra-púras sá-dhūma-ketúḥ
5.1.30.2 pariṣadā yamó dharmas sa-surā́ri-saṅghaḥ
nirr̥tís sá-sámudro varuṇás sá-vāyū́[*49] rā́jā kubéro 'śani-pāṇi-yuktaḥ
5.1.30.3 surá-vr̥nda[*50]-saṅghā́s sahá-kārtikeyā́ gaṇá-mukhya-yuktāḥ
práviśantv idáṃ sthā́nam imé hárer ye pariṣát-práyuktāḥ
kurvántv ídáṃ víghna-vinā́śanī yāḥ
5.1.30.4 sárvaṃ vyápaitu kalmáṣam
ávasiñcāmi
pū́rvaṃ sthitā́ yathéṣṭaṃ gacchantu
carámaṃ cárāmaḥ
[*49] Text: vāyú, corrected to vāyū́, from, presumably, an original sa-vāyúḥ rājā.
[*50] Text: br̥nda, corrected to vr̥nda.
children.translated_text: 5.1.30.1 He who of old was the unborn, the foremost among heroes, the most excellent, the lord of beings, the bearer of all beings, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the hero-city, with his smoking banner — 5.1.30.2 <s>Yama</s> with his retinue, <s>Dharma</s> with the host of gods and demons, <s>Nirṛti</s> with the ocean, <s>Varuṇa</s> with the winds, king <s>Kubera</s> together with the thunderbolt-handed one — 5.1.30.3 the hosts of divine multitudes together with <s>Kārtikeya</s>, attended by the chiefs of <s>gaṇas</s> — let them enter this place, those who are appointed to <s>Hari</s>'s retinue! Let them accomplish the destruction of obstacles! 5.1.30.4 May all impurity depart! I sprinkle. Let those previously stationed depart as they wish. Let us proceed to the final [rite].

children.text:
5.1.31.1 atrá svastí sávitā svastí sarvé vaí devā́ daívikam
5.1.31.2 svásty ástu sarveśvaráś ca dharmā́tmā váruṇo gaṇá-bhr̥d-varaḥ
5.1.31.3 práviśantv idáṃ kúmbhaṃ kúmbha-bhr̥d ámbu-pālakaḥ
5.1.31.4 sárvā váruṇam ánupráviśantu
váruṇaṃ pāśa-bhr̥táṃ vīrám údaka-pám
5.1.31.5 imā́ṃ sīmā́ṃ siñcāmi yajñíyām imā́ṃ sī́mā́ṃ satyenācárāmi
5.1.31.6 bhávatv idáṃ víṣṇor ā́layam
5.1.31.7 átrā́mbu-patir váruṇaś cárátú yathéṣṭam anyā́ gaccantu
5.1.31.8 idáṃ gárbha idáṃ vā́sa idám anyā́nām idáṃ gáruḍasyā́gneyādīnā́m amitasyedáṃ cakrasyedáṃ dhvajasyedáṃ parasyedáṃ yūthādhinā́thasya bhavatu
5.1.31.9 eté ramáṇīyā bhavantu
children.translated_text: 5.1.31.1 Here, may <s>Savitṛ</s> bring well-being; may all the gods bring divine well-being. 5.1.31.2 May there be well-being from the lord of all, the righteous <s>Varuṇa</s>, the best bearer of hosts. 5.1.31.3 Let them enter this vessel (<s>kumbha</s>); the vessel-bearer is the guardian of the waters. 5.1.31.4 Let all enter <s>Varuṇa</s> — <s>Varuṇa</s>, the noose-bearing hero, the guardian of the waters. 5.1.31.5 I sprinkle this sacrificial boundary; I proceed upon this boundary with truth. 5.1.31.6 Let this be the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. 5.1.31.7 Here let <s>Varuṇa</s>, the lord of waters, move about as he wishes; let the others depart. 5.1.31.8 This is the inner sanctum; this is the dwelling; this belongs to the others; this belongs to <s>Garuḍa</s> and the fiery ones and the rest; this belongs to the Immeasurable (<s>Amita</s>); this to the discus (<s>Cakra</s>); this to the banner (<s>Dhvaja</s>); this to the Supreme (<s>Para</s>); this belongs to the lord of the host (<s>Yūthādhi-nātha</s>). 5.1.31.9 Let these be delightful.

children.text:
5.1.32.1 tvā́ṃ khanāmi pr̥thiví tvád-bhartúś śā́sanān mudā́ yuktā bháva
5.1.32.2 devā́nām devásya tásyedáṃ vaíṣṇavaṃ bhávanaṃ deva-vā́hinī
5.1.32.3 pāṃsū́n préṣyāmi bhávantv imé 'bhivŕ̥ddhaye
5.1.32.4 yás sakhā víṣṇor várado varānā́ṃ kártā camūnā́ṃ śúciś śucī́nām
vīró vīrā́ṇām ā́gamiṣyatu[*51]
5.1.32.5 tva(g)ṃ sarvaṃ kāráya várado varásya
tvat-prasādā́t siddhó 'haṃ siddhíṃ gacchāmi
5.1.32.6 śaraṇáṃ prápadye tvā́m evāvighnā́rtham ávighnaṃ bhavatu siddháṃ
5.1.32.7 su-kramā́s santu su-nītā́ś cā́paḥ
5.1.32.8 sūcáyatāṃ váruṇaś śubhā́śubham
5.1.32.9 pātu mā́ṃ váruṇo nityo raktā́mbaro jaléśvaraḥ
5.1.32.10 amíta tvat-prasādéna sárve devā́ḥ prásīdantu
5.1.32.11 ā́yā́tú bhágavān brahmā asmín lóke hitáṅ-karaḥ
nítyo 'smín nírmale padmé rámyatām ŕ̥ṣibhis sahá.
5.1.32.12 idáṃ bráhmaṇā pūrṇáṃ tú tam ā́ruhya devā́s sūcáyantu śubhā́śubham
5.1.32.13 upagatā́s sūcáyantu devā́ḥ
5.1.32.14 ā́yā́tú bhágavān viśvá-karmā viśatu
5.1.32.15 búddhiṃ mamā́viśatu sá evá nírṇáyatāṃ kárma prathamáṃ virā́ḍ badhnātu
5.1.32.16 dvitī́ya(g)ṃ[*52] sápta-ŕ̥ṣayas téṣāṃ prasādā́d ávighnam astu
5.1.32.17 asyā́ṅga-devā́ḥ práviśantv idáṃ puṣṭyaí bhavantu só 'haṃ karómi dívyaṃ kárma kāráyantu devā́ḥ
[*51] This is a rare future imperative form. cf. Whitney's Grammar,  938
[*52] The 1946 edition gave dvitī́yāṃ, however this was corrected in the 1984 edition to dvitī́yaṃ, apparently referring to karma in the previous verse.
children.translated_text: 5.1.32.1 I dig you, O Earth! By the command of your lord, be joyfully united. 5.1.32.2 This is the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) abode of that god of the gods — the divine chariot. 5.1.32.3 I send forth the particles of earth; let these be for increase. 5.1.32.4 He who is the friend of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the granter of boons among boon-granters, the maker of armies, the pure one among the pure, the hero among heroes — may he come. 5.1.32.5 You cause everything to be done, O granter of boons to the excellent! By your grace, I who am accomplished attain <s>siddhi</s> (perfection). 5.1.32.6 I take refuge in you alone, for the purpose of freedom from obstacles; may it be free from obstacles; may it be accomplished. 5.1.32.7 May the waters be well-ordered and well-guided. 5.1.32.8 Let <s>Varuṇa</s> indicate the auspicious and inauspicious. 5.1.32.9 May <s>Varuṇa</s>, the eternal, clad in red garments, lord of the waters, protect me. 5.1.32.10 O Immeasurable One (<s>Amita</s>), by your grace may all the gods be pleased. 5.1.32.11 May the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, the benefactor in this world, come. May he, the eternal, delight in this pure lotus together with the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers). 5.1.32.12 This [lotus] is filled with <s>Brahman</s>; having ascended it, let the gods indicate the auspicious and inauspicious. 5.1.32.13 Let the gods who have arrived indicate [omens]. 5.1.32.14 May the blessed <s>Viśvakarman</s> (Divine Architect) come and enter. 5.1.32.15 May he enter my intellect; may he himself determine the work. Let <s>Virāj</s> bind the first [knot]. 5.1.32.16 The seven <s>ṛṣis</s> [bind] the second; by their grace may there be no obstacle. 5.1.32.17 Let the deities of this body enter; let these be for nourishment. I perform the divine work; let the gods cause it to be accomplished.

children.text: 5.1.0.8 cárāmo bhavantu jaléśvaro náva ca
children.translated_text: 5.1.0.8 Let us proceed; let these be; the lord of waters and the nine [others].

children.text:
5.1.33.1 medínī devī́
5.1.33.2 vā́stoṣ-pate
5.1.33.3 dhārāsu saptasú
5.1.33.4 svastí no mimītām
5.1.33.5 éto nv índram
5.1.33.6 ádité ínumanyasva
5.1.33.7 áto devā́ víṣṇor nú ká(g)ṃ sahásra-śīrṣā púruṣaḥ
5.1.33.8 híraṇya-varṇāṃ bhū́mir bhūmnā́
5.1.33.9 bráhma jajñāná(g)ṃ híraṇya-garbháḥ
5.1.33.10 yám arpáyanti śáṃ no nídhattāṃ bhūmān anto 'gré
nā́gá-rājā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: 5.1.33.1 The goddess <s>Medinī</s> (Earth). 5.1.33.2 O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (Lord of the Dwelling-site)... 5.1.33.3 In the seven streams. 5.1.33.4 May he measure out well-being for us. 5.1.33.5 Come forth now, <s>Indra</s>... 5.1.33.6 O <s>Aditi</s>, be gracious. 5.1.33.7 Then the gods...; <s>Viṣṇu</s>...; now indeed...; the thousand-headed <s>Puruṣa</s>. 5.1.33.8 Golden-colored...; the earth with its expanse. 5.1.33.9 <s>Brahma</s> was born...; <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo). 5.1.33.10 Him whom they offer; may he bestow upon us what is auspicious; the earth, the end, the beginning — <s>svāhā</s> to the <s>Nāga</s>-king!

children.text:
5.1.34.1 índrā́ya svā́hā
5.1.34.2 agnáye svā́hā
5.1.34.3 yamā́ya svā́hā
5.1.34.4 nírr̥taye svā́hā
5.1.34.5 váruṇāya svā́hā
5.1.34.6 vāyáve svā́hā
5.1.34.7 kuberāya svā́hā
5.1.34.8 īśānā́ya svā́hā
5.1.34.9 nārāyaṇā́ya sarva-ratnébhyas svā́hā
5.1.34.10 nārāyaṇā́ya sarva-dhātúbhyas svā́hā
children.translated_text: 5.1.34.1 To <s>Indra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.2 To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.3 To <s>Yama</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.4 To <s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.5 To <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.6 To <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.7 To <s>Kubera</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.8 To <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.9 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with all gems, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.34.10 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with all metals, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
5.1.35.1 nārāyaṇā́ya sarva-bījébhyas svā́hā
5.1.35.2 nārāyaṇā́ya sarva-lohébhyas svā́hā
5.1.35.3 nádībhyas svā́hā
5.1.35.4 pātālébhyas svā́hā
5.1.35.5 vr̥kṣébhyas svā́hā
5.1.35.6 nagébhyas svā́hā
5.1.35.7 dig-gajébhyas svā́hā
5.1.35.8 víṣṇave svā́hā
5.1.35.9 bhūs svā́hā
5.1.35.10 adité ínvama(gg)ṃsthāḥ[*53]
5.1.35.11 ā́tmātmā páramāntarātmā́
5.1.35.12 idáṃ víṣṇor vīryam
5.1.35.13 medínī devī́
5.1.35.14 víṣṇur yóniṃ kalpayatu
5.1.35.15 dhruvá-kṣitiḥ
5.1.35.16 yád asya kármaṇó 'tyárīricam
[*53] The double g, presumably inserted here as recitation guide, is certainly unusual.
children.translated_text: 5.1.35.1 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with all seeds, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.2 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with all metals, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.3 To the rivers, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.4 To the <s>Pātālas</s> (netherworlds), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.5 To the trees, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.6 To the mountains, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.7 To the directional elephants, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.8 To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.9 To the Earth (<s>Bhūḥ</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.35.10 O <s>Aditi</s>, be gracious... 5.1.35.11 The Self, the Self, the Supreme Inner Self. 5.1.35.12 This heroic deed of <s>Viṣṇu</s>... 5.1.35.13 The goddess <s>Medinī</s>. 5.1.35.14 May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb (the dwelling-site). 5.1.35.15 Of firm foundation. 5.1.35.16 Whatever excess there be of this ritual action... [Footnote 53: The double 'g,' presumably inserted here as a recitation guide, is certainly unusual.]

children.text: 5.1.0.9 nāga-rājā́ya svā́hā dhātubhyas svā́hānvama(gg)ṃsthāṣ ṣaṭ ca
children.translated_text: 5.1.0.9 [Catch-words:] '<s>svāhā</s> to the <s>Nāga</s>-king; to the metals, <s>svāhā</s>; be gracious' — and six [mantras in this section].

children.text:
5.1.36.1 víṣṇur mā́ṃ pātu
5.1.36.2 vā́stoṣ-pate dhārāsu saptasú
5.1.36.3 híraṇya-varṇāḥ pávamānas súvar-jánaḥ
5.1.36.4 vana-rājā́ya námaḥ
5.1.36.5 déśādhipátaye námaḥ
5.1.36.6 sárvebhyo devébhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.7 yakṣébhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.8 vidyā-dharébhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.9 rākṣasébhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.10 píśācebhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.11 nāgébhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.12 gándharvebhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.13 aṣṭā-daśá-gáṇebhyo námaḥ
5.1.36.14 tátrá-sthāś śī́ghraṃ vraja
5.1.36.15 ā́tmātmā páramāntarātmā́
5.1.36.16 idáṃ víṣṇuḥ
5.1.36.17 nārāyaṇā́ya
5.1.36.18 úd u tyáṃ jātá-vedasaṃ citráṃ devā́nām
5.1.36.19 rathantarám[*54] asi vāmadevyám asīndrasya tvā
[*54] Text: radhantarám.
children.translated_text: 5.1.36.1 May <s>Viṣṇu</s> protect me. 5.1.36.2 O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (Lord of the Dwelling-site)...; in the seven streams. 5.1.36.3 Golden-colored...; the purifying one, born of the sun. 5.1.36.4 Obeisance to the King of the Forest! 5.1.36.5 Obeisance to the Lord of the Region! 5.1.36.6 Obeisance to all the gods! 5.1.36.7 Obeisance to the <s>Yakṣas</s>! 5.1.36.8 Obeisance to the <s>Vidyādharas</s>! 5.1.36.9 Obeisance to the <s>Rākṣasas</s>! 5.1.36.10 Obeisance to the <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls)! 5.1.36.11 Obeisance to the <s>Nāgas</s>! 5.1.36.12 Obeisance to the <s>Gandharvas</s>! 5.1.36.13 Obeisance to the eighteen groups! 5.1.36.14 You who are stationed there — depart quickly! 5.1.36.15 The Self, the Self, the Supreme Inner Self. 5.1.36.16 This [deed] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>... 5.1.36.17 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. 5.1.36.18 Up rises that <s>Jātavedas</s> (Fire), the wondrous one among the gods. 5.1.36.19 You are the <s>Rathantara</s> (<s>Sāman</s>); you are the <s>Vāmadevya</s> (<s>Sāman</s>); of <s>Indra</s>, you... [Footnote 54: Text reads 'radhantaram'.]

children.text: 5.1.0.10 píśācebhyo námo náva ca
children.translated_text: 5.1.0.10 [Catch-words:] 'Obeisance to the <s>Piśācas</s>' — and nine [mantras].

children.text:
5.1.37.1 asmín deśé vasanta údvasa
5.1.37.2 námo vācé yā́ coditā́
5.1.37.3 vā́stoṣ-pate 'ṇór áṇīyān
5.1.37.4 híraṇya-varṇāḥ pávamānas súvar-jánaḥ
5.1.37.5 dhārāsu saptasú vana-rājā́ya námaḥ
5.1.37.6 vánas-pátibhyo námaḥ
5.1.37.7 vana-devátābhyo námaḥ
5.1.37.8 bhūtébhyo námaḥ
5.1.37.9 yakṣébhyo námaḥ
children.translated_text: 5.1.37.1 You who are dwelling in this place — depart! 5.1.37.2 Obeisance to Speech (<s>Vāc</s>), which has been impelled. 5.1.37.3 O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, smaller than the smallest... 5.1.37.4 Golden-colored...; the purifying one, born of the sun. 5.1.37.5 In the seven streams; obeisance to the King of the Forest! 5.1.37.6 Obeisance to the Lords of Trees! 5.1.37.7 Obeisance to the Forest Deities! 5.1.37.8 Obeisance to the <s>Bhūtas</s> (beings)! 5.1.37.9 Obeisance to the <s>Yakṣas</s>!

children.text:
5.1.38.1 píśācebhyo námaḥ
5.1.38.2 nāgébhyo námaḥ
5.1.38.3 vidyā-dharébhyo námaḥ
5.1.38.4 aṣṭā-daśá-gáṇebhyo námaḥ
5.1.38.5 ástu tr̥ptíḥ
5.1.38.6 idáṃ víṣṇuḥ
5.1.38.7 śríye jātó medínī devī́[*55]
5.1.38.8 nārāyaṇā́ya
5.1.38.9 sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānaṃ váruṇam agním anvā́rabhāmahe
ādityā́n víṣṇu(g)ṃ sū́ryaṃ brahmā́ṇaṃ ca bŕ̥haspátim
5.1.38.10 rathantarám asi
[*55] In the left-hand margin of the manuscript here is written: dāru-samgrahaṇaṃ, “the taking of the wood”.
children.translated_text: 5.1.38.1 Obeisance to the <s>Piśācas</s>! 5.1.38.2 Obeisance to the <s>Nāgas</s>! 5.1.38.3 Obeisance to the <s>Vidyādharas</s>! 5.1.38.4 Obeisance to the eighteen groups! 5.1.38.5 May there be satisfaction! 5.1.38.6 This [deed] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>... 5.1.38.7 Born for <s>Śrī</s> (Prosperity)...; the goddess <s>Medinī</s>. 5.1.38.8 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. 5.1.38.9 We invoke King <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>; we invoke the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. 5.1.38.10 You are the <s>Rathantara</s> (<s>Sāman</s>). [Footnote 55: In the left-hand margin of the manuscript is written: 'dāru-saṃgrahaṇa' — the taking of the wood.]

children.translated_text: 5.1.43.1 To <s>Sthāṇu</s> (the Pillar, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.43.2 To the Serpent-eater (<s>Garuḍa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.43.3 To the <s>Cakra</s> (Discus), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.43.4 To the Immeasurable One, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.43.5 To the Gods, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.43.6 To the <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.43.7 To the Earth (<s>Bhūḥ</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.43.8 Those who live in this place... 5.1.43.9 Obeisance to the Axe! 5.1.43.10 The other <s>Rudra</s>; <s>Tryambaka</s> (the Three-eyed One). 5.1.43.11 Obeisance to <s>Varuṇa</s>; purified. 5.1.43.12 May <s>Viṣṇu</s> protect me. 5.1.43.13 King <s>Soma</s>... [Footnote 56: The text here inserts: 'In existence, through existence, through transcendent existence — worship me; obeisance to the One born from existence; King <s>Soma</s>... <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; guardian protectors... you have conquered, O much-invoked one... of the <s>Revatīs</s>... Transmitted by <s>Kaśyapa</s>.']

children.text: 5.1.0.12 víṣṇur víṣṇus tvā(g)ṃ rakṣatu bhū́s svā́hā bráhmaṇe svā́hā try-ambakaṃ trī́ṇi ca

śáṃ no devī́r
námo váruṇaḥ

na ihá sántá
bhū́yā́(g)ṃsi

ágna ā́ yāhy
agním īle[*57]
pūtás tasya pāré bhúvanasya mádhye

[*59] The VMP here gives the metrical form vŕ̥ṣṇiyam rather than vŕ̥ṣṇyam.
[*60] VMP divides this verse, making the second line the first of chapter 46. The numbering has been adjusted to reflect the complete verse, which now appears here at the end of chapter 45.
children.translated_text: 5.1.45.1 The purifying one, born of the sun. 5.1.45.2 To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. 5.1.45.3 Yours is the purifier, O <s>Vasu</s>...; may the divine [waters] be auspicious for us; obeisance to <s>Varuṇa</s>. 5.1.45.4 The winds blow sweet (<s>madhu</s>) for the righteous one. 5.1.45.5 The true, the immeasurable, the sweet...; not those who are here...; may there be abundance. 5.1.45.6 This — for the honey-maker we set afloat. 5.1.45.7 This honey, having sipped, let it proceed. 5.1.45.8 May the divine [waters] be auspicious...; O <s>Agni</s>, come hither...; I praise <s>Agni</s>...; purified, on the far side of the world, in the middle...; these herbs grew forth...; O you, the hero...; Speech has four [parts]... 5.1.45.9 The four measures of water... 5.1.45.10 Swell up; may fullness come to you from all sides, O <s>Soma</s>, with manly vigor; become the gatherer of wealth. [Footnotes 57-60 contain textual corrections and notes about verse divisions.]

children.text:
5.1.46.1 sahásra-śīrṣā púruṣaḥ
5.1.46.2 ékākṣara(g)ṃ
víṣṇor nú kaṃ vīryāṇi
5.1.46.3 dhārāsu saptásu[*61]
5.1.46.4 svastí no mimītāṃ
svasti-dā́ viśás pátiḥ
5.1.46.5 asthíbhyo námaḥ
5.1.46.6 védāhám etáṃ púruṣaṃ mahā́ntam ādityá-varṇaṃ támasas tú pāré
sárvāṇi rūpā́ṇi vicítya dhī́ro nā́māni kr̥tvā́bhivádan yádā́ste
5.1.46.7 yád vaiṣṇavá(g)ṃ śáyane śayānáṃ tát saha devaís sahárṣibhiḥ
tát sarva-devā́ anumanyatāṃ proktó vaiṣṇavo 'há(g)ṃ śáyitaṃ karomi
[*61] cf. 5.1.12.2 Here the accent is irregularly placed on the penultimate syllable of saptasu, rather than the last syllable as usual.
children.translated_text: (5.1.46.1) 'The thousand-headed <s>Puruṣa</s>...' (5.1.46.2) 'The one-syllabled...' 'What now of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s heroic deeds...' (5.1.46.3) 'In the seven streams...' (5.1.46.4) 'May he measure out well-being for us; the giver of well-being, Lord of peoples.' (5.1.46.5) Obeisance to the bones! (5.1.46.6) 'I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s>, sun-colored, beyond darkness. The wise one, having discerned all forms and having made names, declares them as he exists.' (5.1.46.7) 'As the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> one lies upon the couch, that, together with the gods and together with the <s>Ṛṣis</s> — may all the gods consent to that. I, who have been declared a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, perform the laying down.' [Footnote: *61 Irregular accent on penultimate.]

children.text:
5.1.47.1 ta(g)ṃ śáyane devéśaṃ daítya-nāśāya tát sarva-devaír ánumanyatām
5.1.47.2 avíghnaṃ púṇya(g)ṃ sáṃpadyatāṃ tád bhagavā́n ánumanyatām
5.1.47.3 yád vaiṣṇavatvá(g)ṃ sámatā(g)ṃ samatváṃ vaiṣṇávo 'háṃ váhatāṃ vahāmi
5.1.47.4 víṣṇor aháṃ jíṣṇum aháḥ prápadye svā́hā svadhā vaí śírasā vahāmi
5.1.47.5 síndhoḥ pátiṃ váruṇaṃ mā́ vidantu
5.1.47.6 áto devā́ víṣṇor nú ká(g)ṃ sahásra-śīrṣā púruṣaḥ
5.1.47.7 ā́ tvāhārṣam antár abhū́ḥ
5.1.47.8 śriyé jātó medínī devī́
5.1.47.9 asthíbhyas svā́hā
5.1.47.10 kánikradaj janúṣam
children.translated_text: (5.1.47.1) 'Him, the Lord of Gods, [we lay] upon the couch for the destruction of <s>Daityas</s> — may all the gods consent to that.' (5.1.47.2) 'May it be accomplished without obstacles and with merit — may the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to that.' (5.1.47.3) 'That which is <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>-hood — sameness and equality — I, a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, bear and carry.' (5.1.47.4) 'I take refuge in the victorious light of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. <s>Svāhā</s> and <s>Svadhā</s> indeed I bear upon my head.' (5.1.47.5) 'May they know <s>Varuṇa</s>, the lord of the waters.' (5.1.47.6) 'Thence the gods...' 'What now of <s>Viṣṇu</s>...' 'The thousand-headed <s>Puruṣa</s>...' (5.1.47.7) 'I have brought you here; you have become [present] within.' (5.1.47.8) 'Born for <s>Śrī</s>...' '<s>Medinī</s> the goddess...' (5.1.47.9) To the bones, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.47.10) 'Neighing, [he was] born...'

[*62] The 1984 Telegu script edition of the VMP has accidentally put pages 17 and 18 of the first praśna after page 16 of the fifth praśna. Similarly page 17 and 18 of the fifth praśna has been put after page 16 of the first praśna. The first four praśnas form a single book and praśnas 5-8 form the second book. Therefore the text begins numbering again from 1 at the beginning of praśna 5, and this is why the two sets of pages 17 and 18 were confused.
children.translated_text: (5.1.48.1) 'What now of <s>Viṣṇu</s>...' 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>...' (5.1.48.2) 'Obeisance to <s>Varuṇa</s>.' (5.1.48.3) To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.48.4) To <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the Universal Fire), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.48.5) To <s>Jātavedas</s> (the Knower of All Births), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.48.6) To <s>Pāvaka</s> (the Purifier), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.48.7) To <s>Hutāśana</s> (the Devourer of Oblations), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.48.8) To <s>Havyavāhana</s> (the Carrier of Oblations), <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.48.9) To the One Who Delights in <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (5.1.48.10) To the Embodiment of Sacrifice (<s>Yajña-mūrti</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnote: *62 Note on misplaced pages in the 1984 Telugu edition.]

children.translated_text: 5.1.94.1 To the sub-limbs, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.94.2 To all, <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.94.3 To the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Person), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.94.4 To <s>Bhūḥ</s> (Earth), <s>svāhā</s>! 5.1.94.5 By that, the <s>Ādityas</s> — those three, these [mantras]. 5.1.94.6 The Waters, the All, the fourfold. 5.1.94.7 Of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, the strength, the pride. 5.1.94.8 Then proceeding upward, he who is <s>Mātariśvan</s> (the Wind). 5.1.94.9 He was the one, and he who is of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter]. 5.1.94.10 'Of <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed...' children.text:
5.1.118.1 iṣé tvorjé tvā svasti-dā́ viśás-pátiḥ
5.1.118.2 índraṃ náro nemádhitā havante yát pā́ryā yunájate dhíyas tā́ḥ
śū́ro nŕ̥-ṣātā śávasaś cakāná ā́ gó-mati vrajé bhajā tváṃ naḥ
5.1.118.3 śúcī vo havyā́
5.1.118.4 imé dhūpā́s surabhíno[*95] divyá-dhūpādhivā́sitāḥ
5.1.118.5 pūtā́ brahma-pavítreṇa pūtā́s sū́ryasya raśmíbhiḥ
5.1.118.6 ā́dyam abhígr̥hṇāmīdám āpaś śivā́ḥ
5.1.118.7 viśvátaś cakṣur utá viśváto mukho viśváto hasta utá víśvátas pāt
sáṃ bāhúbhyāṃ námati sáṃpátatrair dyā́vā pr̥thivī́ janáyan devá ékaḥ
5.1.118.8 námas sulomá sulomí
dhārāsu saptásu
5.1.118.9 ā́pa undantu jīváse dīrghāyutvā́ya várcasa óṣadhe tráyas vaina(gg)ṃ svádhite maína(g)ṃ hi(g)ṃsīr deva-śrū́r etā́ni právape svasty úttarāṇy aśī yā́po asmā́n mātáraś śúndhantu ghr̥téna no ghr̥ta-púvaḥ punantu víśvam asmát právahantu riprám údābhyaś śúcirā pūtá emi sómasya tanū́r asi tanúvaṃ me pā́hi mahīnā́ṃ páyo 'si várco-dhā́ asi várcomáyi dhehi vr̥trásya kanī́nikāsi cakṣuṣ-pā́ asi cákṣur me pāhi cit-pátis tvā púnātu vāk-pátis tvā punātu devás tvā savitā́ punātv ácchidreṇa pavítreṇa vásos sū́ryasya raśmíbhis tásya te pavitra-pate pavítreṇa yásmai káṃ puné tác chakeyam ā vo devāsa īmahe sátya-dharmāṇo adhvaré yád vo devāsa āguré yájñiyāso hávāmaha índrāgnī dyā́vā-pr̥thivī ā́pa oṣadhīs tváṃ dīkṣā́ṇām ádhipatir asīhá mā sántaṃ pāhi
[*95] After surabhino the text again has dhūpā, which has been removed in conformity with VMP 5.1.131.10 and 8.1.79.1.
children.translated_text: 5.1.118.1 For vigor, for you; for nourishment, for you; the giver of well-being, Lord of peoples. 5.1.118.2 Men call upon <s>Indra</s>, the unerring, when they yoke those thoughts of theirs for a great task — the hero, winner of men, desirous of might: 'Grant us a share, O you, in the cow-filled enclosure.' 5.1.118.3 Your oblations are pure. 5.1.118.4 These incense-offerings are fragrant, perfumed with divine incense. 5.1.118.5 Purified by the strainer of <s>Brahman</s>; purified by the rays of the Sun. 5.1.118.6 I take hold of the first [water]; these waters are auspicious. 5.1.118.7 Having eyes everywhere and faces everywhere, having hands everywhere and feet everywhere — the one God, creating heaven and earth, welds them together with his arms and wings. 5.1.118.8 Obeisance to the smooth-haired one, the smooth-haired one; in the seven streams. 5.1.118.9 May the waters quicken for life, for long life, for splendor; O herb, [purify] three; O axe, do not harm it; O divine one, I cut these; auspiciously may the upper ones go; O waters, you our mothers, cleanse us; may those who purify with ghee purify us; may they carry away from us all defilement; I emerge from the waters purified and cleansed; you are the body of <s>Soma</s>; protect my body; you are the milk of the great ones; you are the bestower of splendor; place splendor in me; you are the pupil of <s>Vṛtra</s>'s [slayer]; you are the eye-protector, protect my eye; may <s>Cit-pati</s> (Lord of Consciousness) purify you; may <s>Vāk-pati</s> (Lord of Speech) purify you; may <s>Savitṛ</s> the god purify you with the faultless strainer, with the rays of <s>Vasu</s> the Sun; of that strainer-lord, by that strainer, whatever I may purify, may I be able [to accomplish it]; we beseech you, O gods; you of true ordinances at the sacrifice; when you, O gods, arrive; O sacrificial ones, we invoke you; <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>; heaven and earth; O waters; O herbs; you are the lord of consecrations; protect me who am present here. [Footnote 95: After 'surabhino' the text again has 'dhūpā', removed in conformity with VMP 5.1.131.10 and 8.1.79.1.]

children.text:
5.1.119.1 ā́po vā́ idá(g)ṃ sárvaṃ víśvā bhūtā́ny ā́paḥ prāṇā́ vā́ ā́paḥ paśáva ā́po 'mŕ̥tam ā́pó ínnam ā́pas samrā́ḍ ā́po virā́ḍ ā́pas svarā́ḍ ā́paś chándā(g)ṃsy ā́po jyótī(g)ṃṣy ā́pas satyám ā́pas sárvā devátā ā́po bhū́r bhúvas súvar ā́pa óṃ
5.1.119.2 tejovát syāvaḥ
5.1.119.3 óṃ námó víṣṇave
5.1.119.4 óṃ námó nārāyaṇāyá
5.1.119.5 óṃ námó bhágáváté vā́sudevāyá
5.1.119.6 bhūyá ā́tma-vr̥tyā́
5.1.119.7 námas sulomá sá éko bhū́d[*96] devásya tvā savitúr áto devā́ kṣmā́m ekā́m
5.1.119.8 tán mā yaśo 'gré brahmā́ devā́nāṃ bhū́mān anto 'gré
5.1.119.9 tán mā yaśo 'gré śatá-dhāra(g)ṃ tam eka-nemíṃ prajā́-patiṃ prathamám[*97] (?)[*98] nārāyaṇā́ya vidmáhe
5.1.119.10 nārāyaṇā́ya
5.1.119.11 sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānam
5.1.119.12 iyáṃ jā́gratiḥ prathamáṃ práviśya devā́ bhavantu mánu-jā varéṇyaḥ
5.1.119.13 mahā́tmanne no hárate námas te
5.1.119.14 aghaugha-vidhváṃsam amúṃ kuruṣva
5.1.119.15 víṣṇur mā́ṃ rakṣatu
5.1.119.16 óṃ kéśavāya námaḥ
5.1.119.17 óṃ ám
[*96] Text: bhū́r
[*97] prajāpatiṃ prathamaṃ yajñiyānām MS 4.14.1c; TB 2.8.1.4a; ApŚ 20.20.9a
[*98] Question mark appears in the VMP text and also in the following footnote: (?) váraṃ viṣṇúr vareṇīyaṃ bhárgo māyā̀ ca dhīmahi / táṃ no viṣṇúḥ pracodáyāt (íti kaíścit)
children.translated_text: (5.1.119.1) 'Waters indeed are all this. All beings are waters. Vital breaths are waters. Cattle are waters. Immortality is waters. Food is waters. The supreme sovereign is waters. The universal sovereign is waters. The self-sovereign is waters. Metres are waters. Lights are waters. Truth is waters. All deities are waters. <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Suvaḥ</s> — waters are <s>Oṃ</s>.' (5.1.119.2) 'Radiant, dark...' (5.1.119.3) <s>Oṃ</s>. Obeisance to <s>Viṣṇu</s>! (5.1.119.4) <s>Oṃ</s>. Obeisance to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>! (5.1.119.5) <s>Oṃ</s>. Obeisance to the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vāsudeva</s>! (5.1.119.6) 'Again, by the self's own activity...' (5.1.119.7) 'Obeisance to the smooth-haired one. He alone became...' 'Of god <s>Savitṛ</s>, your...' 'Thence the gods...' 'The earth, the one...' (5.1.119.8) 'May that glory [be] mine, in the beginning...' '<s>Brahmā</s>, [chief] of the gods...' 'The Vast One, the end, the beginning...' (5.1.119.9) 'May that glory [be] mine, in the beginning...' 'The hundred-streamed...' 'That one-wheeled...' '<s>Prajāpati</s>, the first...' 'We know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>...' (5.1.119.10) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>...' (5.1.119.11) 'King <s>Soma</s>...' (5.1.119.12) 'This [light], awakening, entering first — may the gods become the chosen ones of mankind.' (5.1.119.13) 'Obeisance to you, the Great-souled One; do not take us away.' (5.1.119.14) 'Destroy the flood of sins for us.' (5.1.119.15) 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> protect me!' (5.1.119.16) <s>Oṃ</s>. Obeisance to <s>Keśava</s>! (5.1.119.17) <s>Oṃ aṃ</s>. [Footnotes on variant readings and <s>Nārāyaṇa Gāyatrī</s>.]

children.text: 5.1.0.31 vidmáhe 'ṣṭāú ca
children.translated_text: (5.1.0.31) [Rubric:] '...we know' — and eight [mantras].

children.text:
5.1.120.1 ā́tmātmā páramāntarātmā́ máhy-antarātmā́ yáś cātirātmā́ satáno 'ntarātmā́ vyā́veṣṭi víśva(g)ṃ sákalaṃ bibhárti yó vyakta-puṇyás sá-tunaḥ pradhā́naḥ
5.1.120.2 prāṇáḥ práṇītis sa udāna ā́dir vára-do varāho vyānaś ca me syā́t tapásāñ ca mūrtíḥ kapílo munīndró yaś cā́pānó háyaśīrṣo naḥ
5.1.120.3 yát sarvam aśnā́ty[*99] ajáras samagrá(g)ṃ śríyam ū́rja-yuktāṃ sá tu me samā́naḥ
5.1.120.4 bálam āsuráṃ yát satátaṃ nihantā bráhmā buddhír me gópa īśvaráḥ
5.1.120.5 savitā́ ca vīryám índuś ca dhātú[*100]-rasá-bhūta-bhūtā́ bhū́tās sa-bhūtā́ḥ
5.1.120.6 dyaúr me ástu mūrdhódara-nābhó[*101] vā bhū́mir yathāṅghrír[*102] vávr̥dhe 'ham ī́śaḥ
5.1.120.7 ásthīni me syúr athá parvatākhyā́ bhujágāś ca keśā́ dívi ye cárantaḥ
5.1.120.8 dvaú netra-rūpaú víthu pr̥ścni [?] múkhyau rúdhirañ ca sā́ra(g)ṃ sákalañ ca tóyam
5.1.120.9 snāyavo mé ā́sánnā dyaúr bhr̥gúr me hŕ̥dayam astu
sárve anyé munáyo 'ṅga-bhūtā́ vedā́ me ā́syaṃ jihvā́ me sárasvatī
5.1.120.10 dántā marutá upájihvā upaśrutíḥ
5.1.120.11 vŕ̥ṣaṇau mitrā́-váruṇāv upastháḥ prajā́-patir āntrā́ me védāś śrúti[*103]-smr̥tī́ medā́dhā́raṇe
5.1.120.12 svedám me várṣaṃ mūtra kóśá(g)ṃ samudráṃ púrīṣaṃ kā́ñcanam
5.1.120.13 sāvitrī́ gāyatrī́ máryādā védi-hŕ̥t-puṇḍarīké vimále praviṣṭás sákalas sa-lakṣmī́s sa-víbhūtikāṅgó yát sarvaṃ púṇyaṃ máyy adhiṣṭhā́nam astu
5.1.120.14 sárveṣāṃ devā́nām ā́tmakas sárveṣāṃ munī́nām ā́tmakas tápo-mū́rtir ihá púṇya-mū́rtir ā́san[*104]
5.1.120.15 sahásra-śīrṣā púruṣaḥ
[*99] Text: aśñchāty
[*100] Text: thātú
[*101] The 1946 edition reads: mūrdhódaran nabhó
[*102] Text: yadhāṅghrír
[*103] Text: śrútis
[*104] Text: ā́sann
children.translated_text: (5.1.120.1) 'The Self, the self, the Supreme Inner Self, the Great Inner Self, and the Transcendent Self — the pervading Inner Self envelops and bears the entire universe. He whose merit is manifest, embodied, is the principal [being].' (5.1.120.2) '<s>Prāṇa</s> (the in-breath) is the guide; he is <s>Udāna</s> (the upward-breath), the origin. The boon-granting <s>Varāha</s> (Boar) — and may <s>Vyāna</s> (the diffused breath) be mine, and the embodiment of austerities, <s>Kapila</s> the chief of sages — and that which is <s>Apāna</s> (the downward-breath), <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> (Horse-headed <s>Viṣṇu</s>) [be] for us.' (5.1.120.3) 'He who devours all, the unaging, the complete, together with <s>Śrī</s> endowed with nourishment — he is my <s>Samāna</s> (the equalizing breath).' (5.1.120.4) 'He who constantly destroys the demonic power — <s>Brahmā</s>, the intellect, my protector, the Lord.' (5.1.120.5) '<s>Savitṛ</s> is the virile power; the Moon is the <s>dhātu</s>-essence of beings — the beings, together with beings.' (5.1.120.6) 'May heaven be my head; the belly and navel, or the earth, like the foot — I have grown; I am the Lord.' (5.1.120.7) 'May my bones be what are called the mountains, and my hair the serpents who move in the sky.' (5.1.120.8) 'The two [luminaries] are in the form of eyes, the chief broad ones; and the blood is the essence, and all water.' (5.1.120.9) 'The sinews are near me; heaven [is mine]; <s>Bhṛgu</s> is my heart. All other sages are born of my limbs. The <s>Vedas</s> are my mouth; <s>Sarasvatī</s> is my tongue.' (5.1.120.10) 'The teeth are the <s>Maruts</s>; the sub-tongue is the organ of hearing.' (5.1.120.11) 'The testicles are <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>; the generative organ is <s>Prajāpati</s>; the intestines are my <s>Vedas</s>; <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> are the supports of the marrow.' (5.1.120.12) 'My sweat is the rain; the urine is the ocean-vessel; the excrement is gold.' (5.1.120.13) '<s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the boundary — entered into the altar-heart-lotus, spotless, complete, with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, with glorious limbs — may all that is meritorious have its abode in me.' (5.1.120.14) 'The self of all the gods, the self of all the sages, the embodiment of austerity, here the embodiment of merit — he was.' (5.1.120.15) 'The thousand-headed <s>Puruṣa</s>...'

children.text: 5.1.0.32 sárasvatī ṣáṭ ca
children.translated_text: (5.1.0.32) [Rubric:] '<s>Sarasvatī</s>' — and six [mantras].

children.text:
5.1.121.1[*105] aṇór áṇīyān maható máhīyān ātmā́ gúhāyāṃ níhito 'sya jantóḥ
tám akratuṃ paśyati vīta-śokó dhātúḥ prasā́dān mahimā́nam īśam
5.1.121.2[*106] saptá-prāṇā́ḥ prabhávanti tasmāt[*107] saptā́rciṣas samídhas saptájihvā́ḥ
saptá imé lokā́ yéṣu cáranti prāṇā́ guhā́śayāṃ[*108] níhitās saptá-sapta
5.1.121.3[*109] átas samudrā́ giráyaś ca sárve 'smā́t[*110] syándante síndhavas sárva-rūpāḥ
átaś ca víśvā óṣadhayo rásāś[*111] ca yénaiṣa bhūtás[*112] tiṣṭhaty[*113] antarātmā́
5.1.121.4[*114] brahmā́ devā́nāṃ padavī́ḥ kavīnā́m ŕ̥ṣir víprāṇāṃ mahiṣó mr̥gā́ṇām
śyenó gŕ̥dhrāṇā(g)ṃ svádhitir vánānā(g)ṃ sómaḥ pavítram áty eti rébhan[*115]
5.1.121.5[*116] ajā́m ékāṃ lóhita-śukla-kr̥ṣṇā́ṃ bahvī́ṃ prajā́ṃ janáyantī(g)ṃ sá-rūpām
ajó hy éko juṣámāṇo 'nuśéte jáhāty enāṃ bhuktá-bhogām ájo 'nyaḥ
[*105] MahānU US 8.3; SwV 12.1
[*106] MahānU US 8.4; SwV 12.2
[*107] Text: tasmāth
[*108] US guhāśayā; SwV guhāśayāt
[*109] MahānU US 8.5; SwV 12.3
[*110] Text: 'smā́th; US asmāt
[*111] US rasaś
[*112] US bhūtais
[*113] US tiṣṭhate hy
[*114] MahānU US 9.1; SwV 12.4
[*115] Text: rébhann
[*116] MahānU US 9.2; SwV 12.5
children.translated_text: (5.1.121.1) 'Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, the Self is hidden in the cave of this creature. One who is free from desire sees the majesty of the Lord by the grace of the Creator, [becoming] free from sorrow.' (5.1.121.2) 'Seven breaths spring forth from Him, seven flames, seven kindling-sticks, seven tongues. Seven are these worlds in which the breaths move, hidden in the cave, seven times seven.' (5.1.121.3) 'From Him arise all the oceans and all the mountains; from Him flow the rivers of every form. From Him arise all the herbs and their essences, by which this inner Self abides among beings.' (5.1.121.4) '<s>Brahmā</s> is [the chief] of gods, the guide of seers, the <s>Ṛṣi</s> of the learned, the buffalo among wild animals, the eagle among vultures, the axe among forests. <s>Soma</s>, passing through the purifier, resounds.' (5.1.121.5) 'The one unborn she-goat — red, white, and black — gives birth to many offspring of like form. One unborn he-goat, enjoying her, lies beside her; another unborn he-goat leaves her after her pleasures are consumed.' [Footnotes: References to <s>Mahānārāyaṇopaniṣad</s>, <s>Śvetāśvataropaniṣad</s>, variant readings.]

children.translated_text: (5.1.122.1) 'The swan seated in purity, the <s>Vasu</s> seated in the atmosphere, the <s>Hotṛ</s> seated on the altar, the guest seated in the house, seated among men, seated in the noble, seated in truth, seated in the sky — water-born, cow-born, truth-born, mountain-born — the great Truth.' (5.1.122.2) 'Than whom nothing greater was born, nor was there anything whatsoever — he who entered all the worlds, <s>Prajāpati</s>, discerning with his offspring, is the sixteenth, possessing three lights.' (5.1.122.3) 'We call upon the Ordainer of wealth — will he grant us riches? — <s>Savitṛ</s>, who watches over men.' (5.1.122.4) 'Today, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, bestow upon us offspring-rich good fortune. Drive away bad dreams.' (5.1.122.5) 'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, drive away all misfortunes. Bestow upon us what is auspicious.' [Footnotes: References to <s>Mahānārāyaṇopaniṣad</s>, <s>Śvetāśvataropaniṣad</s>, variant readings.]

children.translated_text: (5.1.123.1) 'The winds blow sweet for the righteous one; the rivers flow with sweetness. May the herbs be sweet for us.' (5.1.123.2) 'Sweet be the night and the dawn; sweet be the earthly realm. Sweet may our Father Heaven be to us.' (5.1.123.3) 'Sweet be the lord of the forest for us; sweet be the sun. Sweet may our cows be for us.' (5.1.123.4) 'Ghee was mixed; ghee is his source; he rests in ghee; ghee is verily his abode. Following your own nature, bring [the offering] and delight yourself. O Bull, carry the oblation consecrated with <s>svāhā</s>.' (5.1.123.5) 'From the ocean rose a wave full of sweetness. Together with the <s>upāṃśu</s> [libation], immortality was attained. The secret name of ghee — it is the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality.' [Footnotes: References to <s>Mahānārāyaṇopaniṣad</s>, <s>Śvetāśvataropaniṣad</s>, <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s>.]

children.translated_text: (5.1.124.1) We shall proclaim the names with <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter); in this sacrifice we sustain [them] with obeisances. May <s>Brahmā</s> hear what is being recited — the four-horned white [bull] has bellowed this. (5.1.124.2) Four horns, three feet, two heads, seven hands has he. Bound threefold, the bull bellows mightily — the great god has entered into mortals. (5.1.124.3) Placed threefold, hidden by the <s>Paṇis</s>, the gods found the <s>ghṛta</s> in the cow. <s>Indra</s> generated one, <s>Sūrya</s> another; from <s>Vena</s>, by their own power, they fashioned one. (5.1.124.4) He who among the gods is foremost, [coming] from the front, supreme above all — <s>Rudra</s>, the great <s>Ṛṣi</s> — see <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo) being born — may that god unite us with auspicious meditation. (5.1.124.5) Than whom there is nothing higher — nothing smaller nor greater exists than him — standing like a tree fixed in heaven, by that <s>Puruṣa</s> this all is filled. (5.1.124.6) Not by deeds, not by progeny, not by wealth — by renunciation alone some attained immortality. Beyond heaven, hidden in the cave, it shines — that which the ascetics enter. (5.1.124.7) Those whose purpose is well-determined through the knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>, the ascetics purified in nature through the <s>yoga</s> of <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) — they, at the final end, in the world of <s>Brahman</s>, are entirely liberated beyond immortality. (5.1.124.8) The small, sinless, supreme dwelling — the lotus that stands in the middle of the city [of the body] — therein too is the small space, free from sorrow — that which is within it, that is to be meditated upon. (5.1.124.9) That which is proclaimed as the primal sound [<s>Oṃ</s>] at the beginning of the <s>Vedas</s> and is established at the end of the <s>Vedas</s> — of that which is dissolved into <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), he who is beyond — he is <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). [Editorial notes: corrections to section numbering, textual readings from multiple editions.]

(5.1.125.3) The thousand-headed god, all-eyed, all-beneficent — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> the god, imperishable, the supreme lord. (5.1.125.4) Universally supreme, eternal, the all — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>. This universe is the <s>Puruṣa</s>; that universe he sustains. (5.1.125.5) The lord of the universe, the ruler of the self, eternal, auspicious, unfallen — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the great one to be known, the universal self, the supreme refuge. [Editorial notes: variant readings from Upaniṣad sources and Śvetāśvatara parallels.]

children.translated_text: (5.1.126.1) Whatever in this world is seen or even heard — pervading all that, within and without, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> abides. (5.1.126.2) Infinite, imperishable, the seer, situated in the ocean, all-beneficent — resembling a lotus bud, the heart is [situated] facing downward. (5.1.126.3) Below, at a span's length, it stands above the navel — that is the heart, know it — the great abode of the universe. (5.1.126.4) Continuously hung by veins, resembling a bud — at its end, a fine hollow aperture — in that, everything is established. (5.1.126.5) In the midst of that, a great fire, all-flaming, facing all directions — he, consuming first, distributing, stands — imperishable, the seer, consuming food. (5.1.126.6) He heats his own body from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head. In the midst of that, the flame of fire, subtle, stands upward. (5.1.126.7) Like a streak of lightning standing in the midst of a dark rain-cloud, brilliant — thin as a grain of unhusked rice, golden-hued, the measure of the subtle body. (5.1.126.8) In the midst of that flame, the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is established — he is <s>Brahmā</s>, he is <s>Śiva</s>, he is <s>Indra</s> with <s>Indra</s> — he is imperishable, supreme, self-ruling. (5.1.126.9) <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), truth, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, dark and tawny — with upward seed (<s>ūrdhvareta</s>), of varied form — obeisance to the universal form! [Editorial notes: extensive variant readings from Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, Upaniṣadsaṅgraha, and Śvetāśvatara sources.]
