6.1.2 áto devā́ avantu no yáto víṣṇur vicakramé
pr̥thivyā́s saptá-dhā́mabhis svā́hā
6.1.3 idáṃ víṣṇur ví cakrame tredhā́ ní dadhe padám
sámūḍham asya pā(g)ṃsuré svā́hā
6.1.4 trī́ṇi padā́ ví cakrame víṣṇur gopā́ ádābhyaḥ
 [t]áto[*327] dhármāṇi dhāráyan svā́hā
6.1.5 víṣṇoḥ kármāṇi paśyata yáto vratā́ni paspaśé
índrasya yújyas sákhā svā́hā
6.1.6 tád víṣṇoḥ paramáṃ padá(g)ṃ sádā paśyanti sūráyaḥ
divī́va cákṣur ā́tata(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.1.7 tád víprāso vipanyávo jāgr̥vā́ṃsas sám indhate
víṣṇor yát paramáṃ padá(gg)ṃ svā́hā
[*327] RV: áto
children.translated_text: (6.1.1) <s>Hariḥ Oṃ</s>. (6.1.2) 'Thence may the gods assist us, from where <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth, with the seven abodes of the earth, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.1.3) 'This <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth; he placed his foot in three places; all is gathered in his dust, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.1.4) '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth across three realms, the unfailing guardian, thereby upholding the <s>dharmas</s> (laws), <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.1.5) 'Behold the deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whereby he set forth his vows — <s>Indra</s>'s closest companion, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.1.6) 'That supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the wise ones always behold, like an eye spread wide in the sky, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.1.7) 'That [abode] the inspired, eloquent, ever-wakeful ones kindle — that which is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 6.0.1 cákṣur ā́tata(gg)ṃ svā́hā dvé ca
children.translated_text: (6.0.1) [Rubric:] '...an eye spread wide, <s>svāhā</s>' — and two [mantras].

children.text:
6.2.1[*328] sahásra-śīrṣā púruṣas sahasrākṣás sáhásra-pāt
sá bhū́miṃ viśváto vr̥tvā́ty atiṣṭad daśāṅgulá(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.2.2 púruṣa evédá(g)ṃ sárvaṃ yád bhūtáṃ yác ca bhávyam
utā́mr̥tatvásyéśāno yad ánnenātiróhati svā́hā
6.2.3 etā́vān asya mahimā́to jyā́yā́(g)ṃś ca pū́ruṣaḥ
pā́do 'sya víśvā bhūtā́ni tri-pā́d asyāmŕ̥taṃ diví svā́hā
6.2.4 tri-pā́d ūrdhvá úd ait púruṣaḥ pā́do 'syehā́bhávāt púnaḥ
táto víṣvaṅ vy akrāmat sāśanānaśané abhí svā́hā
6.2.5 tásmād virā́ḍ[*329] ajāyata virā́jo ádhí pū́ruṣaḥ
sá jāto áty aricyata paścā́d bhū́mim átho purás svā́hā
[*328] Begin TA 3.12
[*329] RV: virā́l
children.translated_text: (6.2.1) 'The thousand-headed <s>Puruṣa</s>, thousand-eyed, thousand-footed — he, having enveloped the earth on all sides, extended beyond it by ten fingers' breadth, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.2.2) 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this — whatever has been and whatever shall be. And he is the lord of immortality, which he surpasses through food, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.2.3) 'Such is his greatness, and the <s>Puruṣa</s> is even greater than this. One-fourth of him is all beings; three-fourths of him is the immortal in heaven, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.2.4) 'Three-fourths the <s>Puruṣa</s> rose upward; one-fourth of him remained here again. Thence he spread in all directions, over that which eats and that which does not eat, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.2.5) 'From him <s>Virāj</s> was born; from <s>Virāj</s> the <s>Puruṣa</s> [was born]. Being born, he extended beyond the earth — behind and before, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.3.1 yát púruṣena havíṣā devā́ yajñám átanvata
vasantó asyāsīd ā́jyam grīṣmá idhmáś śarád dhavís svā́hā
6.3.2 saptā́syāsan paridháyas trís saptá samídhaḥ kr̥tā́ḥ
devā́ yád yajñáṃ tánvānā́ ábadhnan púruṣaṃ paśú(gg)ṃ svā́hā[*330]
6.3.3 táṃ yajñáṃ barhíṣi praúkṣan púruṣaṃ jātám agratáḥ
téna devā́ áyajanta sādhyā́ r̥ṣayaś ca yé svā́hā
6.3.4 tásmād yajñā́th[*331] sarva-hútas sáṃbhr̥taṃ pŕ̥ṣádājyáṃ
paśū́(g)ṃs tā́(g)ṃś cakre vāyavyā́n ā́raṇyā́n grāmyā́ś ca yé svā́hā
6.3.5 tásmād yajñā́th[*332] sarva-húto[*333] ŕ̥cas sā́māni jajñire
chándā́(g)ṃsi jajñire tásmād yájus tásmād ajāyata svā́hā
[*330] RV 10.90.15 [out of order]; TA; (VC p. 973)
[*331] RV: yajñā́t
[*332] RV: yajñā́t
[*333] RV: sarva-húta
children.translated_text: (6.3.1) 'When the gods performed the sacrifice with the <s>Puruṣa</s> as the offering, spring was its clarified butter, summer was its kindling, and autumn was the oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.3.2) 'Seven were its enclosing sticks, thrice seven were the kindling sticks made. When the gods, spreading the sacrifice, bound the <s>Puruṣa</s> as the sacrificial beast, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.3.3) 'That sacrifice, the <s>Puruṣa</s> born in the beginning, they sprinkled on the sacred grass. With him the gods performed the sacrifice, and the <s>Sādhyas</s> and the <s>Ṛṣis</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.3.4) 'From that sacrifice, the all-offered one, the curdled-butter mixture was collected. He made the creatures of the air, the wild animals and the domestic ones, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.3.5) 'From that sacrifice, the all-offered one, the <s>Ṛc</s> verses and the <s>Sāman</s> chants were born. The metres were born from it; the <s>Yajus</s> was born from it, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.4.1 tásmād áśvā ajāyanta yé ké cobhayā́dataḥ
gā́vo ha jajñire tásmāt tásmāj jātā́ ajāváyas svā́hā
6.4.2 yát púruṣam vy adadhuḥ katidhā́ vy kalpayan
múkhaṃ kím asya kaú bāhū́ kā́ ūrū́ pā́dāv[*334] ucyete svā́hā
6.4.3 brāhmaṇó 'sya múkham āsīd bāhū́ rājanyáḥ kr̥táḥ
ūrū́ tád asya yád vaíśyaḥ padbhyā́(g)ṃ śūdró ajāyata svā́hā
6.4.4 candrámā mánaso jātáś cákṣos sū́ryo ajāyata
múkhād índraś cāgníś ca prāṇā́d vāyur ajāyata svā́hā
6.4.5 nā́bhyā āsīd antárikṣaṃ śīrṣṇó dyáus sám avartata
padbhyā́ṃ bhū́mir díśaś śrótrāt táthā lokā́(g)ṃ akalpayan[*335] svā́hā
6.4.6 védāhám etáṃ púruṣaṃ mahā́ntam ādityá-varṇaṃ támasas tú pāré
sárvāṇi rūpā́ṇi vicítya dhī́ro[*336] nā́māni kr̥tvā́bhivádan yádā́ste svā́hā
6.4.7 dhātā́ purástād yám udājahā́ra śakráh právidvā́n pradíśaś cátasraḥ
tám eváṃ vidvā́n amŕ̥ta ihá bhavati nā́nyáh pánthā áyanāya vidyate svā́hā[*337]
6.4.8 yajñéna yajñám ayajanta devā́s tā́ni dhármāṇi práthamā́ny āsan[*338]
té ha nā́kaṃ mahimā́nas sacante[*339] yatra pū́rve sādhyā́s sánti devā́s svā́hā[*340]
[*334] RV: pā́dā; TA: pādāv
[*335] TA: akalpayann
[*336] TA: dhī́raḥ
[*337] cf. p. 407 tam eva vi...; TA 3.12.7 (VC p. 518)
[*338] TA: āsann
[*339] RV: sacanta
[*340] End TA 3.12
children.translated_text: (6.4.1) 'From it horses were born, and all those with two rows of teeth. Cows were born from it; from it were born goats and sheep, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.4.2) 'When they divided the <s>Puruṣa</s>, into how many parts did they arrange him? What was his mouth? What were his arms? What are called his thighs and feet? <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.4.3) 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was his mouth; the <s>Rājanya</s> (warrior) was made from his arms. What was the <s>Vaiśya</s> — that was his thighs. From his feet the <s>Śūdra</s> was born, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.4.4) 'The moon was born from his mind; from his eye the sun was born. From his mouth <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> [were born]; from his breath <s>Vāyu</s> was born, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.4.5) 'From his navel arose the atmosphere; from his head the sky evolved. From his feet the earth; from his ears the directions — thus they fashioned the worlds, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.4.6) 'I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s>, sun-colored, beyond darkness. The wise one, having discerned all forms and having made names, declares them as he exists, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.4.7) '<s>Dhātṛ</s>, whom <s>Śakra</s> proclaimed beforehand, knowing the four directions — one who knows him thus becomes immortal here. There is no other path to go, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.4.8) 'By sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice — those were the first ordinances. Those mighty ones attain the firmament, where dwell the ancient <s>Sādhyas</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 6.0.2 pura svā́hā 'jāyáta svā́hā 'kalpayan svā́hā ṣaṭ ca
children.translated_text: (6.0.2) [Rubric:] '...beforehand, <s>svāhā</s>' '...was born, <s>svāhā</s>' '...they fashioned, <s>svāhā</s>' — and six [mantras].

children.text:
6.5.1 híraṇya-varṇāṃ háriṇīṃ suvárṇa rajatás rajām
candrā́ṃ hiráṇmayīṃ lakṣmī́ṃ jā́tavedo mam ā́vaha svā́hā[*341]
6.5.2 tāṃ ma ā́vaha jā́ta vedo lakṣmī́m ánapagāmínīm
yásyāṃ híraṇyaṃ vindéyaṃ gā́máśvaṃ púrúṣā́n aháṃ svā́hā[*342]
6.5.3 aśva-pūrvā́ṃ[*343] ratha-madhyā́ṃ hastínād aprabódhinīm
śríyaṃ devī́m úpa hvaye śrī́r mā devī́ juṣatāṃ svā́hā[*344]
6.5.4 kāṃsosmi tā́ṃ híraṇya prākā́rā mārdrā́ṃ jválantīṃ tr̥ptā́ṃ tarpáyantīm
padme sthítā́ṃ padmá-varṇāṃ tvā́m ihópa-hvaye śríyaṃ svā́hā[*345]
6.5.5 candrā́ṃ prabhāsā́ṃ yaśás ā jválantīṃ śríyaṃ loké devá-juṣṭām udārā́m
tā́ṃ padmánemīṃ śáraṇam aháṃ prápadye 'lakṣmī́r me naśyatāṃ tvā́ṃ vr̥ṇomi svā́hā[*346]
[*341] Beginning here with verse 6.5.1 and ending with 6.7.7 we find the “Śrī-sūkta” of the R̥g Veda Khilas. The verse numbers given are from Scheftelowitz, pp. 72-73, RVKh 2.6.1-15. The verse numbers in parentheses are from Bloomfield. RVKh 2.6.1 (5.87.1) (VC p. 1069)
[*342] RVKh 2.6.2 (5.87.2) (VC p. 462)
[*343] RVKh/VC: aśvapūrṇāṃ
[*344] RVKh 2.6.3 (5.87.3) (VC p. 127)
[*345] RVKh 2.6.4 (5.87.4) (VC p. 323)
[*346] RVKh 2.6.5 (5.87.5) (VC p. 366)
children.translated_text: (6.5.1) 'Golden-hued, beautiful as a doe, adorned with gold and silver garlands — the radiant, golden <s>Lakṣmī</s>, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, bring her to me, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.5.2) 'Bring to me, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, that <s>Lakṣmī</s> who never departs, through whom I may find gold, cattle, horses, and men, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.5.3) 'Preceded by horses, with a chariot in the middle, awakened by the trumpeting of elephants — I call upon <s>Śrī</s>, the goddess. May the goddess <s>Śrī</s> delight in me, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.5.4) 'Golden-ramparted, moist, blazing, satisfied and satisfying, established in the lotus, lotus-hued — I call upon you, O <s>Śrī</s>, here, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.5.5) 'Radiant, brilliant, blazing with fame, <s>Śrī</s> in the world, beloved of the gods, noble — I take refuge in her who has the lotus as her rim. May <s>Alakṣmī</s> (misfortune) perish! I choose you, <s>svāhā</s>!' [Footnotes: These are verses from the <s>Śrī-sūkta</s> of the <s>Ṛgveda Khilas</s>, 2.6.1-5.]

children.text:
6.6.1 ādityá-varṇe tápasó 'dhí-jātó vánas-páti stáva vr̥kṣó 'thá[*347] bilváḥ
tásya phálāni tápasā́ nudantu māyā́ntarā yā́ś ca bāhyā́ alakṣmī́s svā́hā[*348]
6.6.2 úpaitu mā́ṃ deva-sakháḥ kīrtíś ca máṇinā sahá
prādur bhutó 'smi rāṣṭre 'smín kīrtím r̥ddhiṃ dadā́tu me svā́hā[*349]
6.6.3 kṣút pipāsā́m alāṃ jyeṣṭā́m alakṣmī́ṃ nāśayāmy áhám
ábhūtim ásamr̥ddhiṃ cá sarvā́ṃ nír ṇudame gŕ̥hāt svā́hā[*350]
6.6.4 gándha-dvārā́ṃ durādharṣān nityá puṣṭāṃ karīṣiṇim
īśvárī́(g)ṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ tā́m ihópa hvaye śríyam svā́hā[*351]
6.6.5 manasaḥ kā́mam ā́kutiṃ vācás satyám aśīmahi
paśūnā́ṃ rūpám annasya máyi śrī́ś śrayatāṃ yáśas svā́hā[*352]
[*347] Text: 'dhá
[*348] RVKh 2.6.6 (5.87.6) (VC p. 163)
[*349] RVKh 2.6.7 (5.87.7) (VC p. 272)
[*350] RVKh 2.6.8 (5.87.8) cf. TAA 10.33 (VC p. 340)
[*351] RVKh 2.6.9 (5.87.9) cf. TA 10.1.10; MahānU 4.8 (VC p. 343)
[*352] RVKh 2.6.10 (5.87.10) cf. VS 39.4; ŚB 14.3.2.19; KŚ 26.7.49 [These references for first line of verse.] (VC p.683) cf. VS 39.4; ŚB 14.3.2.20; TB 2.4.6.6 [These references for second line of verse.] (VC p. 578)
children.translated_text: 6.6.1 Of sun-like color, born of austerity — O lord of the forest, your tree is the <s>bilva</s>; may its fruits by austerity drive away the inner and outer <s>alakṣmī</s> (misfortune), <s>svāhā</s>! 6.6.2 May the friend of the gods approach me, and fame together with the jewel; I have appeared in this kingdom — may he grant me fame and prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.6.3 Hunger, thirst — the elder <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (the goddess of misfortune) — <s>alakṣmī</s>, I destroy; non-existence and non-prosperity — all I drive out from the house, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.6.4 Her whose gateway is fragrance, who is irresistible, ever-nourished, rich in dung, the sovereign of all beings — her, <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), I invoke here, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.6.5 May we attain the desire of the mind, the intent; the truth of speech; the beauty of cattle; the nourishment of food — may <s>Śrī</s> and glory resort to me, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 347-352: References to RVKh 2.6.6-10, TAA, TA, MahānU, VS, ŚB, KŚ, TB.]

children.text:
6.7.1 kardámena prajā bhūtā mayi sámbhava kardámá
śríyaṃ vāsáya me kulé[*353] mātáraṃ padma-mā́linīṃ svā́hā[*354]
6.7.2 ā́pas sr̥jántu snigdhāni[*355] ciklī́tá vasa me gŕ̥hé
ní ca devī́ṃ mātáraṃ śríyaṃ vāsaya me kulé svā́hā[*356]
6.7.3 ārdrā́ṃ[*357] puṣkáriṇīṃ puṣṭíṃ piṅgálā́ṃ[*358] padma-mālínī́m[*359]
6.7.4 candrā́ṃ hiráṇmayīṃ lakṣmī́ṃ jā́tavedo ma ā́vaha svā́hā[*360]
6.7.5 ā́rdrā́ṃ yaṣkáriṇīṃ[*361] yaṣṭiṃ suvarṇā́ṃ hema-mālínī́m[*362]
6.7.6 sūryā́ṃ hiráṇmayīṃ lakṣmī́ṃ jā́tavedo ma ā́ vaha[*363] svā́hā[*364]
6.7.7 tā́ṃ ma ā́ vaha játavedo lakṣmī́m ánapagāmánīm
yásyāṃ híraṇyaṃ prábhūtaṃ gāvo dāsyó 'śvān vindéyaṃ púruṣān aháṃ svā́hā[*365]
6.7.8 mahā-devyaí ca vidmáhe viṣṇu-patnyaí ca dhīmahi
tán no lakṣmīḥ pracodáyāt svā́hā
[*353] RVKh/VC: gr̥he
[*354] RVKh 2.6.11 (5.87.11) (VC p. 320)
[*355] Text: sigdhāni
[*356] RVKh 2.6.12 (5.87.12) (VC p. 172)
[*357] RVKh/IS: pakvā́m; RVKh/VC: ārdrā́ṃ
[*358] Text: piṅgáḷā́ṃ
[*359] RVKh 2.6.13a (5.87.14a) (VC p. 186)
[*360] RVKh 2.6.14b (5.87.14c) (VC p. 366)
[*361] RVKh: puṣkáriṇīṃ
[*362] RVKh 2.6.14a (5.87.13a) (VC p. 186)
[*363] RVKh: mámā́ vaha replaces ma ā́ vaha
[*364] RVKh 2.6.13b (5.87.13c) (VC p. 1027) In the above four verses, 5.6.7.5-8, note the variation between IS and VC in the order of corresponding verse numbers. IS: 2.6.13a, 14b. 14a, 13b. VC: 5.87.14a, 14c, 13a, 13c.
[*365] RVKh 2.6.15 (5.87.15)
children.translated_text: 6.7.1 O <s>Kardama</s>, creatures were born through you — dwell in me, O <s>Kardama</s>; establish <s>Śrī</s> in my family, the Mother adorned with lotuses, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.7.2 May the waters create moist things; O <s>Ciklīta</s>, dwell in my house; and settle the divine Mother <s>Śrī</s> in my family, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.7.3-4 The moist one, <s>Puṣkariṇī</s> (the lotus-rich), nourishing, tawny, adorned with lotus garlands — the radiant, golden <s>Lakṣmī</s>, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, bring her to me, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.7.5-6 The moist one, bearing a staff, golden, adorned with golden garlands — the sun-like, golden <s>Lakṣmī</s>, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, bring her to me, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.7.7 Bring her to me, O <s>Jātavedas</s> — <s>Lakṣmī</s> who never departs, in whom gold abounds — may I obtain cows, female servants, horses, and men, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.7.8 We meditate upon the Great Goddess; we contemplate the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — may <s>Lakṣmī</s> inspire us, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 353-365: Extensive references to RVKh, IS, and VC with variant readings and verse-order discrepancies.]

children.text: 6.0.3 vr̥ṇomi svā́hā yaśa svā́hā nahaṃ svā́hā dvé ca
children.translated_text: 6.0.3 [Catch-words:] 'I choose, <s>svāhā</s>; glory, <s>svāhā</s>; I, <s>svāhā</s>' — and two [additional mantras].

children.text:
6.8.1 bhūmir bhūmnā́ dyáur variṇā́ntarikṣaṃ mahitvā́
upásthe te devy adite 'gním annādám annā́dyāyā́dadhe svā́hā[*366]
6.8.2 āyáṃ gáuḥ pŕ̥śnir akramīd asanan mātáraṃ punaḥ
pitáraṃ ca prayán sthúvás[*367] svā́hā[*368]
6.8.3 tri(g)ṃśád dhā́ma ví rājati vā́k pataṅgā́ya śiśríye
práty asya vaha dyúbhis svā́hā[*369]
6.8.4 asyá prāṇā́d apānaty antaś carati rocanā́
vyakhyan mahíṣás súvas svā́hā[*370]
6.8.5 yá[*371] tvā kruddháḥ paro vápa manyúnā yád ávartyā
sukálpam agne tát táva púnas tvód dīpayāmasi svā́hā[*372]
[*366] TS 1.5.3.1; 4.1 (VC p. 672)
[*367] TS: prayánt súvaḥ replaces prayán sthúvás
[*368] TS 1.5.3.2
[*369] TS 1.5.3.3
[*370] TS 1.5.3.4
[*371] TS: yat
[*372] TS 1.5.3.5
children.translated_text: 6.8.1 The Earth with its expanse, the sky with its breadth, the atmosphere with its greatness — in your lap, O goddess <s>Aditi</s>, I place <s>Agni</s>, the eater of food, for the eating of food, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.8.2 This speckled cow has stepped forth, seeking its mother again and its father, advancing upward, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.8.3 Thirty abodes shine forth; Speech has alighted upon the flying one; bring him back by days, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.8.4 From his inhalation, his exhalation moves within the luminous realm; the great buffalo has revealed the heavenly light, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.8.5 What [fire], O [sacrificer], you extinguished in anger, what you turned by wrath — that which is easy to restore, O <s>Agni</s>, we rekindle you again, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 366-372: All verses from TS 1.5.3.1-5.]

children.text:
6.9.1 yát te manyúparoptasya pr̥thivī́m ánu dadhvase
ādityā́ víśve tád devā́ vásavaś ca samā́bharan svāhā[*373]
6.9.2 máno jyótir juṣatām ā́jyaṃ vícchinnaṃ yajñá(g)ṃ sam imáṃ dadhātu
bŕ̥haspátis tanutām imáṃ no víśve devā́ ihá mādayantā(g)ṃ svā́hā[*374]
6.9.3 saptá te agne samídhas saptá jihvā́s saptá ŕ̥ṣayas saptá dhā́ma priyā́ṇi
sapta hótrās saptadhā́ tvā yajanti saptá yónīr ā́ pr̥ṇasvā ghr̥téna svā́hā[*375]
6.9.4 púnar ūrjā́ ní vartasva púnar agna iṣā́yuṣā
púnar naḥ pāhi viśvátas svā́hā[*376]
6.9.5 saha rayyā́ ní vártasvā́gne pínvasva dhā́rayā
viśvá-phsniyā viśvátas pári svā́hā[*377]
[*373] TS 1.5.3.6
[*374] TS 1.5.3.7
[*375] TS 1.5.3.8
[*376] TS 1.5.3.9
[*377] TS 1.5.3.10
children.translated_text: 6.9.1 Whatever of you, overspread in anger, was laid upon the earth — the <s>Ādityas</s>, all the gods, and the <s>Vasus</s> gathered that together, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.9.2 May the mind enjoy the light; may the ghee unite this broken sacrifice; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> extend this [sacrifice] of ours; may all the gods here rejoice, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.9.3 Seven are your fuel-sticks, O <s>Agni</s>, seven your tongues, seven the sages, seven your beloved abodes; seven <s>Hotṛ</s>-priests in sevenfold manner worship you — fill the seven wombs with ghee, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.9.4 Return again with vigor; O <s>Agni</s>, again with nourishment and life; protect us from all sides, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.9.5 Return with wealth, O <s>Agni</s>; overflow with your stream, all-nourishing from all sides, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 373-377: All verses from TS 1.5.3.6-10.]

children.text:
6.10.1 medínī devī́ vasúṃdharī syād vásudhā devī́ vāsávī
brahma-varcasáḥ pitr̥ṇā́(g)ṃ śrótraṃ víṣṇur mánas svā́hā
6.10.2 deví híraṇya-garbhiṇī devī́ prasodárī
rásane satyā́yane sīda svā́hā
6.10.3 samudrávatī sāvitrī́há no devī́ mahyákī
mahā́-dháraṇī mahódhya tiṣṭha svā́hā
6.10.4 śr̥ṅgé-śr̥ṅge yajñé-yajñe vibhīṣáṇī
índra-patnī vyājánī súrasita ihá svā́hā[*378]
6.10.5 vāyú-párī jala-śáyanī svayán-dhā́rā satyántho párimedínī
sopári dhattaṃgāya svā́hā
6.10.6 dhanur-dharā́yai vidmáhe sarva-siddhyaí ca dhīmahi
tán no dharāḥ pracodáyāt svā́hā
[*378] cf. VC p. 211
children.translated_text: 6.10.1 The goddess <s>Medinī</s> (Earth), the wealth-bearing one, should be the goddess <s>Vasudhā</s>, the one belonging to <s>Vasu</s>; of <s>Brahma</s>-splendor, the ear of the Ancestors, <s>Viṣṇu</s> [is] the mind, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.10.2 O divine one, bearing the golden embryo, O divine one, with a bountiful womb — sit upon the tongue of truth, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.10.3 The ocean-containing <s>Sāvitrī</s>, our divine, great lady — O great sustainer, great foundation, stand firm, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.10.4 At every summit, at every sacrifice, the terrifying one — the consort of <s>Indra</s>, the fanning one, the impetuous one, here <s>svāhā</s>! 6.10.5 Surrounded by wind, reclining on water, self-sustaining, truth-bounded, encompassing the earth — supporting above, to the cow, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.10.6 We meditate upon the Bow-bearing One; we contemplate All-success — may the Earth inspire us, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.0.4 púnas tvóddīpayāmasi svā́hā viśvátas pári svā́hā sopári dhattaṃgāya svā́hā dvé ca[*379]
[*379] AV 12.2.5; TS 1.5.3.2; 4.2 (VC p. 591)
children.translated_text: 6.0.4 [Catch-words:] 'We rekindle you, <s>svāhā</s>; from all sides, <s>svāhā</s>; supporting above, to the cow, <s>svāhā</s>' — and two [additional mantras]. [Footnote 379: References to AV 12.2.5; TS 1.5.3.2.]

children.text:
6.11.1 svastí caivéha svā́hā
6.11.2 prajā́-pataye svā́hā
6.11.3 ágnir dhī-mataye svā́hā
6.11.4 ādityébhyas svā́hā
6.11.5 víśvebhyo devébhyas svā́hā
6.11.6 marud-gaṇébhyas svā́hā
6.11.7 bhū́r agnáye ca pr̥thivyaí ca mahaté ca svā́hā
bhúvo vāyáve cāntárikṣāya ca mahaté ca svā́hā
súvar ādityā́ya ca divé ca mahaté ca svā́hā
bhū́r bhúvas súvaś candrámase ca nákṣatrebhyaś ca digbhyáś ca mahaté ca svā́hā
children.translated_text: 6.11.1 And well-being here, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.11.2 To <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.11.3 To <s>Agni</s>, the wise one, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.11.4 To the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.11.5 To all the gods, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.11.6 To the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.11.7 <s>Bhūḥ</s> — to <s>Agni</s>, to the Earth, and to the Great One, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> — to <s>Vāyu</s>, to the Atmosphere, and to the Great One, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Suvaḥ</s> — to <s>Āditya</s>, to Heaven, and to the Great One, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Bhūr Bhuvas Suvaḥ</s> — to the Moon, to the Stars, to the Directions, and to the Great One, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.12.1 imám me varuṇa prájā-pate ná tvac cittáṃ cāgnír bhūtā́nām r̥tā-ṣā́ṭ
6.12.2 yád devā yád devā yád ádīvyan[*380] ā́yuṣ ṭe vaiśvānarā́ya
6.12.3 cirāyuṣaṃ yáṃ právadanti dhī́rās sámasta-vedā́rtha-vídāṃ varāya
mārkaṇḍeyā́ya mahā́-munaye svā́hā
6.12.4 púṇyaugha-niṣṭhā́ya púrātanāya nítyātmane brahmá-vidā́ṃ várā́ya svā́hā
6.12.5 pádmā-pitre véda-bhŕ̥tāṃ varāya
mahā-vīryā́yāmíta-tejase svā́hā
6.12.6 bhŕ̥gave mahā́-munaye bráhma-nityāyá
bráhmātmane brahmá-sutāya svā́ḥā
[*380] cf. VMP 5.1.77.8
children.translated_text: 6.12.1 O <s>Varuṇa</s>, [hear] this of mine...; O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you...; the mind, and <s>Agni</s> [lord] of beings; the seat of <s>Ṛta</s>. 6.12.2 What the gods, what the gods gambled...; to your life-span, to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. 6.12.3 The one whom the wise call long-lived, the best among those who know the meaning of all the <s>Vedas</s> — to <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, the great sage, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.12.4 To the one who abides in the flood of merit, the ancient one, the eternal self, the best among the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.12.5 To the Father of <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the best among the bearers of the <s>Vedas</s>, of great valor, of immeasurable splendor, <s>svāhā</s>! 6.12.6 To <s>Bhṛgu</s>, the great sage, eternally devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, whose self is <s>Brahman</s>, the son of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnote 380: Cf. VMP 5.1.77.8.]

children.text:
6.13.1 bráhma jajñānáṃ prathamáṃ purástād vísīmatás surúco vená āvaḥ
sá budhníyā upamā́ ásya viṣṭhā́s satáś ca yónim ásataś ca vívas svā́hā
6.13.2 híraṇya-garbhás sám avartatā́gre bhūtásya jātáḥ pátir éka āsīt
sá dādhāra pr̥thivī́ṃ dyā́m utémā́ṃ kásmai devā́ya havíṣā vidhema svā́hā
6.13.3 rúdram anyáṃ bahutó hutaṃ vr̥ṣabháṃ námas te astu
tán me astu bāhúbhyāṃ vītáye svā́hā
6.13.4 try-ambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhíṃ puṣṭi-várdhanam
urvārukám iva bándhanān mr̥tyór mukṣīya mā́ 'mŕ̥tāt svā́hā
6.13.5 dyā́vā-pr̥thivyóś śug áśuk sanniyoktróḥ
sámmānyayoḥ khyātī́ tu kaúram etā(g)ṃ svā́hā
children.translated_text:
<s>Brahman</s> was born first, from the east, from the boundary of radiance; <s>Vena</s> revealed it.
He, the depths and heights of this [universe], the womb of being and non-being, brought forth, <s>svāhā</s> (oblation)!
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo) came into being in the beginning; born, he was the one lord of all that exists.
He upheld this earth and this heaven — to which <s>deva</s> (god) shall we offer oblation with <s>havis</s> (sacrificial offering)? <s>Svāhā</s>!
To <s>Rudra</s>, the other, much-invoked, the bull — homage be to you!
May that be for my arms, for strength, <s>svāhā</s>!
We worship the three-eyed one (<s>Tryambaka</s>), the fragrant one, the increaser of nourishment;
like a cucumber from its stem, may I be freed from death, not from immortality, <s>svāhā</s>!
The radiance and shadowlessness of heaven and earth, the two that are yoked together,
of those two celebrated ones, may this oblation [reach them], <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.14.1 yasyāś śriyo vā́ ánujā agra-jāyā́ yām évājásra(g)ṃ súhutaṃ viśva-vídbhyām
tābhyā́ṃ prasannā́bhyā(g)ṃ hrā́sa-vr̥ddhī bhavetā(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.14.2 tásthuṣo dhŕ̥tyā dhárate yāni śaṃsáḥ
yásyehá tasmai bhúva eváṃ juhomi svā́hā
6.14.3 yá eṣá bibhraty úru tejaḥ pataṅgáḥ
dívas pári stho bhávato yásya vettú svā́hā
6.14.4 ví tatyá viśvaṃ vídadhāty r̥taṃn náḥ[*381]
vr̥tyā vr̥ttáṃ tasyá nītaṃ tam etat svā́hā
6.14.5 yó no 'bhírakṣaty ávamāya nas tu[*382] yás trayyā́ saṃvárdhayan pū́rayati
tásmai sárva-chándaso sáṃvyayan tā(g)ṃ sā́ no devī́ mānásī́m ānam etā(g)ṃ svā́hā
[*381] 1984 edition: ná
[*382] 1946 edition: ávamānayan tu
children.translated_text:
She whose glory is the younger and the elder-born, whom the wise constantly offer as a well-offered oblation,
may there be waning and waxing through those two propitiated ones, <s>svāhā</s>!
Of the stationary, by steadfastness he sustains what is proclaimed;
to him here in this world I offer this oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who bears the vast radiance, the winged sun,
beyond heaven you two stand — may one know his [nature], <s>svāhā</s>!
He extends all and establishes <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) for us;
by his course the course is guided — this is his ordinance, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who protects us from contempt, who nourishes and fulfills through the triple [<s>Veda</s>],
to him, weaving together all the meters — may that goddess incline her mind to us, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.15.1 munī́ndráṃ bráhma-nityāyá várotkr̥ṣṭā́ya
dauvāriká-prádhānāya máṇikāya svā́hā
6.15.2 sandhyā́yai múni-patnyai prabhā́vatyai dr̥ḍhá-vratāyai svā́hā
6.15.3 vaíkhānasāyā́cyúta-sa(gg)ṃśrayā́ya
tápo-ígra-niṣṭhā́ya ca bráhma-darśine svā́hā
6.15.4 tāpasā́ya síddhi-rājāyá
sa(g)ṃhitā́ya sahásrā́śvamedhine svā́hā
6.15.5 kíṣkindhāya báhu-mardanā́ya
bahu-senā́ya dr̥ḍhá-vrátāya svā́hā
6.15.6 tīrthā́ya sárva-sukhāvahā́ya
sarva-yogyā́ya sárva-darśine svā́hā
children.translated_text:
To <s>Munīndra</s> (lord of sages), devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, chosen as the most exalted,
to the chief gatekeeper <s>Maṇika</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
To <s>Sandhyā</s> (twilight), the sage's wife, to <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, of firm vows, <s>svāhā</s>!
To <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, whose refuge is <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable),
whose foremost devotion is <s>tapas</s> (austerity), and who beholds <s>Brahman</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
To the ascetic, to <s>Siddhi-rāja</s> (king of perfection),
to him of the collected [teachings], performer of a thousand <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifices), <s>svāhā</s>!
To <s>Kiṣkindha</s>, the crusher of many, of great armies, of firm vows, <s>svāhā</s>!
To [him who is] a sacred ford (<s>tīrtha</s>), the bringer of all happiness,
fit for all <s>yoga</s>, the all-seeing one, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 6.0.5 mahaté ca svā́hā bráhmá-sutāya svā́hā kauram etā(g)ṃ svā́hā mānam etā(g)ṃ svā́hā dr̥dhá-vratāya svā́hā dvé ca
children.translated_text: To the great one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the son of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! May this oblation [reach], <s>svāhā</s>! May this honor [reach], <s>svāhā</s>! To him of firm vows, <s>svāhā</s>! And [these are] two.

children.text:
6.16.1 trātā́ram índram avitā́ram índra(g)ṃ háve-have suháva(g)ṃ śū́ram índram
huvé nú[*383] śakráṃ puru-hūtám índrá(gg)ṃ svastí no maghávā dhātv índras svā́hā[*384]
6.16.2 mahā́(g)ṃ índro yá ójasā parjányo vr̥ṣṭimā́(g)ṃ iva
stómair vatsásya[*385] vāvr̥dhe svā́hā[*386]
6.16.3 mahā́(g)ṃ índro nr̥vád ā́ carṣaṇiprā́ utá dvibárhā aminás sáhobhiḥ
asmádríyag vāvr̥dhe vīryāyorúḥ pr̥thús súkr̥taḥ kartŕ̥bhir bhūt svā́hā[*387]
6.16.4 bhúvas tvám indra bráhmaṇā mahā́n bhúvo víśveṣu sávaneṣu yajñíyaḥ
bhúvo nr̥̄́(g)ṃś cyautnó víśvasmin bháre jyéṣṭhaś ca mántro viśva-carṣaṇe svā́hā[*388]
6.16.5 éndra sānasí(g)ṃ rayí(g)ṃ sajítvāna(g)ṃ sadāsáham
várṣiṣṭham ūtáye bhara svā́hā[*389]
[*383] AV, TS: huvé nú; RV, VS (M), KS: hváyāmi
[*384] RV 6.47.11; TS 1.6.12.5 (VC p. 448)
[*385] TB: vathsásya
[*386] RV 8.6.1; TS 1.4.20.1; TB 3.5.7.4 (VC p. 695)
[*387] RV 6.19.1; TS 1.4.21.1; TB 3.5.7.4 (VC p. 695)
[*388] RV 10.50.4; TS 3.4.11.4; AŚ 1.6.1; 4.11.6; 9.5.16 (VC p. 670)
[*389] RV 1.8.1; TS 3.4.11.3; TB 3.5.7.3; AŚ 1.6.1 (VC p. 302)
children.translated_text:
<s>Indra</s> the protector, <s>Indra</s> the helper — in every invocation I call the easily invoked hero <s>Indra</s>;
now I invoke <s>Śakra</s> (the Mighty), <s>Indra</s> invoked by many — may the generous <s>Indra</s> grant us well-being, <s>svāhā</s>!
Great <s>Indra</s>, who by his might is like <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) rich in showers,
has grown great through praises, like a calf, <s>svāhā</s>!
Great <s>Indra</s>, manly, present among all peoples, of double might, undiminished in powers;
for our sake he has grown in heroic strength — the broad, expansive, well-fashioned one became [so] through his deeds, <s>svāhā</s>!
You became great, O <s>Indra</s>, through <s>brahman</s> (sacred utterance); you became worthy of worship at all <s>savana</s> (pressings of Soma);
you became the impeller of men, foremost in every contest, and the greatest <s>mantra</s> (hymn) among all peoples, <s>svāhā</s>!
O <s>Indra</s>, bring to us conquering wealth, ever-victorious, ever-surpassing,
the most excellent, for our protection, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.17.1 prá sasāhiṣe puru-hūta śátrūñ jyéṣṭhas te śúṣma ihá rātír astu
índrā́ bhara dákṣiṇenā vásūni pátis síndhūnām asi revátīnā(g)ṃ svā́hā[*390]
6.17.2 asmā́kam índras sámr̥teṣu dhvajéṣv[*391] asmā́kaṃ yā́ íṣavas tā́ jayantu
asmā́kaṃ vīrā́ úttare bhavantv asmā́n u devā avatā háveṣu svā́hā[*392]
6.17.3 índro 'bhūd asyá bhúvanasya rājéndro dādhāra pr̥thivī́n dyā́m uté mā́m
indro ha víśvāni bhūtā́ni bhúvánāśritā́ni svā́hā
6.17.4 índro dyaúr vyóma bhū́r indrás sámudbháva no vírāṭ páśca
urv-antarikṣa-svargá-pavanam índrād índraṃ mánye pitáraṃ mātáraṃ ca svā́hā
6.17.5 índraṃ práṇayantaṃ vápur índra(gg)ṃ srávanta(g)ṃ savitā́ram índraṃ dadhātu
śákras sukŕ̥tasya lokám índraṃ manye pitáraṃ mātáraṃ ca svā́hā
[*390] RV 10.180.1; TS 3.4.11.4; MS 4.12.3: 184.15; 4.14.18: 248.17; TB 2.6.9.1; 3.5.7.4; AŚ 1.6.1; 3.7.11; 4.11.6; etc. (VC p. 631)
[*391] Text: thvajéṣv
[*392] RV 10.103.11; TS 4.6.4.3; MS 2.10.4: 136.11; 4.14.14: 238.11 (VC p. 140)

6.18.1 índro vr̥tráṃ vájreṇāvadhīd índro vyáyas sámudra-śuṣkaḥ
índraṃ manye pitáraṃ mātáraṃ ca svā́hā
6.18.2 índro babhūva bráhmaṇo gambhīrám ā́bhūti-párituṣṭiḥ
índro bhaviṣyád utá bhūtám índraṃ manye pitáraṃ mātáraṃ ca svā́hā
6.18.3 índro 'smā́n avatu vájra-bāhur índro bhūtā́ni bhúvanāni
índro 'smā́kam avatu vájra-prasādam índraṃ manye pitáraṃ mātáraṃ ca svā́hā[*393]
6.18.4 agnír mūrdhā́ diváḥ kakút-pátiḥ pr̥thivyā́ ayám
apā́(g)ṃ rétā́(g)ṃsi jinvati svā́hā
6.18.5 ayám agnís sahasríṇo vā́jasya śatínas pátiḥ
mūrdhā́ kavī́ rayīṇā́(g)ṃ svā́hā
[*393] MS 4.14.7: 225.13-14 (VC p.229)
children.translated_text:
<s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s> with his <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt); <s>Indra</s> [dried up] the waters when the ocean was drained;
I consider <s>Indra</s> as father and mother, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Indra</s> came into being through <s>brahman</s> (sacred power), the profound, the abundance and satisfaction;
<s>Indra</s> shall be in the future and was in the past — I consider <s>Indra</s> as father and mother, <s>svāhā</s>!
May <s>Indra</s> protect us, the <s>vajra</s>-armed (thunderbolt-armed); may <s>Indra</s> [protect] all beings and worlds;
may <s>Indra</s> protect us with the grace of his <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) — I consider <s>Indra</s> as father and mother, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Agni</s> is the head, the pinnacle of heaven, the lord of the earth;
he quickens the seed of the waters, <s>svāhā</s>!
This <s>Agni</s>, lord of thousandfold and hundredfold sustenance,
is the head, the sage among riches, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.19.1 yamó dādhāra pr̥thivī́ṃ yamó dyā́m utá sū́ryaḥ[*394]
yamás sárva-mr̥tyus stenáḥ[*395] prāṇā́nāṃ vāyūnā́(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.19.2 námas te nírr̥taye ghána-tejāya tásmai vísr̥ja bándhanāt
6.19.3 yáma naya tvá(g)ṃ sávitā́ devá uttamā́n ánīke abhírócaya yāyinā́(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.19.4 vásavaḥ prathamó devátānā(g)ṃ so 'sya prajā́ṃ paśū́n pāhi
6.19.5 áto devébhyaḥ paśúbhir yó vaí vásavas svasty ástu svā́hā
6.19.6 sahasrākṣó vā́ ayám agníḥ pitaro devátānām
6.19.7 vásūn yátra vásavo bhūtā́nāṃ pā́layanti tásmā ánya-vasubhya svā́hā
6.19.8 yé te śatáṃ váruṇa yé sahásraṃ yajñíyāḥ pā́śā vítatāḥ púrutrā́
tébhyo na índras savitótá víṣṇur víśvedevā́ muñcantu marútas svastyā́ svā́hā
[*394] KS: sūryam
[*395] cf. VMP 8.1.151.6: te náḥ instead of stenáḥ
children.translated_text:
<s>Yama</s> upheld the earth; <s>Yama</s> [upheld] heaven and the sun;
<s>Yama</s> is the thief of all death, of the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) and the winds, <s>svāhā</s>!
Homage to you, O <s>Nirṛti</s> (goddess of destruction), of dense radiance — release him from bondage!
O <s>Yama</s>, lead [him]; may <s>Savitṛ</s> the <s>deva</s> (god) illumine the highest realms for those who journey, <s>svāhā</s>!
The <s>Vasus</s> are the foremost among the <s>devatās</s> (deities) — may he protect your offspring and cattle!
Therefore, to the <s>devas</s> (gods), with cattle — he who is indeed of the <s>Vasus</s> — may there be well-being, <s>svāhā</s>!
This <s>Agni</s>, the thousand-eyed, is the father of the <s>devatās</s> (deities);
where the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Vasus</s> of beings, protect — to him, to those other <s>Vasus</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
Your hundred snares, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, your thousand sacrificial bonds spread in many places —
from those, may <s>Indra</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods), and the <s>Maruts</s> release us to well-being, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.20.1 úd uttamáṃ varuṇa pā́śam asmád ávādhámáṃ ví madhyamá(gg)ṃ śrathāya
áthā vayám āditya vraté távā́nāgaso áditaye syāma svā́hā
6.20.2 ayā́ś cāgné 'sy anabhíśastī́ś cāyā́taḥ
yajñáṃ vahatu sadā́ dhehi bheṣajá(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.20.3 ā́pas sr̥jántu[*396] snigdhāni ciklītá vasa me gŕ̥hé
ní ca devī́ṃ mātáraṃ śríyaṃ vāsáya me kulé svā́hā
6.20.4 marútaḥ paramātmā́ páramā gatíḥ páraṃ bráhma páraṃ yógam
paramātmā́naṃ manye ajáraṃ yo 'gnir ahám ánnaṃ vāyáve svā́hā
6.20.5 marúto gaṇā́nāṃ prathamás saptádhānāṃ mūrdhā́ vāyo ányam ajárá(gg)ṃ śriyám
hótāraṃ vaí ráyan tvā́hur ágne havyáṃ marúdbhyas svā́hā
6.20.6 miśrá-vāsasaḥ kauberakā́ rakṣo-rājéna préṣitāḥ
grā́ma(g)ṃ sá-jānayo gacchántīcchánto paridā́kr̥tā́nt[*397] svā́hā
6.20.7 etā́n ghnataitā́n gr̥hṇītéty ayáṃ bráhmaṇas putráḥ
tā́n agníḥ páryasarat tā́n índras tā́n bŕ̥haspátiḥ
tā́n aháṃ veda brāhmaṇáḥ pramr̥śatáḥ kūṭa-dantā́n vikeśā́ṇ lambana-stanā́nth[*398] svā́hā
6.20.8 ī́śānas sárva-lokānā́ṃ try-ambakas sárva-vidyānā́m
ná dvitīyo bhavodbhavāya svā́hā
6.20.9 ī́śa ī́śitre bhū́r bhúvas súvar ī́śāya lokā́nām
bhīmā́ya vāmadevā́ya svā́hā
[*396] RVKh: sravantu
[*397] Text: 'paridā́kr̥tā́nth
[*398] ApMB: -stanā́nt
children.translated_text: 6.20.1 'Release from us the uppermost bond, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, loosen the lowest and the middle one! Then, O <s>Āditya</s>, may we be sinless in your ordinance, [devoted] to <s>Aditi</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.2 'You are of these, O <s>Agni</s>, and of the unblamable ones that have come; may [the sacrifice] carry the offering; always bestow healing, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.3 'May the waters release unctuous [substances]; O purified one, dwell in my house! And settle the divine mother <s>Śrī</s> in my family, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.4 'The <s>Maruts</s> [are] the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), the supreme goal, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme <s>Yoga</s>; I consider the Supreme Self to be unaging — who is <s>Agni</s>; I am food — to <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.5 'The <s>Maruts</s>, foremost of the hosts, heads of the seven-fold [streams]; O <s>Vāyu</s>, [grant us] another unaging glory! They call you the invoker (<s>Hotṛ</s>), O radiant <s>Agni</s> — the oblation to the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.6 'Clad in mixed garments, the followers of <s>Kubera</s>, sent by the king of <s>rākṣasas</s>, go to the village with their kin, desiring to seize those who are marked out, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.7 '"Strike these! Seize these!" — thus [speaks] this son of <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Agni</s> went around them, <s>Indra</s> [pursued] them, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [pursued] them. I, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, know those who touch [with evil] — the ones with crooked teeth, disheveled hair, and pendulous breasts, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.8 'The ruler (<s>Īśāna</s>) of all worlds, the three-eyed one (<s>Tryambaka</s>) [lord] of all knowledge — there is no second — to the one born from existence (<s>Bhavodbhava</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.20.9 'The Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) rules; <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvas</s>, <s>Suvar</s> — to the Lord of the worlds, to the terrible one (<s>Bhīma</s>), to the Beautiful God (<s>Vāmadeva</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 6.0.6 bhára svā́hā mātáraṃ ca svā́hā rayīṇā́(g)ṃ svā́hā svastyā́ svā́hā marúdbhyas svā́hā náva ca
children.translated_text: 6.0.6 [Rubric:] 'Bear, <s>svāhā</s>! And the mother, <s>svāhā</s>! Of riches, <s>svāhā</s>! With well-being, <s>svāhā</s>! To the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — and nine [more mantras].

children.text:
6.21.1 úd u tyáṃ jātá-vedasaṃ deváṃ vahanti ketávaḥ
dr̥śé víśvāya sū́rya(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.21.2 citrán devā́nām úd agād ánīkaṃ cákṣur mitrásya váruṇasyāgnéḥ
ā́prā dyā́vā-pr̥thivī́ antárikṣa(g)ṃ sū́rya ātmā́ jágatas tasthúṣapaś[*399] ca svā́hā
6.21.3 mámāgne várco vihavéṣv astu vayán tvéndhānās tanúvaṃ puṣema
máhyaṃ namantām pradíśaś cátasras tváyā́dhyakṣeṇa pŕ̥tanā jayema svā́hā[*400]
6.21.4 ahám agner agníṃ gr̥hṇāmi mámāgne 'gnír mámāntárikṣam
mā́rgo 'hám asmín prámadān kāmáye túbhyaṃ mánasā prajā́-pátaye svā́hā
6.21.5 ágna ā́ yāhi vītáye gr̥ṇānó havyádātaye
ní hótā sathsi[*401] barhíṣi svā́hā
[*399] RV: tasthúṣaś
[*400] This text is an example of how the 1946 edition is more reliable for accents. In this instance it more accurately reflects the RV than the 1984 edition.
[*401] RV: satsi
children.translated_text: 6.21.1 'Up they bear that god <s>Jātavedas</s>; the rays [bear] <s>Sūrya</s> for all to see, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.21.2 'The brilliant face of the gods has risen — the eye of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>. He has filled heaven, earth, and the atmosphere — <s>Sūrya</s>, the Self of all that moves and stands, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.21.3 'May my splendor be in the invocations, O <s>Agni</s>; may we, kindling you, nourish [our] body! May the four directions bow to me; with you as overseer may we conquer in battle, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.21.4 'I take fire from fire; mine is the fire, O <s>Agni</s>, mine is the atmosphere. I am the path; in this [rite] I desire joy — to you in mind, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.21.5 'O <s>Agni</s>, come to the feast, invoked [by us], to the giving of oblation! Sit down as the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker) on the sacred grass, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.22.1 prabhur devó mando 'sitáś cāvyáyaḥ púruṣo víśvāya sū́ryāya svā́hā
6.22.2 grahā́dhipatiḥ pr̥thivī́ cāntárikṣaṃ ca
6.22.3 sū́rya ātmā́ jágatas tasthúṣaś ca svā́hā
6.22.4 bŕ̥haspatir devā́nām imáṃ yajñáṃ br̥ható me dadhātu
bŕ̥haspáti-vītaye svā́hā
6.22.5 bŕ̥haspátis sóman dadhātu bŕ̥haspátir yajñáṃ dadhātu
bŕ̥haspáti-vītaye svā́hā
6.22.6 bŕ̥haspáte áti yád aryó árhād dyumád vibhā́ti krátumaj jáneṣu
yád dīdáyac chávasarta-prajāta tád asmā́su dráviṇaṃ dhehi citrá(gg)ṃ svā́hā
children.translated_text: 6.22.1 'The Lord, the god, exhilarating, and dark (<s>Asita</s>), and imperishable — the <s>Puruṣa</s> — to the all-pervading <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.22.2 'The lord of the planets (<s>grahādhipati</s>), and the earth, and the atmosphere.' 6.22.3 '<s>Sūrya</s>, the Self of all that moves and stands, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.22.4 'May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> of the gods grant this sacrifice for me, [and] greatness. For the enjoyment of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.22.5 'May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> bestow <s>Soma</s>; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> bestow the sacrifice. For the enjoyment of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.22.6 'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, whatever [wealth] that transcends the generous one's [giving], that shines brilliantly, full of purpose among people — that which gleams, born of power — place that wonderful wealth upon us, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.23.1 upayāmá-gr̥hīto 'si bŕ̥haspate tveṣáte yóniḥ
bŕ̥haspáti-vītaye svā́hā
6.23.2 śraviṣṭhá-jó yaḥ páramo nu goptā́ prajā́-pateḥ prathamá(g)ṃ hūyámānaḥ
6.23.3 prajā́-pataye 'sū́yamāna suṣúve yam bha-pas svā́hā
6.23.4 tád víṣṇoḥ paramáṃ
tád víprāsaḥ
6.23.5 prájā-pate ná tvád etāny anyó víśvā jātā́ni pári tā́ babhūva
yat kāmās te juhumás tán no astu vayá(gg)ṃ syāma pátayo rayīṇā́(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.23.6 subhū́s sváyam-bhū́ḥ prathamáṃ[*402] mahaty arṇavé dadhe ha gárbham r̥tvíyam
yáto jātáḥ prajā́-patis svā́hā
6.23.7 bhū bhā́minī bhúve-bhuve
6.23.8 bhū́r bhúvas súvar lóka-pāvanyai svā́hā
6.23.9 íṣṭa-gāminy aniṣṭa-ghnī́ nalíny[*403] eka-mūrdhní tásthur jāhnavyaí svā́hā
6.23.10 sóma yā́s te máyo-bhúva ūtáyas sánti dāśúṣe
tā́bhir no 'vitā́ bhava svā́hā
6.23.11 yā́ te dhā́māni diví yā́ pr̥thivyā́ṃ yā́ párvateṣv óṣadhīṣv apsú
tébhir no víśvais sumánā áhedan[*404] rā́janth[*405] soma práti havyā́ gr̥bhāya svā́hā
6.23.12 rúdram anyáṃ try-ambakam
[*402] VS: prathamo 'ntar
[*403] Text: naḷíny
[*404] RV: áhelan
[*405] RV: rājan
children.translated_text: 6.23.1 'You are taken with the <s>upayāma</s> [vessel], O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the source of fierce brilliance. For the enjoyment of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.2 'Born under <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, the supreme protector of <s>Prajāpati</s>, being invoked first.' 6.23.3 'To <s>Prajāpati</s> — the one being urged forth, whom the radiant one has generated, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.4 'That supreme [step] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>...' 'That the sages...' 6.23.5 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you has encompassed all these beings that have come into existence. May that for which we offer to you with desire be ours; may we be lords of riches, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.6 'The well-being one, the Self-existent (<s>Svayambhū</s>), first in the great ocean placed the seasonal embryo; from which <s>Prajāpati</s> was born, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.7 '<s>Bhū</s>, the radiant one, in world after world.' 6.23.8 '<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvas</s>, <s>Suvar</s> — to the Purifier of the worlds, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.9 'Going to the desired, destroying the undesired, lotus-bearing, standing single-headed — to <s>Jāhnavī</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.10 'O <s>Soma</s>, those aids of yours that are joy-giving for the worshipper — with those be our protector, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.11 'Those abodes of yours that are in heaven, that are on earth, that are in the mountains, in the herbs, in the waters — with all those, O King <s>Soma</s>, being gracious and uninjured, accept our oblations, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.23.12 'Another [hymn to] <s>Rudra</s>, the three-eyed one (<s>Tryambaka</s>).'

children.text: 6.0.7 barhíṣi svā́hā citrá(gg)ṃ svā́hā suveṣṭaú ca
children.translated_text: 6.0.7 [Rubric:] 'On the sacred grass, <s>svāhā</s>! The wonderful, <s>svāhā</s>!' — and the two <s>Suveṣṭa</s> [mantras].

children.text:
6.24.1[*406] jágad-bhuvaṃ bahutó hutaṃ yájad-bhuvan námas te astu
víśva-bhúve svā́hā
6.24.2 jágad-bhavó 'dhipatis senā-nī́r máyūra-priyáṣ ṣáḍ ānana āṅgāráḥ
sáñjáyā́ há námas te 'stu sukhā́vahāya svā́hā
6.24.3 subrahmaṇyó[*407] bŕ̥haspátes sutā́yāsya padma-yonéḥ
yásyātmā́ váhane vahati svā́hā
6.24.4 subrahmaṇyó rúdra-bhuvo bráhma-bhuvaḥ
bhavódbhavo mámāmŕ̥tāya svā́hā
6.24.5 jágad-bhuvas subrahmaṇyáḥ kŕ̥ttikā-sutáḥ
ṣaṣṭikā́ya svā́hā
[*406] 25 in book.
[*407] 1946 edition: subahaṇyo
children.translated_text: 6.24.1 'To the one born of the world (<s>Jagadbhuva</s>), offered by many, born of sacrifice (<s>Yajadbhuva</s>) — obeisance be to you! To the one born of all (<s>Viśvabhuva</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.24.2 'The world-born one, the overlord, the army-leader (<s>Senānī</s>), the peacock-lover, the six-faced one (<s>Ṣaḍānana</s>), the Glowing One (<s>Āṅgāra</s>) — with <s>Sañjayā</s> indeed; obeisance be to you, to the bringer of happiness, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.24.3 'The excellent devotee (<s>Subrahmaṇya</s>), the son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, of the lotus-born one — whose Self carries in the conveyance, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.24.4 'The excellent devotee (<s>Subrahmaṇya</s>), born of <s>Rudra</s>, born of <s>Brahman</s> — born from <s>Bhava</s>, for my immortality, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.24.5 'The world-born one, the excellent devotee (<s>Subrahmaṇya</s>), the son of the <s>Kṛttikās</s> — to the sixty-fold one, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.25.1 jágad-bhuvo yó yájad-bhuva skánda-viśākha-netā́
hávyam asmā́t ṣáṇ-mukhāya svā́hā
6.25.2 áto devā́
idáṃ víṣṇuḥ
6.25.3 yā́ brahmacāríṇy ámarāṇām údagrāyās sannámitā agra etā́ ramante
tásyā ānaya tváṃ havíṣo mātariśvanth svā́hā
6.25.4 sā́ cāru-janmā́ 'malā kasya jātā́ bhūtaís súmānyā vividhaíś śáṅkaraiṣā
hr̥ṣādhr̥ṣyā́ bahír antar vasū́nā(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.25.5 eṣā́marāṇā́ṅ gúrave satyám ādádhāti yā́ prā́dadhac cā́vani-gopā́m
sádasyā́ rameta sā́ rakṣatu nas sadā́ vai svā́hā
6.25.6 yā́myā niyamyā́ páramā kāla[*408]-randhrā́ kā́kānibhā sū́ninī sā́ rametām
dattáṃ japtáṃ pū́jitaṃ vā hután nas tasyā́ agnā́v etu pātu sadā nas svā́hā[*409]
[*408] Text: kāḷa
[*409] VMP divides this verse making the second line the first line of chapter 26. The numbering is adjusted so that the complete verse comes at the end of chapter 25.
children.translated_text: 6.25.1 'The world-born one who is sacrifice-born, the leader of <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Viśākha</s> — the oblation from this to the Six-faced One (<s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.25.2 'From here the gods...' 'This <s>Viṣṇu</s>...' 6.25.3 'She who is the <s>brahmacāriṇī</s> of the immortals, the foremost among the lofty ones, bowed before them — they delight in her. You, O <s>Mātariśvan</s>, bring for her the oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.25.4 'She, of beautiful birth, spotless — whose [daughter] is she born? By various beings, she of good honor, auspicious — fearlessly bold, within and without the treasures, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.25.5 'She indeed places truth in the teacher of the immortals, she who also established the earth-guardian. May the assembly-member delight; may she protect us always, truly, <s>svāhā</s>!' 6.25.6 'She who is to be restrained, to be controlled, the supreme one, the aperture of time, dark-complexioned like a crow, the fruitful one — may she delight! May that which is given, muttered, worshipped, or offered by us go to her fire; may she protect us always, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.26.1 jātávedase sunavāma sómam arātīyató ní dahāti[*410] védaḥ
sá naḥ parṣad áti durgā́ṇi víśvā nāvéva síndhuṃ duritā́ty agní svā́hā
6.26.2 tā́m agní-varṇāṃ tápasā jvalantī́ṃ vairocanī́ṃ karma-phaléṣu júṣṭām
durgā́ṃ devī́(g)ṃ śáraṇam aháṃ prápadye sutárasi tarase námas[*411] svā́hā
6.26.3 ágne tváṃ pārayā návyo asmā́nth[*412] svastíbhir áti durgā́ṇi víśvā
pū́ś ca pr̥thvī́ bahulā́ na urvī́ bhávā tokā́ya tánayāya śáṃ yos svā́hā
6.26.4 víśvāni no durgá-hā́ jātavedas síndhuṃ ná nāvā́ duritā́ti parṣi
ágne atriván mánasā[*413] gr̥ṇāno 'smākaṃ bodhy avitā[*414] tanū́nā(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.26.5 pr̥tanā-jíta(g)ṃ sáhamānam agním ugrá(g)ṃ huvema páramā́th sadhásthāt
sá naḥ parṣad áti durgā́ṇi víśvā kṣā́mad devó áti duritā́ty agnís svā́hā
6.26.6 pratnó ṣi[*415] kam ī́ḍyo ádhvaréṣu sánāc ca hótā návyaś ca sáthsi
svā́ṃ cāgne tanúvaṃ pipríyasvāsmábhyaṃ ca saúbhagam ā́ yajasva svā́hā
[*410] Text: dahātti
[*411] In RVKh the phrase sutárasi tarase námas appears twice in the verse, whereas VMP only gives it once.
[*412] RV: asmān
[*413] RV: námasā
[*414] Text: bhūtva vitā́
[*415] RV: hi
children.translated_text: (6.26.1) 'To <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press <s>Soma</s>; may he who is our knowledge burn down the hostile ones. May he carry us past all dangers, as a boat across a river — <s>Agni</s>, past evils, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.26.2) 'I take refuge in her who is fire-colored, blazing with austerity, daughter of <s>Virocana</s>, invoked in the fruits of action — the goddess <s>Durgā</s>. You who transport well, obeisance to you the transporter, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.26.3) 'O <s>Agni</s>, carry us across by newer paths, with blessings, past all dangers. Be broad and vast earth for us — be the source of happiness for our offspring and descendants, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.26.4) 'O <s>Jātavedas</s>, carry us past all hardships, as a boat across a river, past evils. O <s>Agni</s>, being praised with devotion like <s>Atri</s>, be the protector of our bodies, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.26.5) 'Let us invoke <s>Agni</s>, the battle-winner, the overpowering, the fierce one, from the highest seat. May he carry us past all dangers — may the god <s>Agni</s> deliver us from evils, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.26.6) 'You are the ancient one, worthy of praise in sacrifices. Of old a <s>Hotṛ</s> priest, and ever new you remain. Delight your own form, O <s>Agni</s>, and sacrifice good fortune for us, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 6.0.8 ṣaṣṭíkā́ya svā́hā ramétā́ṃ th sádhásthā trīṇi ca
children.translated_text: (6.0.8) [Rubric:] 'To the sixtieth, <s>svāhā</s>...' '...may they delight at the seat' — and three [mantras].

children.text:
6.27.1 nandínyā mū́lavatyā jágato vasatyā́ jyeṣṭhā́yā astu suhutá(g)ṃ hutám
svasur devyā́ dharitryā rajáta-priyāyās svā́hā
6.27.2 ā́pó vivéśa prajáyā brahma-dārā́s skandá-prabarháṃ bháraṇe vidma devyā́ḥ
vegínī devī́ śárma deyāt sadā nas svā́hā
6.27.3 śā́khā-bhūta suśā́khayā divó bhettúm ayūyujat
dhātā́ devyā́ yájāma homā́gryāṃ tátra vāhiny udetu svā́hā
6.27.4 devī́ pravā́hiny ániśaṃ pāti-bhūtá(g)ṃ sarvaṃ chandó víkīrayan
bhajato mé śivaṃ dhattā́ṃ jáyā vr̥ttáṃ járayatv ā́dhim eṣā́ svā́hā
6.27.5 bisínī bhūtā́ jánanīvā sr̥jánty útā́vanītā bráhmaṇy adhy upā́ste
tā́ṃ vidyútā́(g)ṃ samyág u tarpayāmi svā́hā
children.translated_text: (6.27.1) 'Of <s>Nandinī</s>, rooted, dwelling in the world, the eldest — may the offering be well-offered. Of the divine sister, the sustainer, who loves silver, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.27.2) 'She entered the waters with offspring; the sacred wives of <s>Brahman</s>. We know the streaming forth of <s>Skanda</s> in bearing, of the goddess. May the swift goddess <s>Vegīnī</s> always grant us shelter, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.27.3) 'She who is branches, with good branches, yoked to break through heaven — let us worship <s>Dhātṛ</s>'s goddess; may the carrying one rise forth there in the principal oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.27.4) 'The goddess, flowing unceasingly, protecting all that has become, scattering all metres — may she grant auspiciousness to the one who worships me; may <s>Jayā</s> (Victory) destroy and consume grief, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.27.5) 'She who, having become the lotus-stemmed one, releases like a mother, and being led away, dwells in the <s>Brahman</s> — I properly satisfy her, the lightning-like one, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.28.1 pravidyutāyā́ súmano-dharā cā́muṃ virañjáty[*416] atá eṣa panthā́ḥ
tasyābhavat víndu-karānuráñjo juhomi sā́ no śiva-dā́ vidheyā svā́hā
6.28.2 gaṅgā-vā́ṇī sárasvatī phalaty ūrdhvá(g)ṃ śivā́ya nas sádābhayā bhavet
táta ādā́nam emi dhā́tus samastáṃ vísr̥jantīha devyā́s tasyā́ agnā́v etu pātu sadā nas svā́hā
6.28.3 vidyā́ṃ nno mā́tu vítanotu māná(g)ṃ sómena saumyā́ṃ ávatārayantu
táyā pratyáṅgaṃ vívr̥taṃ yad viśāmó 'mógháṃ vídma prajáyā brahmá etát svā́hā
6.28.4 mātā́ hy améyā máhī mūrtimatyā́ yáyā satváṃ[*417] vítanotīndriyéṣu
yásyā́ asyā́ váśa-niṣṭham ajāyata svaíriṇyā sā bhū́taye me bhavetā(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.28.5 ā́yām ahan tvā́ jánanīṃ prāṇina[s] syúḥ prājñā́ḥ prajñā́tām etyā́dhyavasthā́ṃ mamá dhiyo niyogám
pravāhiṇy ánaíṣi mama dhehi[*418] priyá(g)ṃ sā mā na hí(g)ṃsī svā́hā
[*416] 1984 edition: vīrañjáty; 1946, 1926 eds.: virañjáty
[*417] 1946 edition: sasatvaṃ
[*418] Text: thehi
children.translated_text: (6.28.1) 'Of the flashing one, the bearer of good minds, she illumines that [region]; hence is this path. Hers was the making of ornamental dots. I offer to her; may she, the giver of blessings, be our guiding one, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.28.2) 'The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s> — she bears fruit upward, auspicious for us, ever without fear. Thence I go to receive the entire substance of <s>Dhātṛ</s>; of the goddess who releases here, may hers be in the fire; may she protect us always, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.28.3) 'May she extend knowledge and honor to us as a mother. May they, with <s>Soma</s>, bring down the gentle one. Whatever limb is uncovered by her when we enter — we know this unfailing <s>Brahman</s> with offspring, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.28.4) 'The mother is immeasurable, the great embodied one, by whom truth is extended in the senses. From whose domain what is subject to her will was born — may she, the free-willed one, be for my prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.28.5) 'I have come to you, the mother. May breathing beings be wise; let them reach the well-known state of wisdom, and the command of my thoughts. O Flowing One, you have led me — place what is dear in me; do not harm us, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.29.1 yáyā satas satyáṃ várata uditaṃ jyāyó jāyā́yai jarasáṃ vidhatte
táta újjihānāṃ tanúbhiś catúrbhir ímām agacchat svakáyā mahimnā svā́hā
6.29.2 prasaviṇy aṅgé mánavo vicakṣávo yáyā tu vr̥ddhíṃ várdhayanto viyāntáḥ
súbodham ānínyuḥ prásavaṃ prajā́nāṃ tádā ta ebhír vahantu puṣṭí(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.29.3 yābhyo hi taptáṅ kr̥nvánto[*419] ínujātā́ yā́bhyo[*420] bhavaty árcir harā ca dhūrtíḥ
devyáḥ prasannā́ dhava-sammatā́ yā́ vahantu naś śá(g)ṃ súyaśaḥ kriyāsu svā́hā
6.29.4 yā́ mānasā vā́dhigátānuṣaṅgā́ḥ kriyā́su satyáḥ prasávas svávaitu
sánnīyate yā́bhir avantu devyó yájāmahe[*421] tád dhavíṣo tatābhyas svā́hā
6.29.5 yátas svám ā́sīd dhŕ̥dayād anādér ŕ̥ṣis tviṣādī́pya jágad dadhāra
khyātér īśase dhr̥g-agnaú juhomi svā́hā
[*419] Present stem in older form: kr̥ṇu.
[*420] Text: 'yā́bhyo
[*421] 1946 edition: yájāmaho
children.translated_text: (6.29.1) 'By whom the true truth of beings is spoken, who bestows old age upon the wife who is greater — thence she, rising up, with four bodies, came to this with her own greatness, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.29.2) 'In whose limbs the discerning <s>Manus</s> generate, by whom the departing ones increase their growth — they brought forth the easily-awakened progeny of creatures; then may these carry nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.29.3) 'For whom the performed austerity, being born of them, and from whom arises flame and also destructive force — the goddesses, pleased and approved by the sacrificer, may they carry to us blessings and good fame in our rites, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.29.4) 'Those mental and consequential attachments — may the generation in rites be true and well-born. May the goddesses by whom things are gathered together protect us; we sacrifice to them that oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.29.5) 'From where his own [light] arose, from the heart of the beginningless one — the <s>Ṛṣi</s>, blazing with splendor, upheld the world. To <s>Khyāti</s>'s lord I offer in the fire of firmness, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.30.1 asmā́ asmād[*422] ā́dadānó[*423] 'da éno[*424] búddhinā yó svá-tápasaḥ
āyá māṃ bhū́yo bhū́yas sr̥té[*425] ghr̥té svā́hā
6.30.2 kásyā́ṅgirā abhūc chíraso yáṃ mánanti
śréṣṭháṃ víbhor vītī́ hotre dadeya(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.30.3 vísmāpayaty átra múdā babhāse
pópuṣyate syā́t prabháyāgamo nas svā́hā
6.30.4 vyā́vartate yó vibúdho vyāna eṣá vyā́pūrayan nó dharáté[*426] sarvam arvā́k
tásmād eváṃ juhutaś śá(g)ṃ sametu svā́hā
6.30.5 sá smā[*427] rasó 'gre asr̥jac cátasraḥ kanyās sa ukthyaṃ ca sá kīrtimantáḥ
smŕ̥tyā tásmād itá etu hótus svā́hā
[*422] cf. RV 6.42.4 (VC p. 138)
[*423] 1984 edition: ā́dadau nó
[*424] Text: éna
[*425] 1984 edition: pr̥te
[*426] 1946 edition: vyā́pūrayan nó tharáté
[*427] cf. RV 5.7.4 (VC p. 999)
children.translated_text: (6.30.1) 'From this, from that, taking, he [removed] sin through wisdom, he of his own austerity. Come to me again and again, in the flowing ghee, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.30.2) 'Whose <s>Aṅgiras</s> was he? From whose head? Whom they consider the best of the mighty — may I give to the <s>Hotṛ</s> at the invocation, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.30.3) 'He astonishes; here he shone with delight. May he prosper; may the approach of radiance be to us, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.30.4) 'He who, wise, turns about — this is the diffused breath, filling us; he holds everything near. From him, thus, may what is offered bring us blessings, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.30.5) 'He, the essence, in the beginning released the four maidens, and that which is to be praised, and the famous ones. From him, therefore, through <s>Smṛti</s> (memory), may [wisdom] come here to the <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.31.1 yá éṣódāná[*428] údítaḥ pulastyá upoṣa[*429] viśváṃ prábháyāham asmaí
júhomi ŕ̥ṣaye só 'vatu[*430] śárma svā́hā
6.31.2 ānándá rodaítya saraḥ púlastyáḥ prītyā́ tráyan tát sahate dvitīyáḥ
tásyāsti sānnidhyán níyata(g)ṃ rakṣatu svā́hā
6.31.3 prá prāyáśo pā́na[*431] idaṃ vapur yás te pā́pam ágryáḥ krátu-kīrti-kāmáḥ
tám ā́hutīr yó 'juhuta pretá eṣás svā́hā
6.31.4 yé níṣyantā ájāyanta patánty arka-pathā́ api
tántus tárhi tásmai yajāni svā́hā
6.31.5 yó no vásiṣṭhas sá sa-māna-jātáḥ kasyā́śéṣa(g)ṃ sárvam ídan tatāra
tásmai yaja ī́śāya munáya idán tu svā́hā
6.31.6 saptóttámā yé múnayo vásiṣṭha ū́rjā tú tébhyas sá hi tebhyas sujātáḥ
nityám asmā́d ámudajāni svā́hā
6.31.7 yá ānasūyéśo nídadhan nirakṣás sa(gg)ṃsā́rá-velā́m údíto rarakṣa
bhū́yād áya(g)ṃ váṃśa-karo 'sya vaṃśás svā́hā
6.31.8 yá eṣá digbhyó vavŕ̥dhe 'trī rā́jā
asmaí tásyedáṃ juhutó rātú sóma(gg)ṃ svā́hā
[*428] Text: éṣó 'dāná
[*429] 1984, 1946 editions: uṣopa; 1926 edition: upoṣa
[*430] 1926 edition here inserts the word yātu
[*431] cf. RV 7.8.4; TS 2.5.12.4 (VC p. 625)
children.translated_text: (6.31.1) 'He who arose, giving day and night, is <s>Pulastya</s>; dwelling near, [he holds] the whole by his radiance. I offer to that <s>Ṛṣi</s>; may he protect us with shelter, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.31.2) '<s>Pulastya</s>, from joy, came to the lake crying; protecting with love, the second bears that. His constant nearness — may it guard [us], <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.31.3) 'Let this be the priestly draught — he who is your body, the chief one, the first, desiring the glory of rites — the oblations that he offered — let this one go forth, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.31.4) 'Those who, streaming forth, were born, who fall also on the sun's path — the thread then, to him I sacrifice, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.31.5) 'He who is our <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, born equally — whose all this remainder he crossed. To him I sacrifice, the Lord, the sage — this indeed, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.31.6) 'The seven supreme sages, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> — with nourishment to those, for he is well-born from them. From him eternally [this] arose, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.31.7) 'He who, without malice, the Lord, establishing the unseen, rose and protected the shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>. May this one be the maker of his lineage, his lineage, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.31.8) 'He who grew from the directions — <s>Atri</s>, the king. To him, of that, this oblation — may <s>Soma</s> grant [his favor], <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 6.0.9 samyág u tarpayā́mi svā́hā na hí(g)ṃsī svā́hā juhomi svā́hā hotus svā́hā idán tu svā́hā ṣaṭ ca
children.translated_text: (6.0.9) [Rubric:] '...I properly satisfy, <s>svāhā</s>; ...do not harm, <s>svāhā</s>; ...I offer, <s>svāhā</s>; ...of the <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; ...this indeed, <s>svāhā</s>' — and six [mantras].

children.text:
6.32.1 sa eko 'bhū́d divā́-niśaṃ nas sáñcāri-bhavódbhavaḥ
sraṣṭús sr̥ṣṭéś ca sáñcita svā́hā
6.32.2 yas traíṣṭubhaś cā́gra imá(g)ṃ sisr̥kṣus sásmāra sārvaṃ mánasā makheṣṭā
puṣpáṃ vimānáṃ vibúdhasya hetus svā́hā
6.32.3 prakramyā́tha ū́rdhvaṃ púruṣa-jo vivéśa prájāsu vr̥tyā́ya ásun dadāti
so 'ham asmín yájāni sámāpātu svā́hā
6.32.4 yó mātaríśvā víyaj-jātó 'ṃśako vr̥to hūyáte
yásya satá(g)ṃ sametu svā́hā
6.32.5 vŕ̥ṣākaper[*432] ihá úpoṣa-vr̥ttyā́[*433] yám ādattá déva āste
tásyābhám agne suhutá(g)ṃ harasva svā́hā
[*432] cf. RV 10.86.2; AV 20.126.2 (VC p. 900)
[*433] 1984, 1946 editions: -vr̥tyā; 1926 edition: -vr̥ttyā
children.translated_text: (6.32.1) 'He, the one, existed day and night — the source of wandering existence for us, the collected [essence] of the creator and creation, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.32.2) 'He who, in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [metre], foremost, wishing to create this, remembered all with his mind, the seeker of sacrifice — the flower-temple, the cause of the wise one, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.32.3) 'Having stridden forth upward, the one born of <s>Puruṣa</s> entered. He gives life-breaths to creatures for their sustenance. I sacrifice to him in this; may he fully protect [us], <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.32.4) 'He who is <s>Mātariśvan</s>, born of sacrifice, the allotted one, is invoked — whose hundred [blessings], may they come together, <s>svāhā</s>!' (6.32.5) 'Of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, here, with the subsistence of fasting — whom the god took and is established — of his, O <s>Agni</s>, accept the well-offered oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
6.33.1 ojo-íbhimānī́ nídadhāra víśvaṃ trí-kośa-gair yád daśábhir yad agré
jātébhya ebhyás sa-hávo yajāni svā́hā
6.33.2 ā́po víśvan dadhāty ásūn divó dadhé 'dhaś cá kháṃ caran
cátuś-śr̥ṅgiṇa étu hótu svā́hā
6.33.3 cā́turyam[*434] asmín dádhati prajās tā́ḥ
cā́tur-guṇānā́m áta adbhya etát svā́hā
6.33.4 táyādityā́ nírviśanti bhū́tā víśve guṇānā́ṃ havíṣo vahantyā́
várāṃbarāyā́[*435] súhutan nidhattā(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.33.5 tat trīṇy[*436] eṣā́ dhárate sarvam arvā́g yā́m āyāntás sūráyo dyā́ṃ vrajantaḥ
tasyā́ agnā́v únnīyante juhomi svā́hā
[*434] caturyam= dexterity (MW p. 392)
[*435] 1946 edition: párāṃbarāyā́
[*436] 1984, 1946 editions: tatrīṇy; 1926 edition: tat trīṇy
6.0.10 harasva svā́hā juhomi svā́hā
children.translated_text: Take away, <s>svāhā</s>! I offer oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.34.1 pāvakā́ nas sárasvatī vā́jebhir vājínīvatī
yajñáṃ vaṣṭu dhiyā́vasus svā́hā
6.34.2 mahó árṇas sárasvatī prá cetayati ketúnā
dhíyo víśvā ví rājati svā́hā
6.34.3 śa(g)ṃ sā́niyaccháty[*437] ániśaṃ naḥ pavitrī́ yáyā sva-rā́jā sáṃvirājo virājáḥ
séhā hrāse púṣṭi-vardhane dhattā(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.34.4 bhūyá ā́tma-vr̥ttyā́[*438] bála-tejo-jananyā́ devópavāhyā́ mánasā yayā́sánn
dākṣāyaṇyā́ dhanyaí yajeya(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.34.5 yá úttámó mū́rtímáto 'dhidhāmā́
śréṣṭhārpitaṃ tvā́hur ato yajāni svā́hā
[*437] 1984 edition: sā́niyaścháty
[*438] 1926 edition: vr̥ttyā; 1946, 1984 eds.: vr̥tyā
children.translated_text:
May purifying <s>Sarasvatī</s>, rich in prizes, abounding in nourishment,
desire our sacrifice, she who is rich in thought, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Sarasvatī</s>, of the great flood, awakens [us] with her beacon;
she illumines all thoughts, <s>svāhā</s>!
She who constantly bestows auspiciousness upon us, the purifier, through whom the self-sovereign [shines forth] among the resplendent <s>Virāj</s> powers,
may she establish [the oblation] here, in waning and in increase of nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>!
Again, through self-sustaining activity, she who gives birth to strength and radiance, conveyed by the <s>devas</s> (gods), by whose mind [all] existed,
to the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, the blessed one, I would worship, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who is the highest abode among embodied beings,
they call you the one established in the most excellent — therefore I worship, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.35.1 agnéḥ pathā[*439] yáṃ práviśanti bhā́bhih
havī́(g)ṃṣi tasmā́ abhíto dadhātu svā́hā
6.35.2 yám arpáyanty átra kalā[*440] nidhāné diśā́sv ādityáḥ pítaro 'paras yā́ḥ
r̥kṣā nr̥̄ṇā́ṃ samprásaras sudhā́ṃ tásmai marīcaye súhutan nidhattā(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.35.3 yás saṃharaty éṣa sr̥jaty ahar náḥ
nénekti sañjī́vati[*441] mā́ nametā(g)ṃ svā́hā
6.35.4 ŕ̥cām adhīśó vísr̥jaṃś catásraḥ
prájāh prajéśo rámate rathé 'sya svā́hā
6.35.5 nī́tāṃ dhr̥tíṃ cétasi tāsu nityám
prajā́sv anáparo bibharti svā́hā
6.35.6 yéneṣṭe rása agra agrim ā́sate
áṃbhasi tásya havír juhomi svā́hā
6.35.7 samūhyate 'mbā́ sahá saptalokā́ḥ
dívi sthitā yé ca dharā́dharé ca bhūs svā́hā
6.35.8 cáruṃ paced yás sahá sapta-loké
rákṣā́(g)ṃsi rakṣánn ihá jīva-loké svā́hā
6.35.9 culyā́(g)ṃ haví rakṣan pácanaṃ bibharti
tásmai yaja īśā́ya bubhúkṣitāya svā́hā
[*439] 1984 edition: padhā; 1946 edition: pathā
[*440] Text: kaḷā
[*441] 1926 edition: sañjī́vati; 1946, 1984 eds.: sañjī́vatī
children.translated_text:
By the path of <s>Agni</s>, which they enter with splendor,
may he place the oblations all around, <s>svāhā</s>!
Those whom they direct there, an art-portion, in the repository, in the directions; <s>Āditya</s>, the ancestors, the further ones,
the <s>ṛkṣā</s> (bear-constellation), the rivers of men, the nectar — to that <s>Marīci</s>, may the well-offered oblation be placed, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who gathers and he who releases day for us,
he purifies and revives — may he incline toward us, <s>svāhā</s>!
The lord of the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, releasing the four [directions],
the lord of offspring — he delights in his chariot, <s>svāhā</s>!
The guided one, the steadfast one, constantly in the mind among those [devotees],
among offspring, the unsurpassed one sustains [all], <s>svāhā</s>!
By whom the essence is foremost among the foremost,
in the waters I offer his oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!
The Mother gathers together the seven worlds;
those established in heaven and those below in the underworld, <s>svāhā</s>!
May one who cooks the oblation in the seven worlds,
protecting what is to be protected here in the world of the living, <s>svāhā</s>!
In the hearth, protecting the oblation, bearing the cooking,
to him I worship, to the Lord who hungers, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 6.0.11 yajāni svā́ḥā bibharti svā́hāṣtáu ca
children.translated_text: I worship, <s>svāhā</s>! He sustains, <s>svāhā</s>! And [these are] eight.

children.text:
6.36.1 catur-mukhī́ loká-ramī ca kuṇḍínī
devī́ vívartínī virájo vidhātus svā́hā
6.36.2 yó loka-bhartrī́ rámatā prajā́nām
jātā́bhis sárvaṃ mánasā priyā́bhis svā́hā
6.36.3 tri-nétra-dhārī́ tápaso-dhi-devī́
víśveṣu devéṣu gáṇeṣu mukhyā svā́hā
6.36.4 cíhnaṃ ca raudráṃ dadhatī gaṇa-mukhyā́
bhasmā́ṅga-dhautī́ gaṇá-kāla-hāriṇī svā́hā
6.36.5 jvālā mālā́[*442] gumbhínī guha-jātā́
raudráṃ gaṇaṃ yā́ bíbhr̥yāt surūpī svā́hā
[*442] cf. TA 10.11.2 (VC p. 385)
children.translated_text:
The four-faced one, delighting in the worlds, the bearer of the <s>kuṇḍa</s> (fire-pit),
the goddess revolving, the <s>Virāj</s> of <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Creator), <s>svāhā</s>!
He who is the sustainer of the worlds, the delight of offspring,
with all those born, with the beloved ones, by mind, <s>svāhā</s>!
The three-eyed bearer, the goddess of austerity and meditation,
foremost among all <s>devas</s> (gods) and <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants), <s>svāhā</s>!
Bearing the fierce mark of <s>Rudra</s>, chief of the <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants),
bathed in ashes, destroyer of the <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants) of death, <s>svāhā</s>!
Garlanded with flames, clustered, born in the cave,
she who would bear the fierce <s>gaṇa</s> (host), the beautiful one, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.37.1 bālā́n harī rakṣíṇī śr̥ṅgi-patrī́
ákṣeṣu śaktíṣu marī́ci-ramī́ ca devī́ svā́hā
6.37.2 yuge-yúge sámparirakṣitā́ ca
strī́ rūpa-dhārī́ púruṣasya cāriṇī svā́hā
6.37.3 sárvaṃ ramā rákṣíṇī loka-dhātrī́
viśváṅ gaṇai rákṣitā yā́s tu bhū́tyai svā́hā
6.37.4 kálpeṣu kalpéṣu súsaṃplaveṣu
alpī́ bhavitrī́ sahá goṣu bhūṣu svā́hā
6.37.5 ánteṣu ghoréṣu vā́rāha-lolā́
mándhī[*443] karṣī kŕ̥ṣṭa-mukhī́ ca devī́ svā́hā
6.37.6 sā́ sarva-devéṣu márud-gaṇeṣu
sámbhāvitā yā́ trí-daśādhipā́ ca svā́hā
6.37.7 mālā-dharī yā́ trí-daśādhipā́ ca
sándhyā daśī sá(g)ṃhita-sapta-dhātús svā́hā
6.37.8 caṇḍī́ harī bhī́ṣáṇī rudra-rūpī́ dhātrī́ dharitrī rasá-hārī ca loké
śūlī́ jaṭī mukta-keśī vikeśī svā́hā
6.37.9 mohī́ vimohī́ vimúhī guha-dhā́riṇī ca
nídrā ca devī́ vírajās tu bhū́tyai svā́hā
[*443] 1926 edition: mánthī
children.translated_text:
Protectress of children, the tawny one, with horned leaves,
among the rays and powers, the radiant one, the delightful goddess, <s>svāhā</s>!
In age after age, well-protected,
the woman bearing form, the consort of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Cosmic Person), <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), protectress of all, sustainer of the worlds,
protected with all <s>gaṇas</s> (hosts) for prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>!
In <s>kalpa</s> after <s>kalpa</s> (aeon after aeon), during the great dissolutions,
she becomes subtle, together with the cows and the earth, <s>svāhā</s>!
In the terrible ends [of creation], playful as a boar,
the slow one, the dark-eared one, the goddess with a playful face, <s>svāhā</s>!
She who is honored among all <s>devas</s> (gods), among the <s>Marut</s>-hosts,
the revered one, she who is the ruler of the thirty [gods], <s>svāhā</s>!
She who bears garlands, the ruler of the thirty [gods],
<s>Sandhyā</s> (Twilight), the tenth, composed of the seven constituents, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Caṇḍī</s> (the Fierce), the tawny one, the terrifying one, of <s>Rudra</s>-form, the nourisher, the sustainer, the essence-bearer in the world,
the trident-bearer, the matted-haired one, the loose-haired one, the disheveled one, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Mohī</s> (the Deluder), <s>Vimohī</s> (the Bewilderer), <s>Vimuhī</s> (the Confuser), the bearer of the cave,
and <s>Nidrā</s> (Sleep) the goddess — may the <s>Virāj</s> powers [bring] prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 6.0.12 surūpī svā́hā devī́ svā́hāṣṭáu ca
children.translated_text: To the beautiful one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the goddess, <s>svāhā</s>! And [these are] eight.

children.text:
6.38.1 dhātā́sya víśvaṃ hí bíbharti yo vaí
púṣpāṇi rakṣánn ihá jīva-loké svā́hā
6.38.2 phullā́n hi yó rakṣati vr̥kṣa-ṣaṇḍā́n
víśvaṃ sr̥jaty éṣa vidhā́ya tásmai svā́hā
6.38.3 víśvān balí-rakṣita-sarva-devā́n
tásmād bálí(g)ṃ rakṣatu bhū́taye svā́hā
6.38.4 saúrya-hitá ī́śa pathābhirakṣánn
víśvān balé no 'bhiharán vidheya svā́hā
6.38.5 ā́gneyó yásmād yájāmahe tvā́ víśve sadā tváṃ máhito nu śámbho
vaírājan te suhútan nídhattā(g)ṃ svā́hā
children.translated_text:
<s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator) of this [universe] indeed sustains all,
protecting the flowers here in the world of the living, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who protects the blossoming groves and thickets of trees,
he creates all by his ordinance — to him, <s>svāhā</s>!
All <s>devas</s> (gods), protected by the <s>bali</s> (food-offering),
therefore may the <s>bali</s> (offering) protect for prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>!
O Lord, established for the benefit of the sun, protecting along the path,
all [offerings] in the <s>bali</s> — may one bring [them] to us, may it be so ordained, <s>svāhā</s>!
Since from <s>Agni</s> we worship you, O <s>Śambhu</s> (the Auspicious One), all [gods] always honor you greatly;
to the <s>Vairāja</s>, may the well-offered oblation be placed, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.39.1 praíṣām adhīśó víbudhānām anādíḥ
yā́ me śastā́ṃ dhánitān dadhātu svā́hā
6.39.2 śatá-dhāra(g)ṃ hiraṇmáya(g)ṃ sómo 'gham āsté járad udvahán naḥ
víśvaṃ nó nú dadāt sadaína(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.39.3 kadā́pí sr̥jate prajā́ ávigiraty ayán no gopāyatí naḥ
yajāmahe vípāpmā́ bhūyāma járato 'griyāya svā́hā
6.39.4 dhármaugha-mātā́ vídadhe samástam
dháran dhariṣyate sáha saptama(gg)ṃ svā́hā
6.39.5 yógan dháraṃ nu prásuva(g)ṃs tu jántū́n
júgopa gopa-gárbhaṃ surādis svā́hā
children.translated_text:
The lord of desires, the foremost of the wise ones, the beginningless one,
may he who is praised place riches for me, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Soma</s>, of hundred streams, golden, sits [in the vessel]; bearing away sin, carrying us forward,
may he give us all constantly, <s>svāhā</s>!
At some time he releases offspring; this one does not devour; he protects us;
we worship — may we become sinless, foremost among those who age, <s>svāhā</s>!
The mother of the flood of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) established all together;
sustaining, she is sustained, together with the seventh, <s>svāhā</s>!
The one who maintains <s>yoga</s> (union) and indeed brings forth creatures,
protected the embryo of the cowherd, the foremost of the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.40.1 yám arpáyanti múnayo havír yó 'jo 'hijānír víbudhā virā́jánn
táṃ mayi doṣā́ yásyānanāgnaú vípināni patantu svā́hā
6.40.2 śáṃ no nídhattāṃ tápaso jíhartām
svayambhúr ágre mŕ̥taye 'mŕ̥tāya svā́hā
6.40.3 bhū́mān anto 'gré bhúvanasya goptā́ vāmábhya ī́śanty amárā márāś ca
kurvate 'gnaú súhutáṅ ghr̥tena svā́hā
6.40.4 vándyo na eṣá vasúṣu nidadhyā́t
tri-dhā́ tri-dhāmā́ bíbhr̥yād adīnānth svā́hā
6.40.5 ā́sāgra agré súhutāñ jitaítā́n
ŕ̥ṣīn avāpyógra íto jayāya svā́hā
children.translated_text:
That which the sages offer as oblation, he who is unborn, the serpent-born, the wise one, shining as <s>Virāj</s>,
may the faults in me — may they fall into the sinless fire, <s>svāhā</s>!
May he place auspiciousness for us, may he take away [the fruits] of <s>tapas</s> (austerity),
the Self-existent one, first, for death and for immortality, <s>svāhā</s>!
The abundant ones, the protector of the world at the end and beginning, the desirable ones — both immortals and mortals rule;
they make well-offered oblations in the fire with ghee, <s>svāhā</s>!
May this praiseworthy one establish us among treasures;
may the triple-aboded one sustain those who are not weak, <s>svāhā</s>!
At the foremost of the forefront, the well-offered and ever-victorious ones,
the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), having attained — foremost, for victory, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
6.41.1 ójo-bálāyāsy ámr̥tāya śambhó
pácasy ayo no 'pácayan na hi(g)ṃsī svā́hā
6.41.2 tán mā yaśo 'gré tā́vake vasū́nāṃ yájāmahe syā́d bhávataḥ prasánnaḥ
tádā vadaty úttama-gaṃ jayán te svā́hā
6.41.3 asmād upāsyó sy éhi hi
vr̥ddhi śarma bhávatodarā́t[*444] svā́hā
6.41.4 bhūtā́nām ágraṇyam aháṃ juhomi bhūtā́nām ī́śaṃ bhúvanasya gopám
bhūtā́nāṃ pátim átyúgra-vīryaṃ bhūtā́nāṃ pátaye námas svā́hā
6.41.5 bhūtó bhūtéṣu carati práviṣṭas sá bhūtā́nām ádhipatir babhūva
6.41.6 sárveṣāṃ bhūtā́nāṃ ádhipatis tásmai víṣṇu-bhūtākṣa-hantā́ya svā́hā
6.41.7 ákṣa-hante níhitās sahāyā́ḥ
sárveṣāṃ prāṇínā(g)ṃ śā́ntaye svā́hā
6.41.8 yé bhūtā́ḥ pracáranti dívā náktaṃ bálim icchánto vitúdasya préṣyāḥ
tébhyo balíṃ puṣṭi-kā́mo harāmi máyi púṣṭíṃ púṣṭi-patir dadhātu svā́hā
[*444] 1926, 1946 editions: bhávatodarā́t; 1984 edition: bhávatodharā́t
children.translated_text:
For vigor and strength, for immortality, O <s>Śambhu</s> (Auspicious One),
you cook for us what is uncooked — you do not harm, <s>svāhā</s>!
May that glory of mine, foremost among your treasures — we worship; may the propitiated one be pleased;
then he proclaims the highest song of your victory, <s>svāhā</s>!
From this, you are to be worshipped — come indeed,
may growth and protection come from your belly, <s>svāhā</s>!
I offer oblation to the foremost of beings, to the lord of beings, the protector of the world,
to the lord of beings of exceedingly fierce power — homage to the lord of beings, <s>svāhā</s>!
The existing one moves among beings, having entered; he became the overlord of beings;
The overlord of all beings — to him, the destroyer of the evil-eyed one, allied with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
To the destroyer of the evil-eyed, the allies are established;
for the pacification of all living beings, <s>svāhā</s>!
Those <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits) who roam about by day and by night, seeking <s>bali</s> (food-offerings), messengers of <s>Vituda</s>,
to them I carry the <s>bali</s>, desiring nourishment — may the lord of nourishment grant me nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 6.0.13 nídhattā(g)ṃ svā́hā surādis svā́hā jayāya svā́hākṣa-hantā́ya svā́hā catvā́ri ca
children.translated_text: May [the oblation] be placed, <s>svāhā</s>! To the foremost of gods, <s>svāhā</s>! For victory, <s>svāhā</s>! To the destroyer of the evil-eyed, <s>svāhā</s>! And [these are] four.

children.text: 6.42.1 áto devā́ idáṃ víṣṇus trī́ṇi padā́ víṣṇoḥ kármāṇi tád víṣṇoḥ paramáṃ padáṃ tad víprāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>devas</s> (gods) [worship] this <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the three strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that the wise ones [behold].

children.text:
6.0.14 cákṣur ā́tata(gg)ṃ svā́hā dvé ca[*445]
[*445] 1984 edition omits this verse
children.translated_text: (6.0.14) [Catch-words:] 'The eye extended,' <s>svāhā</s>; and two. [Editorial note: 1984 edition omits this verse.]

children.text:
6.0.14 áto devā́s sahásra-śīrṣā híraṇya-varṇāṃ bhū́mir bhūmnā́ svastí caívá trātā́ram índram údutyáṃ jágan naṃdíny ā sa ekaḥ pāvakā́ naś catur-mukhī́ dātā́ íto devā́ś cátur-daśa[*446]
[*446] 1946 edition omits this verse
children.translated_text: (6.0.14) [Catch-words:] 'Henceforth the gods...' 'The thousand-headed...' 'Golden-colored...' 'The earth, with [its] vastness...' 'Auspiciousness indeed...' 'The protector <s>Indra</s>...' 'Rising up...' '<s>Jagat</s>...' '<s>Nandinī</s>...' 'He, the one...' 'The purifiers, our...' 'The four-faced...' 'The giver...' 'Henceforth the gods...' — fourteen [mantras]. [Editorial note: 1946 edition omits this verse.]

children.text:
6.0.15[*447] áto devā́ svasti caivodutyáṃ yá eṣó ójo bálāya dví-catvāri(g)ṃśat[*448]
[*447] 42 in book
[*448] 1946 edition omits this verse
children.translated_text: (6.0.15) [Catch-words:] 'Henceforth the gods...' 'Auspiciousness indeed...' 'Rising up...' 'He who is this...' 'Strength, for power...' — forty-two [mantras]. [Editorial note: 42 in book. 1946 edition omits this verse.]

children.text:
[Colophon:]
áto devā́s tad víprāsaḥ
háriḥ oṃ
tatth sat
children.translated_text: [Colophon:] 'Henceforth the gods...' 'Thus the inspired ones...' <s>Hariḥ Oṃ</s>. That is truth.

children.text:
Śrī Śrī vikhanasa mahā-gurave namaḥ
Śrī-vaikhānasa-mantra-praśnāṣṭake
Saptama-praśna-prārambhaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to the great preceptor of the Śrī <s>Vaikhānasa</s> [school]. In the collection of eight <s>praśnas</s> (sections) of the Śrī <s>Vaikhānasa Mantra</s>, the beginning of the Seventh <s>Praśna</s>.

children.text:
hariḥ oṃ[*449]
7.1.1.1[*450] [1.1] víṣṇus sárveṣām ádhipatiḥ paramáḥ purāṇáḥ
paró lokā́nām ájito 'jitātmán[*451] bhávate 'bhavāya[*452] svā́hā
7.1.1.2 [1.2] sú-sū́kṣmas sā́rvas[*453] sárveṣām antarātmā́ tásthus tásthusāṃ jáṃgámo jaṃgamānā́m vibhur vibhū́ṇāṃ vibhavódbhavāya svā́hā
7.1.1.3 [1.3] jyótir vā́ pā́ramātmikaṃ sā́rvaṃ víśva-bhavám bhavāya
prábhūtaṃ[*454] prāhiṇván páramparāya súkr̥taṃ kr̥tāya tásmai várāyá[*455] ī́śiṣe svā́hā
7.1.1.4 [1.4] īśó yásmād vítataṃ vitatyá káṃ kaṃ[*456] dhr̥táṃ kā́ma-hutó juhoti
kákúdaṅ kakuc chitvā́ bhū́yaḥ parāya svā́hā
7.1.1.5 [1.5] rāyā́m īśó 'ráhita[*457] ābharantyā́[*458] rā́ṃ rāṃ váhantyām ahítaḥ[*459]
rāyā́ṃ patiṃ rā́ṃ rā́ṃ dhárate dharitryai rā́ṃ váhatodvahāya svā́hā
[*449] pā́rámā́tmíkópáníṣád íti prásíddhám pā́rā́yáṇé námóntáḥ hómé svā́hā́ntá ítí
[*450] VMP 7.1 tends to follow Bhaṭṭa-bhāskara.
[*451] US jitātman
[*452] US bhavāya
[*453] US has the normal visarga before an initial `s' of the following word, thus: sārvaḥ.
[*454] US prābhūtaṃ
[*455] US parāya
[*456] US omits second kam
[*457] US rahito
[*458] US bharantyai
[*459] US vahantyāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: (7.1.1.1) <s>Hariḥ Oṃ</s>. <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of all, supreme, ancient, beyond the worlds, unconquered — O unconquered self, for becoming and for the cessation of becoming, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.1.2) Most subtle, all-pervading, the inner self of all — the stationary among the stationary, the moving among the moving, the all-pervading among the all-pervading — for the arising of [all] manifestation, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.1.3) The light that is of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), universal, the source of all existence, for becoming — sending forth abundantly in succession the well-performed to the doer — to that excellent Lord, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.1.4) The Lord, from whom all this is extended and pervaded, who, holding each and every [being], offers as one whose desire is the oblation — cutting peak after peak, [leading] again to the beyond, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.1.5) The Lord of wealth, placed in her who brings wealth; bearing forth wealth in her who carries — the lord of wealth upholds wealth upon wealth for the earth — for the uplifting, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: extensive variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha (US) and Bhaṭṭa-bhāskara editions throughout.]
