children.translated_text: (7.1.2.1) He who is the <s>Brahma</s>-word, the <s>Praṇava</s> (sacred syllable <s>Oṃ</s>), the primordial sound, the inner self of all words, eternal, released, spreading freely — performing the work of <s>Prajāpati</s>, spreading abundantly, moving for the sake of the moving — for greater prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.2.2) He who is the supreme <s>Tri-mūrti</s> (three-formed), the highest and beyond — enjoying the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), he creates the whole; threefold, of three natures, in three ways — he arranged the whole, of threefold form — for the supporter of all, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.2.3) That which is accomplished, immortal among the moving, that which is the ultimate foundation of all, the undying, the complete — that which, while being perceived, the self enjoys within — for the one who cannot be reached through [mere] deep sleep, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.2.4) Who, having skillfully fashioned the sheath in the body, intentionally makes this foremost, most beautiful — for the hump-bearing one, moving at will among the moving, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.2.5) Whom the sages worship with sacrifices, whom the gods [regard as] the supremely pure — the foremost ones who shall bow down in times of distress, whom the wise recite, whom the <s>yogins</s> see with subtle, excellent visions — for the Lord, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha throughout.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.3.1) He who is the foremost, supreme, principal — the goal whose being was truth, whose superiority the sages perceive — to that chief <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.3.2) He who as <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), twofold, is the inner self of all, moving within all things here — O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, you who revive the gods, men, and the slain, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.3.3) You are <s>Agni</s> (fire), threefold, the greatest, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme light — for the protection of all, you shall carry the offered immortal [substance], <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.3.4) You are the life-force (<s>jīva</s>), you are the waters — the begetter of all, you are nourishment — O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, fourfold, for the removal of fatigue, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.3.5) Extending the crevices of the earth, the principal one, growing ever greater with five serene qualities of his own — you shall support all these, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.4.1) Having become mind, foremost before the existent — that which is born from you, you shall bring forth for all bodies — worthy of worship for the worthy, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.4.2) You are the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), the inner self of beings, clinging to the meritorious among the meritorious — you, discerning with intellect — for the one of meritorious form, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.4.3) He who, moving among the subtle beings, characterized by states of being and non-being, making [things] fit and unfit — the immeasurable one shakes off his own [burden] — for the one who bears the yoke, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.4.4) He out of fear of whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> Sun himself arose, carrying the true course of time — from whom, having made [the Sun's] own splendor, he shall protect all of us, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.4.5) You whom all [revere] as overcome for the sake of protection — all the gods see [you] and move about — those gods, you yourself are all of them — all is <s>māyā</s> (illusion), this <s>māyā</s> is yours, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: extensive variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.5.1) You who, having become <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god), [dwelling] in the void of destruction, drawn by creatures, shall gladden [them], protecting the true course of time with a vow, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.5.2) Having become <s>Kāma</s> (desire), situated among creatures, gladdening all the worlds while living — for the delight of <s>Hari</s>, the excellent one, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.5.3) You who entered limb by limb into all the worlds for their protection — he who is the god <s>Mātariśvā</s> (the Wind), dwelling [within] — may he be for our prosperity and well-being, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.5.4) He who, deluding, [serves] for the creation and protection of beings — he who is contraction, for the sake of contraction, may it be so, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.5.5) He who, the twelve-fold self, touching above — the light of the gods, the highest of lights — himself touching — for the light, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.translated_text: 7.1.6.1 [3.6] He who would be <s>Brahman</s>, the Self of those who know <s>Brahman</s>, the Self of those whose vision is the <s>Ātman</s> — prosperity of the prosperous, the good deed for the accomplished one, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.6.2 [3.7] He is indeed the <s>Sārasvata</s> god, or the fearless one, of supreme-self nature; whether fear or fearsome — he unites all, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.6.3 [3.8] He who unites the supreme light with the supreme — the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self) who will generate the <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.6.4 [3.9] He who is the cup, the four, the fourth, [who encompasses] the four categories of meaning — uniting all of the world, bestowing being upon the existent, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.6.5 [3.10] Whose are these <s>Brahman</s>-forms of the great <s>Brahman</s>, who bestows <s>Brahman</s> — who [acts] for the protection of <s>Brahman</s>, for the succession, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 500-508: Variant readings from US (Upaniṣad-saṅgraha) for each verse.]

children.translated_text: 7.1.7.1 [4.1] Speech indeed, the following utterance, delighting in speech upon speech — for the protection of what belongs to the gods, self-luminous, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.7.2 [4.2] These two birds, one motionless and one moving — he does not shake off the yoke; the one who alone enjoys, for the enjoyer, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.7.3 [4.3] He who is life itself, the <s>Paramātmā</s>, of the bountiful one, from succession the highest, the supreme refuge, beyond the worlds, bestowing the highest — from beyond, for the beyond, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.7.4 [4.4] He who is splendor, the splendor of splendors, bestowing splendor upon splendor — the true one, the splendor of splendors, splendor for splendor, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.7.5 [4.5] Together with me, that blessing which I have blessed, the blessing that was of past and future — blessing upon blessing, we have experienced, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 509-520: Extensive variant readings from US for each verse.]

children.translated_text: 7.1.8.1 [4.6] He who delights in union, the kindler of kindlings — establishing union, the meritorious one of the meritorious, for merit, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.8.2 [4.7] A thousandfold indeed is the canopy he bestows upon us; a thousand blessings with their thousands — whose thousands are thus endowed, for the thousand-of-thousands, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.8.3 [4.8] Self-arrayed protections, the protection — being among beings, the abode of being; what was being among beings, being upon being — for him who bestows being, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.8.4 [4.9] Being alone was the pre-eminent one; what being protects both — that being, the proclaimer of being, for truth, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.8.5 [4.10] The light of being, the inner self of being, the exertion of truth, the true one of true action — truth was the canopy of being, for the truth of truth, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 521-536: Variant readings from US for each verse.]

children.translated_text: 7.1.9.1 [5.1] Truth was being, was merit; merit indeed is divine being, truth is <s>Ṛṣi</s>-born; truth and being — for the true path, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.9.2 [5.2] The exertion of truth, being as life-breath, the support of being, the binder of being — truth illuminating being, light — for light, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.9.3 [5.3] I have ruled over this desirable one, I have ruled over truth, ruling over rulers — that being of truth's form; for truth that unites, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.9.4 [5.4] The fire-churning stick indeed, the <s>āranda</s> (delighter), the encloser, the delighter — this one, crushing the crusher, delighter — for blessing, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.9.5 [5.5] That being indeed is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the exertion is <s>Sūrya</s>, the cow indeed entering <s>Viṣṇu</s> — uniting all with all, that universe — for <s>Viṣṇu</s> of universal form, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 537-558: Extensive variant readings from US for each verse.]

children.translated_text: 7.1.10.1 [5.6] That is <s>Bhūḥ</s>; that <s>Bhūḥ</s> — the one established on earth is of universal form; that <s>Bhūḥ</s> is the <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), enumerated. You are <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Suvaḥ</s>; you are <s>Bhūḥ</s>, you are <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, you are <s>Suvaḥ</s> — <s>Bhūḥ</s>, for becoming, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.10.2 [5.7] The waters indeed, water — the waters are the inner self; he who is the <s>Veda</s>, the support of the <s>Vedas</s>, the inner self of the <s>Vedas</s>, full of essence, enumerated by essence — he was essence upon essence, for essence, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.10.3 [5.8] The <s>Trayī</s> (triple <s>Veda</s>) indeed is desire, consisting of the <s>Trayī</s>, threefold in quality, threefold in nature; the <s>Trayī</s> indeed is light, of three qualities, of three-quality nature — for that threefold <s>Agni</s>, the three-qualified, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.10.4 [5.9] Two indeed are the chief ones, the chief supports, with happiness, with bliss — smiling, with smiling expanse, with bliss, the givers of bliss, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.1.10.5 [5.10] He alone is the one, with support, with foundation, yet without support — whom, whom, for what station he causes to fall, in the fallen, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 559-572: Variant readings from US for each verse.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.11.1) He himself the beginning, the inner self of all, the god — he himself released the playful [creation]; he who himself ascertained the world, ascertaining, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.11.2) He who, having himself created, protected by himself — following that expanse, the unmoving among the moving — himself playing, causing play, entering into another play, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.11.3) He who by his own power sustains all, who strikes down the sinful step by step — he upheld the most meritorious, of meritorious nature, the expanse of merit — to the god, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.11.4) The one earth, submerged in water — hearing her crying out, rushing toward [her] — himself becoming <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar), the excellent one, he lifted her up — to that god, the well-doer, the father, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.11.5) He who, while supporting with tusks, said to those supporting with tusks, 'Support with tusks!' — distributing them along the mountain-ridges with his own splendor — to that god, the boon-giver, the father, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: extensive variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.12.1) He who, wiping [clean] the stumbling <s>Pr̥thivī</s> (Earth), making her limbs immortal, placed her upon [his] thighs — to that greatest one, the boon-giver, the father, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.12.2) The sky-cow, desirous, filled with desire, red-blue, moving immortally — caressing her with tinkling bracelets — to that lord of creatures, the boon-giver, the father, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.12.3) O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you has encompassed all these born creatures; whatever desires we offer with oblations, may that be ours — may we be lords of riches, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.12.4) He who [bears] the yoke of yokes, the best of yokes among the yoke-bearers — O good yoke, you are the yoke, the yoke of yoke-bearers, you are the yoke — O yoke-limbed one, [grant] me you, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.12.5) He who indeed slew without aging the unaging one — that chief of <s>Daityas</s>, of immortal self-form — the well-hoofed among the hoofed, sounding somewhat — to that <s>Nr̥siṃha</s> (Man-Lion), the father who is lord of gods, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.13.1) The treasury of those who are treasuries of austerity — by austerity [giving] wealth, wealth, life, and limb — destroyer of the flood of calamities — seated among swords, at the pressing, for the impeller — to that lord of gods, maker of the host of gods, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.13.2) He who as <s>Nr̥siṃha</s> bears victory, radiant, wealth-giving to the wise — radiant, victorious, a thousandfold — to that one of good restraint, to the treasury of treasuries, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.13.3) Wealth, the humped one, providing for the lost — the arrangement endowed with wealth — to that humped one, the terrible one, the father, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.13.4) I invoke <s>Rākā</s> (the Full Moon), easy to invoke, with fair praise — may she, the auspicious one, hear us, may she know of herself; may she sew with an unbroken needle — may she give a hero, a hundredfold giver, worthy of praise, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.13.5) I know that great <s>Puruṣa</s>, sun-colored, beyond darkness — the wise one, having discerned all forms and having made names, when he sits, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.14.1) He whose directions are the faults and sub-directions are the ears, whose sky is the mouth, whose belly is the atmosphere — he who rules and himself attained [supreme] standing — to that best of reins, the boon-giver, to whom [else]? <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.14.2) Lotus-faced, [with lotus-]chest, the supreme, most meritorious — the lotus is his origin, supreme is his dwelling — the subtle one, placing himself for the impeller — the <s>Sāvitra</s> (Solar) form, supreme and most meritorious, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.14.3) He who is the lotus (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>), the supreme inner self, who bore the lotus that has become a lovely body — seated among swords, for the essence of essences, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.14.4) The lord of riches, the worshipful, the great, freed from attachment to wealth, the weighty preceptor, of fair visage — that form of wealth, the prosperity of all that has come into being — for the one endowed with wealth, for the protector, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.14.5) For the one with wings of wealth, who bestows wealth, whose wealth is great and well-nourished — radiant, may they sacrifice for delight — that image-bearing one, for the peak, the auspicious one, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: extensive variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.translated_text: (7.1.15.1) That which is the essence of the whole, the supporter — experienced and pervaded with the fullness of joy — the subtle lord of gods bears the whole — to that lord of gods, the whole, the most meritorious, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.15.2) He is indeed the fruit of the worlds, the ageless great self, who protects the universe, spotless, called the immaculate — to that humped one, the boon-giver, for nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.15.3) He who bears us as a yoke, delighting in delight — the prosperity of the earth within, the proper time, the most excellent — radiant, for the protection of all, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.15.4) He who bears the universe, the very powerful one, crying out — sovereign, the whole, well-grown — may he, having extended, send us forth upon a wing, <s>svāhā</s>! (7.1.15.5) He who is of his own form, equal-visioned, complete — shaking yet prosperous, establishing the footstep — in the sky, radiant, for the great, the worthy — that image-bearing one, equally giving, complete, <s>svāhā</s>! [Editorial notes: variant readings from Upaniṣadsaṅgraha.]

children.text:
7.1.16.1 [8.6] bhūr bhuvaṃ vá bhuvo vā́ suvar[*640] vā́ kíñcit svanántaṃ súṣuve samástam
sárvasya dātā́ram ajáraṃ janitre svā́hā

children.translated_text: (7.1.16.1) 'Earth, atmosphere, or heaven — whatever resounding [being] gave birth to all collectively, to the ageless giver of everything, to the progenitor, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.16.2) 'Having contracted the entire expanse spread forth in <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, dwelling together with me in the most excellent totality — to that Lord of Creatures (<s>Prajeśa</s>), the burden-bearer, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.16.3) 'All the directions, advancing and praising, those lotuses indeed in the river, all together — may he bestow nourishment upon me, or in my abode, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.16.4) 'He who bears the totality of moving beings, who is able to traverse all space — may he indeed nourish us in our lineage unceasingly, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.16.5) 'He who, from the ten directions, [gathers] the assembled forces, placing those good seeds at the proper time, transcending sound, [offering] his own strength for [cosmic] strength, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.translated_text: (7.1.17.1) 'The four night-watches proceed for him — to the protector of all, the one of sweet essence, the abode. For the sacred, wealth-increasing prosperity of <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.17.2) 'In his chest dwells the best of the best; placing speech, she has increased everything. To that most excellent one, for the growth of boons, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.17.3) 'Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great — the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is hidden in the cave of this creature. One who is free from sorrow sees that desireless Lord in his majesty, by the grace of <s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator), <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.17.4) '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the greatest, the foremost bestower of boons, who, being without universal fear, meditating and creating, established the universe as fearsome — that <s>mantra</s>, for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, for the powerful one, the immeasurable sustainer, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.17.5) 'The unborn ones, delighting, falling forth from their station, nurturing again and again, whoever speaks forth — to the progenitor of equal radiance, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.translated_text: (7.1.18.1) 'You bear me, the self-protected one, for prosperity — her, the radiant one, bearing the burden. You are the yoke, for the steadfast one, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.18.2) 'Those who contemplate him whose form is the end of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>Nigamānta</s>), whose form is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the sacred Supreme Self — they, finding [him], attain the whole. To that chief of the gods, the one delighting in good, for existence, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.18.3) 'The meritorious and sacred one, foremost in the <s>Puruṣa</s>, her, the radiant one, impelled by the treasure for us — he bestows the supreme nourishment, for the Supreme, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.18.4) 'May he who has become [our protector], whose self is immortal, distributing to us pure, excellent nourishment — may he be for our prosperity, for the boon of the lotus (<s>Kamalā</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.18.5) 'He alone is eternal — all his own forms are delightful and infinite. They conquered the calamity of the imperishable ones. To that very creator (<s>Savitṛ</s>), to <s>Hari</s>, the remover, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.translated_text: (7.1.19.1) 'Those cows, the most excellent, the powerful, dwelling in the sustaining earth, indeed auspicious with wealth here — licking, they shine like silver, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.19.2) '<s>Vāyu</s>, the inner self, carries everything — thus the very auspicious god, he the sage-liberated. The patron of the gods, of sweet essence, the life-giver — gathering together, to the god, the bestower of boons, to the father, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.19.3) 'Above all stands the <s>Ātman</s> (Self); above that, the Supreme, the liberated one. To that stainless one, of beautiful form, moving forth — for the hereafter, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.19.4) 'The most excellent one shook off the darkness of all beings, having illuminated the entire form of <s>Sattva</s> (truth). He who causes affliction for the purpose of creation — to that Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, to the Supreme Light, <s>svāhā</s>!' (7.1.19.5) 'Light, light, the light of lights, bringing vigor and strength — <s>Sattva</s> (truth), of the nature of truth, with its own light, as declared — to that most subtle of the subtle, to that radiance, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.translated_text: 7.1.20.1 [10.6] '<s>Sattva</s>, whose essence is <s>sattva</s>; <s>rajas</s>, whose essence is <s>rajas</s>; <s>tamas</s>, the support of <s>tamas</s> — the well-made, that Lord — to the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.20.2 [10.7] 'Unbroken, for whom this was — it was water-natured; whose [light] burns away harm, most high — to the Widely-praised One (<s>Urugāya</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.20.3 [10.8] 'By whose will in the world offspring would strive; he who holds the world as dweller — that was not [separate from him]; whatever has come into being, whatever is all — to the Lord, [you] who rule, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.20.4 [10.9] 'He who is the beginning of the <s>Vedas</s>, the supreme, the highest <s>Brahman</s>, whose measure is the triple [<s>Veda</s>], whose form is the triple [<s>Veda</s>] — sound, the origin of sound — to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, to the Supreme Light, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.20.5 [10.10] 'He who, through the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), wholly by his growth — whatever all this was — bearing [it] with bliss, well-made — to the Supreme, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 7.1.0.10 téjase svā́hā parāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.1.0.10 [Rubric:] 'To radiance (<s>tejas</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To the Supreme, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.translated_text: 7.1.21.1 [11.1] 'He who was indeed the prosperity of prosperity — she [too was] bliss in response to bliss; I go delighting together — truth, to Truth, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.21.2 [11.2] 'True, abiding in truth, dwelling in the world of truth — Truth was the origin. To the True of the true, to the swiftness, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.21.3 [11.3] 'Cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>), truth, immeasurable, ancient, the beginning, the origin, the immortal, the lord of the gods — delighting in those who possess light, may you delight, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.21.4 [11.4] 'Who bears the immortal — the streaked one, the guardian of immortality, delighting in <s>Soma</s>? He bears well-nourished wealth and virtue here — to that most meritorious, boon-granting Father, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.21.5 [11.5] 'Me, self-protected, of the form of the canopy of all truth, continuously delighting, the supreme, the most pure — self-sustaining, herself unwavering — to the Uniter, the boon-granting Father, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.1.0.11 [Rubric:] 'To the Father, <s>svāhā</s>!' — and two [more].
