[*740] Text: anmarātmā́
[*741] Text: prāhiṇván
children.translated_text: <s>Hariḥ Oṃ</s>. 7.2.1.1 [1.1] '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the overlord of all, the supreme, the ancient — beyond the worlds, unconquered, of conquered Self — to Being, to Non-being, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.1.2 [1.2] 'Most subtle, universal, the inner Self (<s>antarātman</s>) of all — the standing one of those that stand, the moving one of those that move — the all-pervading one of the all-pervading — to the source of all magnificence, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.1.3 [1.3] 'The light that is of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), universal, born of all — to existence; the abundant one, sending forth to the succession — well-accomplished, to the accomplished — to that best one, [you] who rule, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.1.4 [1.4] 'The Lord, from whom [all] is spread forth, having extended — whom, whom he sustains; the one offered in desire offers oblation — having cut through peak after peak, again to the Supreme, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.1.5 [1.5] 'Lord of wealth, freely bearing — to the one who carries wealth upon wealth, placed [in her] — the lord of wealth, she who sustains wealth upon wealth, the supporter — may she carry wealth to the Uplifter, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.2.1 [1.6] yó brahma-śabdáḥ práṇavaḥ pradhānáś śabdáś śábdāntarātmā́ nítyo viyattáḥ prátaran prakāmám
prājāpatyáṃ prátaraṃ prakurván bhūyó bhūtyaí acaráṃ carāya svā́hā
7.2.2.2 [1.7] yó vā trí-mūrtíḥ páramaḥ paraś cá trí-guṇaṃ juṣāṇás sákalaṃ vídatte
trís-tris tri-dhātmā́ tri-dhā́ tri-dhā́ vā vídadhe samástaṃ tri-dhā́ tri-rūpáṃ sákalaṃ-dharāya svā́hā
7.2.2.3 [1.8] yad vā́ kr̥tám amŕ̥taṃ cárāṇāṃ yát sarva-niṣṭhám ajáraṃ samastám
yát páśyamānam ātmā́bhijuṣāṇám ántas suṣuptyā́n[*742]abhígamyamānāya svā́hā
7.2.2.4 [1.9] kaḥ[*743] kośam aṅgé kúśalaṃ vidhāya sā́kr̥táṃ kr̥ṇvate 'grá idaṃ sukāntám
kákudvaté kā́ma-caráṃ carāya svā́hā
7.2.2.5 [1.10] yám yajñaír múnayo juṣánti yáṃ devā́ḥ páramaṃ pavítraṃ bhaviṣyánty ā́rtiṣu práṇatāḥ pradhānā́ḥ ya(g)ṃ sū́rayo japantó yóginás sū́kṣmais súpradarśanaiḥ páśyantīśvarāya svā́hā
[*742] VMP text 1984 edition: suṣuptyā́g. 1946 edition: suṣuptyā́n.
[*743] Text: kaṃ
children.translated_text: 7.2.2.1 [1.6] 'He who is the <s>Brahma</s>-sound, the <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>), the chief sound, the inner Self of sound, eternal, pervading, extending further and further at will — effecting the creation of <s>Prajāpati</s> further and further, again for prosperity — the immovable to the movable, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.2.2 [1.7] 'He who is the three-formed one (<s>Trimūrti</s>), the supreme and beyond — delighting in the three <s>guṇas</s>, he perceives all. Thrice-thrice, the threefold Self — threefold and threefold — he established the totality, threefold, three-formed — to the bearer of all, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.2.3 [1.8] 'That which is accomplished, the immortal of the moving ones; that which is the ultimate abode, the ageless, the totality — that which, being seen, delighting in the Self — to the one approached within through deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.2.4 [1.9] 'Who, having skillfully fashioned the sheath (<s>kośa</s>) in the body, makes it well-made — this beautiful [creation] in the beginning — to the hump-bearing one, moving at will, to the movable, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.2.5 [1.10] 'Him whom sages worship with sacrifices, whom the gods [regard as] the supremely pure — the foremost ones who shall bow in affliction — whom the wise ones and <s>yogins</s> see, muttering, with subtle and beautiful visions — to the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 7.2.0.1 ud vahāya svā́heśvarā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.0.1 [Rubric:] 'To the Uplifter, <s>svāhā</s>! To the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.3.1 [2.1] yó vā gáviṣṭhaḥ páramaḥ pradhānáḥ padáṃ vā yásya satvám āsīt
yásyopáritvaṃ múnayo 'núpaśyanti tásmai mukhyā́ya víṣṇave svā́hā
7.2.3.2 [2.2] yó vā vā́yur dví-guṇo 'ntarātmā́ sárveṣām antáś caratīhá víṣṇo
sa tváṃ devā́n manuṣyān mr̥tān párisaṃjīvase svā́hā
7.2.3.3 [2.3] tvám agne trí-guṇo variṣṭháḥ paraṃ brahma páraṃ jyótiḥ
sárveṣāṃ tváṃ pā́lanāya hutám amŕ̥taṃ vahiṣyaṣe svā́hā
7.2.3.4 [2.4] tváṃ[*744] jī́vas tvám ā́pas sárveṣāṃ jánitā́ tvam ā́hāraḥ
tváṃ víṣṇo śramā́pánudāya cátur-guṇāya svā́hā
7.2.3.5 [2.5] bhū́mer vítanván prátaran prakāmáḥ pópūyamānáḥ
pañcábhis svá-guṇaiḥ prasannaís sárvāṇi mā́n dhārayiṣyasi svā́hā
[*744] 1946 edition: taṃ
children.translated_text: 7.2.3.1 [2.1] 'He who is most desirous of speech, the supreme, the chief — whose step was <s>sattva</s> (truth/being) — whose supremacy the sages behold — to that foremost <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.3.2 [2.2] 'He who as <s>Vāyu</s>, the two-<s>guṇa</s> one, the inner Self, moves within all here, O <s>Viṣṇu</s> — you yourself revive the gods, humans, and the dead, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.3.3 [2.3] 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, the three-<s>guṇa</s> one, the most excellent — the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Light — you shall carry the offered immortal [oblation] for the protection of all, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.3.4 [2.4] 'You are life (<s>jīva</s>), you are the waters, the begetter of all, you are nourishment — to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, remover of fatigue, the four-<s>guṇa</s> one, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.3.5 [2.5] 'Extending from the earth, spreading further at will, being purified — with five own <s>guṇas</s>, serene — you will sustain all beings, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.4.1 [2.6] mánas tváṃ bhūtvā́ prátaran prado 'gré tvátto bhūtáṃ sáṃbhāváyiṣyasi sárveṣāṃ kā́yānām árham arhate svā́hā
7.2.4.2 [2.7] tváṃ buddhír bhūtā́nām antarātmā́ púṇyavatāṃ púṇyéṣu sájjamānaḥ tváṃ buddhyā́ vicínvamānaḥ puṇya-rūpā́ya svā́hā
7.2.4.3 [2.8] yás sūkṣmā́n saṃcáramāṇān bhāvā́bhāvā́n bhavyābhavyā́n
kúrvann ā́tmīyam ámito dhunoti dhuráṃ vahiṣyase svā́hā
7.2.4.4 [2.9] yásya vā bháyād bhágavān uttasthé svayáṃ sū́ryas satyáṃ kā́laṃ váhamānaḥ
yásmāt téja ātmíyaṃ kr̥tvā́ sarvān asmā́n pālayiṣyasi svā́hā
7.2.4.5 [2.10] yaṃ tvā́ṃ sarváṃ pā́lanāyābhibhūtáṃ devā́s sárve páśye
vícaranti té devā́s tvam evá sárve māyā́ māyaíṣā te svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.4.1 [2.6] 'Having become mind (<s>manas</s>), extending further, generous in the beginning — you will bring into being all that is born from you, worthy of all bodies — to the worthy one, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.4.2 [2.7] 'You are intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), the inner Self of beings, attached to the meritorious among the meritorious — you, discerning through intellect — to the one whose form is merit (<s>puṇya</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.4.3 [2.8] 'He who, making subtle, moving entities — existences and non-existences, what is to be and what is not to be — his own, the immeasurable one shakes [them]; you will bear the yoke, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.4.4 [2.9] 'From whose fear the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself — <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) — arose, bearing true time — from whom, having made the radiance one's own, you will protect us all, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.4.5 [2.10] 'You whom all, overcome, [look to] for protection — may all the gods see! The gods move about — you alone are all; <s>māyā</s> (illusion) — this <s>māyā</s> is yours, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: 7.2.0.2 yiṣyasi svā́hā māyaíṣā te svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.0.2 [Rubric:] '...you will [protect], <s>svāhā</s>! This <s>māyā</s> is yours, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.5.1 [3.1] yás tváṃ bhūtvā́ parjányo bibheti randhré prajā́bhir
 ākr̥ṣyámāṇaḥ satyáṃ kālaṃ vraténa pāláyan hlā́dayiṣyase svā́hā
7.2.5.2 [3.2] kāmó bhūtvā́ prajā́nām antarā sthitás sárvā lokān hlādáyañ jī́vamānaḥ sandárpaṇāya haráye varāya svā́hā
7.2.5.3 [3.3] áṅgād aṅgād ánuprā́viśat sárvān lokā́n saṃrakṣaṇāya
yó vā vasán devó mātaríśvā sá yo 'smā́kaṃ bhū́tyai bhū́taye svā́hā
7.2.5.4 [3.4] yó mohayan bhūtā́nā(g)ṃ[*745] sargā́dhirákṣaṇāya
yás saṃkócas saṃkócanāya bhávatāt svā́hā
7.2.5.5 [3.5] yó vā daśātmā́ úpari spr̥śan vā́ devā́nāṃ jyótir jyótiṣām
úttaraḥ svayáṃ vā spŕ̥śan jyótir jyótiṣe svā́hā
[*745] 1946 edition bhūtā́nāṃ
children.translated_text: 7.2.5.1 [3.1] 'You who, having become <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god), [make all] tremble in their openings, drawn by offspring — protecting true time through your vow, you will refresh [all], <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.5.2 [3.2] 'Having become <s>Kāma</s> (Desire), dwelling within offspring, refreshing all worlds while living — to the one who fills with pride, to <s>Hari</s>, to the best one, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.5.3 [3.3] 'From limb to limb he entered, for the protection of all worlds — he who as the god <s>Mātariśvan</s> dwells [in all] — he who [is] for our prosperity, for [our] well-being, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.5.4 [3.4] 'He who, deluding beings, [acts] for the protection of creation — he who is contraction, for the [cosmic] contraction — may it be, <s>svāhā</s>!' 7.2.5.5 [3.5] 'He who is the ten-fold Self, touching above — the light of the gods, of lights — the higher one, himself touching — [that] light, to the Light, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.6.1 [3.6] yó brahmā́ bráhma-vídām ātmā syād ātmá-cakṣuṣām
bhū́tir bhū́timatāṃ súkr̥taṃ kr̥tāya svā́hā
7.2.6.2 [3.7] sārasvato vā́ eṣá devó 'yáṃ na vā́ hayaḥ pā́ramātmikaḥ
bhayó 'bhayó vā́ sárvaṃ sáṃdhuṣe svāhā
7.2.6.3 [3.8] yó vā páraṃ jyotiḥ páraṃ sándadhānaḥ
paramātmā́ púruṣaṃ sáñjánáyíṣyase svā́hā
7.2.6.4 [3.9] yó doṣáś catúraś caturtháś catúraḥ pádārthā́n
sarváṃ lokásya sándadhānas sáte sátvam ādádhānāya svā́hā
7.2.6.5 [3.10] yásyaitā́ bráhma-mū́rtayo br̥hád-brahmā́ṇaṃ brahma
ā́dadhānaḥ yáṃ bráhma brahma-gúptaye páraṃparāya svā́hā
children.translated_text:
He who is <s>Brahmā</s>, the Self of those who know <s>Brahman</s>, who would be the Self of those with the eye of the Self,
the prosperity of the prosperous, the good deed for the doer, <s>svāhā</s>!
This <s>deva</s> (god) is indeed of <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s nature, or else he is the swift one, pertaining to the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self);
whether fearful or fearless, he kindles all together, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who indeed establishes the supreme light, the supreme,
the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), you shall bring forth the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Person), <s>svāhā</s>!
He who is the fault [remover], the fourth among the four, [establishing] the four categories of meaning,
establishing all of the world, placing being in the existent, <s>svāhā</s>!
He whose forms are these forms of <s>Brahman</s>, the great <s>Brahman</s>,
establishing <s>Brahman</s> — whom <s>Brahman</s> [protects] for the protection of <s>Brahman</s>, in succession, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 7.2.0.3 jyótiṣe svā́hā parāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: To the light, <s>svāhā</s>! To the supreme, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.7.1 [4.1] vā́ko vā́ ánuvāko vā́kaṃ vā́kaṃ sáṃjúṣamāṇaḥ
devás sa sváṃ sva-gúptaye sváyaṃ jyótiṣe jyótiṣe svā́hā
7.2.7.2 [4.2] dvā́v etaú pakṣī́ ácaraṃ carantaú nā́dhuráṃ vyádhunīte
yáś caiko bhunakti bhóktre svā́hā
7.2.7.3 [4.3] yó vā ā́yuḥ páramātmānaṃ[*746] mīḍhúṣaḥ pāraṃparyā́t paráḥ parāyaṇáḥ paró lokā́nāṃ paramā́ dadhānaḥ parátaḥ parāya svā́hā
7.2.7.4 [4.4] yó vā téjas téjasāṃ téjas téja ā́dadhānaḥ
satyás téjas téjasāṃ téjas téjas téjase svā́hā
7.2.7.5 [4.5] saha saṃpāyā́s tvam āśíṣam āśīr bhūtā́bhūtám
āśíṣam āśī-rāsī́r āśir ánubhūmis[*747] svā́hā
[*746] páramātmānaṃ read as páramātmāyaṃ
[*747] Text: ánubhūmi
children.translated_text:
Speech indeed, or recitation — delighting in speech after speech,
the <s>deva</s> (god) himself, for the protection of his own, himself to the light, to the light, <s>svāhā</s>!
These two birds, one unmoving and one moving, do not shake off the yoke;
the one who eats — to the enjoyer, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who is indeed the life-force, the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), of the bountiful one, beyond succession, the supreme refuge, beyond the worlds, establishing the highest, beyond — to the supreme, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who indeed establishes radiance, the radiance of radiances, the radiance among radiances,
truly the radiance, the radiance of radiances — to the radiance of radiances, <s>svāhā</s>!
Together with the draughts, you [are] the blessing; the blessing is for what has been and what has not been;
the blessing, the giver of blessings, the blessing experienced, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.8.1 [4.6] yó vā sáṃyogas saṃjúṣamāṇás sandhús sandhúkṣaṇānām
saṃyógaṃ sándadhānaḥ puṇyáḥ puṇyā́nāṃ puṇyā́ya svā́hā
7.2.8.2 [4.7] sahásraṃ vā́ yásyaivá vitānám ā́dadhānas sahásraṃ vā́
āsíṣas sāsikā́ḥ sahasraṃ yásya vaí sā́sikās sahásraṃ sahasrāya svā́hā
7.2.8.3 [4.8] svātígā gúptayo guptís satyáṃ satyā́nāṃ sā́tváṃ padám
tát satváṃ satvám āsīt sā́tvaṃ sā́tvaṃ vaí sātvám ādádhānāya svā́hā
7.2.8.4 [4.9] satváṃ vā́ údrekám āsīd yát satvám ubháyor anugoptā́
tát satváṃ satyáṃ-vadāya satyā́ya svā́hā
7.2.8.5 [4.10] satyo jyotis sátyāntarātmā́ satyódyógás sátyas sat-karmá
satyáṃ satyá-vítānam āsīt satyá-satyā́ya svā́hā
7.2.0.4 bhūmi svā́hā satyā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: To the earth, <s>svāhā</s>! To truth, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.9.1 [5.1] satyas satváṃ púṇyam āsīt púṇyo vā daivíkam satyáṃ
satvám ārṣaṃ satyaṃ satváṃ sát-pathāya svā́hā
7.2.9.2 [5.2] satyó jyotís satvaṃ prāṇā́s satvādhārā́s sátva-sáṃdhānáḥ
satyas satváṃ prákāśaṃ jyótir jyótiṣe svā́hā
7.2.9.3 [5.3] kā́mīm umā́m īśiṣam ī́śiṣa satyám īśiṣam ī́śiṣāṇām tát satyáṃ satyá-rūpaṃ
satyáṃ satyā́ya sandádhānāya svā́hā
7.2.9.4 [5.4] ā́riṇī vā́ ārandá ā́vārandó
ayám ārandáḥ mā́randá ā́nandáté svā́hā
7.2.9.5 [5.5] tat satvó vā́ víṣṇur udyogás sūryo go vā́ víṣṇur viśat
víśvaṃ víśvaṃ sándadhānas tád víśvaṃ víṣṇave viśvá-rūpāya svā́hā
children.translated_text:
Truth and essence were meritorious; merit indeed is the divine truth;
essence is of the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers), truth and essence — to the path of truth, <s>svāhā</s>!
Truth is light, essence is the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths), the support of essence, the joiner of essences;
truth and essence are radiance, light — to the light, <s>svāhā</s>!
The desirable <s>Umā</s>, I would rule, I would rule over truth, I would rule among rulers — that truth, of the form of truth,
truth — to the one who establishes truth, <s>svāhā</s>!
The fire-drill indeed, the churning stick, the counter-churning,
this churning stick — may the non-dying one rejoice, <s>svāhā</s>!
That essence indeed, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the exertion, the sun, the cow; or <s>Viṣṇu</s> entered,
establishing everything, all — that all, to <s>Viṣṇu</s> of universal form, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.10.1 [5.6] tád bhū́r bhū́-sthaṃ bhū́-stho vā́ viśvá-rūpas tád bhū́ḥ prāṇá-saṃkhyātáḥ
bhū́r bhū́r āsīd bhū́r asi bhúvo 'si súvar asi bhū́r bhū́taye svā́hā
7.2.10.2 [5.7] ā́po vā́ ā́pa ā́po 'ntarātmā́ yó vedó vedā́nām ādhāráḥ
vedāntarātmā́ sá-raso rasa-saṃkhyātó rásaṃ rasam āsīd rasā́ya svā́hā
7.2.10.3 [5.8] trayī vā́ kā́maṃ trayī-máyaṃ trí-guṇaṃ tretātmakám
trayī vā́ jyótis trí-guṇaṃ tri-guṇātmakáṃ tásmai tretā́gnaye trí-gúṇāya svā́hā
7.2.10.4 [5.9] dvaú vā múkhyau múkhyādhārau sá-sukhau sānandaú
sá-smeraú smerā́yatau sā́nandám ānandáte svā́hā
7.2.10.5 [5.10] sá ekaíkas sādhārás sā́dhiṣṭhānó ínādhiṣṭhānáḥ
káṃ kaṃ padé pade pātaḥ pādā́ya pā́dite svā́hā
children.translated_text:
That is <s>bhūḥ</s> (earth), established on earth; he who stands on earth is indeed of universal form; that <s>bhūḥ</s>, enumerated by <s>prāṇa</s> (breath),
<s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhūḥ</s> it was, <s>bhūḥ</s> you are, <s>bhuvaḥ</s> you are, <s>suvaḥ</s> you are — <s>bhūḥ</s>, for prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>!
Waters indeed, water, the waters' inner Self; he who is the <s>Veda</s>, the support of the <s>Vedas</s>,
the inner Self of the <s>Vedas</s>, with essence, enumerated by essence — essence was essence — to essence, <s>svāhā</s>!
The triple [<s>Veda</s>] indeed, desire, consisting of the triple, of three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), of the nature of <s>Tretā</s>,
the triple indeed is light, of three <s>guṇas</s>, of the nature of three <s>guṇas</s> — to that <s>Tretā</s>-fire, of three <s>guṇas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
Two indeed are the principal ones, the chief supports, with happiness, with bliss,
with smiles, the wide-smiling ones — with bliss he rejoices, <s>svāhā</s>!
He, each one, the fundamental support, the one with the supreme abode,
in step after step, the guardian — to the foot, to the established one, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.0.5 viśva-rū́pā́ya[*748] svā́hā pādite svā́hā
[*748] 1946 edition: rū́pā́ya
children.translated_text: To the one of universal form, <s>svāhā</s>! To the established one, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.11.1 [6.1] svayam ādis sárvāntarātmā́ devás sa sváyaṃ krīḍā́tmakam ávāsr̥jat
yás svayáṃ lokám ávadhāram avadhārayant svā́hā
7.2.11.2 [6.2] yás svayáṃ sr̥ṣṭám ātmánā guptám ánu saṃvitānám ácaraṃ carantam
svayáṃ krī́ḍan krīḍáyan krīḍā́ntaram ánuprā́viśat svā́hā́
7.2.11.3 [6.3] svaújasā sárvám ā́dadhāti yáḥ pā́pīyā(g)ṃsam ánupádam ā́hí(g)ṃsat
supuṇyaṃ púṇyātmakaṃ[*749] púṇya-vitānán dádhāra devā́ya svā́hā
7.2.11.4 [6.4] kṣmā́m ekā́ṃ sálilāvasannā́ṃ śrutvā́ svanantī́m ánu supátantīm
svayáṃ bhūtvā́ varāhó vára újjahāra tásmai devā́ya súkr̥tā́ya pítre svā́hā
7.2.11.5 [6.5] yáḥ kundháramāṇaḥ kún-dharān kúṃ-dharatām íty avocat
tā́ṃ sānumato vídadhat sva-téjasā tásmai variṣṭhā́ya váradāya pítre svā́hā
[*749] 1946 edition: súpúṇyātmakam
children.translated_text:
Self-originated, the inner Self of all, the <s>deva</s> (god) himself created that which is of the nature of play;
he who himself, determining the world, continues to determine, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who himself, having created by his own Self, protected, spread out — the unmoving [becoming] moving,
himself playing, causing to play, entered into the midst of the play, <s>svāhā</s>!
By his own might he establishes all; he who does not harm the sinful one step by step,
he upheld the supremely meritorious, of meritorious nature, the canopy of merit — to the <s>deva</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
Hearing the earth, the one [submerged] in the waters, sounding, falling well,
himself becoming the boar (<s>Varāha</s>), the excellent one, he lifted her up — to that <s>deva</s> (god), the well-doing one, the Father, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who, while supporting, spoke to the mountain-bearers: 'Bear the earth!' —
establishing her with mountains by his own radiance — to that most excellent boon-giver, the Father, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.12.1 [6.6] yó vā pr̥thāṃ práskhalantīṃ prámr̥jyāmr̥jāṃgī́m
yá ūrvór úpadadhāt tásmai mukhyā́ya váradāya pitre svā́hā
7.2.12.2 [6.7] yā́ṃ gām uśantī́m úśanābhipūrṇā́m ā́rakta-nīlā́m amŕ̥tā́ṃ rajantī́m
ā́lālayan[*750] lā́lita[*751]-kaṃkaṇāṃ tā́ṃ tásmai prajeśā́ya váradāya pítre svā́hā
7.2.12.3 [6.8] prájā-pate ná tvad etā́ny anyó víśvā jātā́ni pári tā́ babhūva
yát-kāmās te juhumás tán no astu vayá(gg)ṃ syāma pátayo rayīṇā́(g)ṃ svā́hā
7.2.12.4 [6.9] yó dhū́r dhuraṃ dhū́r dhuraṃ dhūr varāṇā́m
sudhū́r dhū́r asi dhūr dhurāṇā́ṃ dhū́r asi dhū́r-váṃga me[*752] svā́hā
7.2.12.5 [6.10] yó vā vyahiṃṣī́j járayājarantáṃ tán daitya-mukhyám amŕ̥tātma-rūpám
súkhuraṃ khurāṇā́ṃ kíñcit svánántaṃ tásmai nr̥siṃhā́ya súreśa-pitre svā́hā
[*750] Text: ā́lāḷayan
[*751] Text: lā́ḷita
[*752] Text: mes
children.translated_text:
He who, when <s>Pr̥thā</s> (the Earth) was stumbling, cleansed the unblemished-limbed one,
who placed her upon [his] thighs — to that chief boon-giver, the Father, <s>svāhā</s>!
The cow, the willing one, filled with desire, dark-red and blue, immortal, glowing,
he who caressed her, with tinkling bangles — to that lord of offspring, the boon-giver, the Father, <s>svāhā</s>!
O <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of Creatures), none other than you has encompassed all these born beings;
what desires we have when we offer oblation, may that be ours — may we be lords of riches, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who is the yoke-bearer, the yoke of yokes, the yoke of the best,
the good yoke-bearer — you are the yoke, the yoke of yoke-bearers, you are the yoke, the yoke-pole for me, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who indeed destroyed the unaging one by aging, that chief of the <s>Daityas</s> (demons), of immortal self-nature,
with good hooves among the hoofed, somewhat roaring — to that <s>Narasiṃha</s> (Man-Lion), the Father, lord of the <s>Suras</s> (gods), <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 7.2.0.6 váradāya pitre svā́hā sureśa-pitre svā́hā
children.translated_text: To the boon-giver, the Father, <s>svāhā</s>! To the Father, lord of the <s>Suras</s> (gods), <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.13.1 [7.1] tápo-nídhiṃ tápasāṃ rayíndaṃ ráyim āyur aṃgáṃ vyásanaugha-hiṃsrám
sā́siṣv asantáṃ sávane savítre tásmai suréśā́ya surá-br̥nda-kartre svā́hā
7.2.13.2 [7.2] yó vā nr̥siṃhó víjayaṃ bibhárṣi rā́-rājimantáṃ ráyi-daṃ kavī́nām
sá-rājimantáṃ sájayaṃ sahásraṃ tásmai suyantré suśévadhaye śevádhaye svā́hā
7.2.13.3 [7.3] ráyiḥ kakudmā́n vídadhad vináṣṭaṃ[*753] ráyimad vidhā́nam
tásmai kakutré víkaṭāya pítre svā́hā
7.2.13.4 [7.4] rākā́m ahá(g)ṃ suhávā́(g)ṃ suṣṭutī́ huve śr̥ṇótu nas subhágā bódhatu tmánā[*754]
sī́vyatv ápas sūcyā́ccidyamāna yā dádātu vīra(g)ṃ śatá-dāyam ukthyá(gg)ṃ svā́hā
7.2.13.5 [7.5] védāhám etáṃ púruṣaṃ mahā́ntam ādityá-varṇaṃ támasas tú pāré
sárvāṇi rūpā́ṇi vicítya dhī́ro nā́māni kr̥tvā́bhivádan yád ā́ste svā́hā
[*753] Text: dvináṣṭaṃ
[*754] 1946 edition: dmánā
children.translated_text:
The treasure-house of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), the giver of wealth among austerities, wealth, life, limb, the destroyer of the flood of misfortunes,
the one present in the swords, at the <s>savana</s> (pressing), to <s>Savitṛ</s> — to that lord of the <s>Suras</s>, the maker of the host of gods, <s>svāhā</s>!
He who indeed, O <s>Narasiṃha</s> (Man-Lion), you bear victory, the radiant and wealthy one, the giver of riches to the sages,
with radiance, with victory, a thousandfold — to that one of excellent instruments, to the excellent treasure, the treasure, <s>svāhā</s>!
Wealth, the eminent one, apportioning what was lost, the wealthy ordinance,
to that eminent one, the terrible one, the Father, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Rākā</s> (the Full-Moon goddess) I invoke, easily invoked, with good praise; may the blessed one hear us and awaken of herself;
may she sew her work with an unbreaking needle — may she give a hero, a giver of a hundredfold, worthy of praise, <s>svāhā</s>!
I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Person), of the color of the sun, beyond darkness;
the wise one, having discerned all forms, having made names, who thus speaks — <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.14.1 [7.6] dig-dóṣā yásya vídiśas sva-karṇaú dyáur āsa vaktrám údaran nabho vā
sā́si ṣma vā yā́s sváyam āpa dáṃtaṃ tásmai varatré váradāya kásmai svā́hā
7.2.14.2 [7.7] padmā́sya-vákṣāḥ páramas supuṇyáḥ padmā́ janitrī́ páramasya vā́saḥ
sūkṣmáṃ sā́vitraṃ sváyam ādadhā́nas sā́vitra-rūpáṃ parámaṃ supuṇya(gg)ṃ svā́hā
7.2.14.3 [7.8] yáḥ puṇḍarīkáḥ parámāntarātmā kámrāṃga-rūpáṃ kamalaṃ dadhāra
sá-rase rasā́ya svā́hā
7.2.14.4 [7.9] rayīṇā́ṃ pátiṃ br̥hántaṃ rā́-rāga-muktáṃ gurúṃ sanīkám[*755]
táṃ rāyo rūpáṃ ráyi-bhūta-bhū́taṃ rayímat-sura-mitre[*756] svā́hā
7.2.14.5 [7.10] rāyā́ṃ patatré rayím ādadhātré rāyó br̥hántaṃ ráyimat supúṣṭām
rā́-rājimantáṃ ratáye ramantáṃ táṃ biṃbavantáṃ kákudāya bhádre svā́hā
[*755] From: sanī, gift. MW p. 1141.
[*756] PUB: suratre instead of sura-mitre; US: suratraḥ instead of sura-mitre
children.translated_text: 7.2.14.1 [7.6] He whose directions are his arms, whose intermediate directions are his ears, whose face is heaven, whose belly is the sky — she who herself obtained the tooth; for that boon-granting one, for whom, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.14.2 [7.7] Lotus-faced, broad-chested, the supreme, most meritorious — <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is the mother, the garment of the Supreme; bestowing the subtle <s>Sāvitra</s> (form) himself — of <s>Sāvitra</s> form, the supreme, most meritorious, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.14.3 [7.8] He who is the lotus, the supreme inner self, who bore the lotus of lovely-limbed form — with essence, for essence, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.14.4 [7.9] The lord of riches, the great one, freed from passion, weighty, the gift-giver — that form of wealth, who has become the being of wealth, for the wealthy friend of the gods, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.14.5 [7.10] On the wings of wealth, bestowing wealth, the great wealth, well-nourished — radiant with streaks of wealth, delighting in delight, that orb-bearing one, for the summit, O auspicious one, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 755-756: From sanī 'gift' (MW p. 1141); variant readings in PUB and US.]

children.text: 7.2.0.7 yádā́ste svā́hā bhadre svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.0.7 [Catch-words:] 'When at rest, <s>svāhā</s>! O auspicious one, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.15.1 [8.1] yát sāra-bhūtáṃ sákalaṃ dharítraṃ móda-prāyeṇā́nubhūtam ánuviddham
sūkṣmás sureśás sákalaṃ bibhárti tásmai súreśā́ya sakálaṃ supuṇya(gg)ṃ svā́hā
7.2.15.2 [8.2] phálo vā́ eṣá lokā́nām ájaro mahātmā́ víśvaṃ yáḥ pāti vímalo 'malākhyaḥ
tásmai varatré váradasya púṣṭyai svā́hā
7.2.15.3 [8.3] dhū́r no vahantā́ṃ ratáye ramantā́ṃ púṃ-bhūtimantás sámayas suṣúmnā
áṃ rājimantáṃ sákalasya gúptyai svā́hā
7.2.15.4 [8.4] víśvaṃ bibhárṣi prásuro rudantáṃ
sáṃrājimantáṃ sákalaṃ prarūḍhám
sá no vitatya práhiṇotu pátre svā́hā
7.2.15.5 [8.5] só vā́ sva-rū́pas sámadr̥k samágro vídhu-daṃ tudán yo vídadhat padáṃ vā
víyati prakā́śaṃ bŕ̥hate ruhéṇa táṃ biṃbavantáṃ samádaṃ samagra(gg)ṃ svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.15.1 [8.1] What is the essential, the entire support, experienced and penetrated mostly with joy — the subtle Lord of the Gods sustains all; for that Lord of the Gods, all most meritorious, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.15.2 [8.2] He is indeed the fruit of the worlds, the unaging great self, who protects all, stainless, called 'Immaculate' — for that chosen one, for the nourishment of the boon-giver, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.15.3 [8.3] May the yoke bear for us, may they delight in delight — endowed with manly prosperity, the agreement, the gracious — the radiant one, for the protection of all, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.15.4 [8.4] You bear the universe, the swiftly moving weeping one — the radiant sovereign, all fully grown; may he, extending, send forth for the vessel, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.15.5 [8.5] He indeed, of his own form, equal-seeing, complete — striking the moon-destroyer, who establishes the abode, luminous in the sky, by ascent to the great — that orb-bearing one, of complete equanimity, entire, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.16.1 [8.6] bhūr bhuvaṃ vā́ bhuvo vā́ suvo vā́ kíñcit svanántaṃ súṣuve samastám
sárvasya dātā́ram ajáraṃ jaritre svā́ḥa
7.2.16.2 [8.7] dākṣāyaṇyā́ṃ prásr̥taṃ samástaṃ sámkocayitvā́ sákalaṃ vitānám
sáṃvāsayan me sákalaṃ varíṣṭaṃ tásmai prajeśā́ya dhuráṃ-dharāya svā́hā
7.2.16.3 [8.8] ā́śās samástāḥ prátaran v antás tā́s tā́ vased yā́ kámalā samástā
sā́ me gr̥he vā́ sámadatta puṣṭí(gg)ṃ svā́hā
7.2.16.4 [8.9] yó jaṃgamānā́ṃ sákalaṃ bibharṣi[*757] sárvaṃ viyad vā́ vícareta śákṣyán
tán naur jale vapuṣy ánty ajásra(gg)ṃ svā́hā
7.2.16.5 [8.10] yó vā daśānā́ṃ prásr̥tās samástās tāṃs tā́n dadhānā́s sámayāt sa-bī́jāḥ
śabdā́tiriktyaí sva-baláṃ balāya svā́hā
[*757] Text: bibhirṣi
children.translated_text: 7.2.16.1 [8.6] <s>Bhūḥ</s>, or <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, or <s>Suvaḥ</s> — whatever resounding, gave birth to all; the giver of all, the unaging one, for the praiser, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.16.2 [8.7] In <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> (daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>), what was spread forth entire — having contracted the entire canopy, making the entire best dwell in me; for that Lord of Creatures, the yoke-bearer, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.16.3 [8.8] All the directions, crossing inward — may all those abide; she who is <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) entire — she in my house gave equal nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.16.4 [8.9] You who bear all of the moving beings, able to traverse all the sky — that ship in the water, in the body, ceaselessly, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.16.5 [8.10] He who of the ten, all extended forth — holding those, from agreement, with seed; for the transcendence of sound, one's own strength for strength, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnote 757: Text reads bibhirṣi.]

children.text: 7.2.0.8 sámágra(gg)ṃ svā́hā balā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.0.8 [Catch-words:] 'Entire, <s>svāhā</s>! For strength, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.17.1 [9.1] catvā́ro dóṣāḥ práharanti yásya sárvasya goptré sá-rasāya dhā́mne
sómasya puṇyáṃ ráyimat-pravŕ̥ddhyai svā́hā
7.2.17.2 [9.2] vákṣo vasaty ásya várāṃ variṣṭháṃ vā́kan dadhānā́ vávr̥dhe samástam
tásmai variṣṭhā́ya vára-pravr̥ddhyai svā́hā
7.2.17.3 [9.3] aṇór áṇīyān maható máhīyān ātmā́ gúhāyāṃ níhito 'sya jantóḥ
tám akratuṃ paśyati vīta-śokó dhātúḥ prasā́dān mahimā́nam īśa(gg)ṃ svā́hā
7.2.17.4 [9.4] víṣṇur váriṣṭho vára-dāna-mukhyó yó viśva-r̥ṣī́n dhyā́yan nu kurván
víśvaṃ hī́ṣad[*758] vyádadhat tam átra tád víṣṇave yāḥ prabhavíṣṇave yā amítaṃ bharatre svā́hā
7.2.17.5 [9.5] ábjo juṣantáḥ právadat patántaḥ pūṃ pū́ṃ[*759] puṣantáḥ púnar yaḥ pravā́laḥ[*760]
káṃ kaṃ janitré sáma-tejasan te svā́hā
[*758] Text: hī́hiṣad
[*759] Text: pū́ṃ
[*760] Text: pravā́ḷaḥ
children.translated_text: 7.2.17.1 [9.1] The four watches strike for him — for the protector of all, for the abode full of essence; the merit of <s>Soma</s>, for the growth of wealth, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.17.2 [9.2] His chest dwells as the best of the best, bearing speech — he has grown in entirety; for that most excellent one, for the growth of boons, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.17.3 [9.3] Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great — the <s>Ātman</s> is hidden in the cave of this being; one who is free from desire sees him, free from sorrow — through the grace of the Creator, [one sees] the greatness of the Lord, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.17.4 [9.4] <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the most excellent, foremost in granting boons — who, meditating on the universal sages, acting, arranged the entire universe here; for that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, those powers for the powerful one, the immeasurable, for the bearer, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.17.5 [9.5] Delighting in the lotus, speaking while descending, nourishing again and again — he who is the new shoot; for the progenitor, of equal splendor, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 758-760: Variant readings in the text.]

children.text:
7.2.18.1 [9.6] mā́m ātma-guptā́ṃ váhate sma bhū́tyaitā́ṃ rājimantā́ṃ sudhū́r dhū́rayantīm
dhū́r asi dhruvā́ya svā́hā
7.2.18.2 [9.7] yáṃ cintayantó nigámānta-rūpáṃ yáṃ viśva-rūpáṃ parámātma-rūpám
táṃ vindamānā́ṃ sákalaṃ vrajántīṃ táṃ deva-mukhyáṃ surátaṃ bhavā́ya svā́hā
7.2.18.3 [9.8] puṇyā́ṃ ca púṇyaḥ púruṣe pur-agré tā́ṃ rājimantā́ṃ níśi coditā́nām
vídadhāti púṣṭyai harán-parāya svā́hā
7.2.18.4 [9.9] só no bhūtó yó vāmr̥tātmā́ supúṣṭim ásmat pítaraṃ pavítram
só no 'stu bhū́tyai kamalā́-varāya svā́hā
7.2.18.5 [9.10] sa tv eva nityáṃ sákalās sa-mūrtáyas sá-ratās tv anántāḥ
té jījayanto víyati kṣayā́ṇāṃ tát-tat-śavitré hárate harāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.18.1 [9.6] She carries me, self-protected, with prosperity — this radiant one, the good yoke-bearer, bearing the yoke; you are the yoke, for the steadfast, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.18.2 [9.7] Those who contemplate him of <s>Vedānta</s> form, of universal form, of supreme-self form — her who finds that, going entirely — that chief of the gods, delightful, for becoming, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.18.3 [9.8] The meritorious one, the meritorious in the person, at the forefront — that radiant one, of those urged at night; he bestows for nourishment, taking away, for the beyond, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.18.4 [9.9] May he who is the immortal self be for us, [granting] good nourishment — our father, the pure one; may he be for our prosperity, for the boon of the lotus, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.18.5 [9.10] He indeed is eternal — all embodied forms, delightful and infinite; they conquering in the sky of dwellings, for that <s>Savitṛ</s> of each and every — he takes, for the remover, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 7.2.0.9 sánte svā́hā harāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.0.9 [Catch-words:] 'For the existent, <s>svāhā</s>! For the remover, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.19.1 [10.1] yā́ gā váriṣṭhā sáhasūr dharitrī́ vasúṃ vasuṃ vaí vásunīha bhádrā
rérījayanto rájitáṃ rajate svā́hā
7.2.19.2 [10.2.] vāyúr antarātmā́ váhatī samástas sá-puṇya devéti sá sūri-muktáḥ
sū́ris súrāṇāṃ súraso 'py asun-dás samū́hya devā́ya vára-dāya pítre svā́hā
7.2.19.3 [10.3] sárvopáriṣṭād ádhi tiṣṭhat ātmā́ yásyopáriṣṭāt páramas sa-muktáḥ
táṃ nī́rajantam ánusáṃparāya svā́hā
7.2.19.4 [10.4] támas sárva-bhūtam ádhunod vareṇyás táṃ satva-rūpáṃ sákalaṃ prakāśya
sáṃkleśayant sŕ̥ṣṭi-nímittaye yás tásmai páraṃ-bráhmaṇe páraṃ-jyótiṣe svā́hā
7.2.19.5 [10.5] jyótir jyótiṣāṃ jyótir ójo bálaṃ satváṃ satvā́tmakaṃ sáṃjyótir itthám tásmai sūkṣma-sūkṣmā́ya téjase svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.19.1 [10.1] She who is most excellent among the cows, conquering with a thousand, the supporter — with wealth upon wealth here, O auspicious one; they shine forth the silvered one, in silver, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.19.2 [10.2] <s>Vāyu</s> is the inner self, bearing all — the meritorious one goes divinely, he is freed by wisdom; the wise one of the wise, full of essence, life-giving — gathering for the god, for the boon-giving father, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.19.3 [10.3] The <s>Ātman</s> stands above all; above whom is the supreme, the liberated — him, the lotus-like, for the hereafter, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.19.4 [10.4] He, the excellent one, shook off darkness from all beings — illuminating all in the form of being; he who causes affliction for the purpose of creation — for that supreme <s>Brahman</s>, for the supreme light, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.19.5 [10.5] Light of lights, light, vigor, strength — being of the nature of being, thus co-luminous; for that subtlest of the subtle, for splendor, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
7.2.20.1[*761] [10.6] satváṃ satvā́tmakaṃ vā́ rájo rájasa ātmakám támas támasa ādhārás
sā́kr̥táṃ táṃ nirīśvaram īśvárā́ya svā́hā
7.2.20.2 [10.7] ánirbhiṇṇaṃ yásyedám āsīd ā́sīd údakam ātmakám
yásyo dā́vodan-artham[*762] uccam uccaír úrugāya svā́hā
7.2.20.3 [10.8] yásyecchā́ loké vā prájāyatir loké yán naivā́sīt tán naivāsīt
yád vā saṃjātáṃ yát sarvám ī́śam īśíṣe svā́hā
7.2.20.4 [10.9][*763] yó védādíḥ páramaḥ paro brahmā́ tri-mā́tras tráyī-mūrtikáḥ
śabdáś śabdātigáḥ paraṃ-bráhmaṇe páraṃ-jyótiṣe svā́hā
7.2.20.5 [10.10][*764] yó vā 'vyaktáṃ sákaláṃ právr̥ddhyai yád idáṃ sárvam āsīt
sānandáṃ sākr̥táṃ taṃ harán parāya svā́hā
[*761] 21 in book
[*762] Text: dā́vodhan-ardham
[*763] Missing in US
[*764] Missing in US
children.translated_text: 7.2.20.1 [10.6] <s>Sattva</s>, of the nature of <s>sattva</s>; <s>rajas</s>, of the nature of <s>rajas</s>; <s>tamas</s>, the support of <s>tamas</s> — well-made, him beyond the Lord, for the Lord, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.20.2 [10.7] For whom this was undivided, was of the nature of water — whose purpose most high, most high; for the wide-striding one, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.20.3 [10.8] Whose will in the world is creation in the world — what was not, that was not; whatever came to be, all that — the Lord; you rule, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.20.4 [10.9] He who is the beginning of the <s>Vedas</s>, the supreme, the transcendent <s>Brahman</s>, of three measures (the three <s>mātrās</s> of <s>Oṃ</s>), embodying the triple <s>Veda</s> — sound, transcending sound; for the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, for the supreme light, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.20.5 [10.10] He who is the unmanifest, all for growth — whatever all this was, with bliss, well-made; him, taking for the beyond, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 761-764: Numbering discrepancy; verses 10.9-10 missing in US.]

children.text: 7.2.0.10 téjase svā́hā parāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: 7.2.0.10 [Catch-words:] 'For splendor, <s>svāhā</s>! For the beyond, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
7.2.21.1 [11.1][*765] yó vā bhū́ter bhū́tir āsīt sā vānandáṃ pratyānandám
sáṃjuṣan vrajāmi[*766] satyáṃ satyā́ya svā́hā
7.2.21.2 [11.2] satyás satyá-sthas satyá-loka-sthas satyáṃ sáñjanitrám āsīt
satyáṃ satyā́ya ráṃhase svā́hā
7.2.21.3 [11.3] r̥tá(g)ṃ satyáṃ ámitaṃ purāṇám ā́diṃ janitrám ámr̥taṃ suréndram
saṃjyótiṣāṃ juṣámāṇaṃ[*767] juṣasva svā́hā
7.2.21.4 [11.4] áṃ rājimantáṃ sákalasya guptíṃ sóme juṣantám ámr̥taṃ bibharti
ráyimat supúṣṭiṃ gúṇavantam átra tásmai supuṇyā́ya váradāya pítre svā́hā
7.2.21.5 [11.5] mā́m ātma-guptā́ṃ sátvasya sarvásya vítāna-rūpā́ṃ saṃjū́juṣantī́ṃ páramāṃ pavítrām
sántārayantīṃ sváyam apramáttāṃ sáṃyojayitré váradāya pítre svā́hā
[*765] This chapter missing in US.
[*766] Text: vr̥jāmi
[*767] 1946 edition: r̥ṣámāṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 7.2.21.1 [11.1] He who was the prosperity of prosperity — she, bliss upon bliss, delighting, I go; truth, for truth, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.21.2 [11.2] The true one, established in truth, established in the world of truth — truth was the generatrix; truth, for truth, for swiftness, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.21.3 [11.3] <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), truth, immeasurable, ancient, the primal source, the immortal, lord of the gods — delighting in lights, delight! <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.21.4 [11.4] The radiant one, the protection of all, delighting in <s>Soma</s> — he bears the immortal; wealthy, well-nourished, endowed with qualities here; for that most meritorious, boon-granting father, <s>svāhā</s>! 7.2.21.5 [11.5] Me, self-protected, of canopy form encompassing all being, greatly delighting, the supreme, the pure — causing to cross over, herself vigilant; for the uniter, for the boon-granting father, <s>svāhā</s>! [Footnotes 765-767: This chapter missing in US; variant readings noted.]

children.text: 7.2.0.11 pítre svā́hā́ dve ca
children.translated_text: 7.2.0.11 [Catch-words:] 'For the father, <s>svāhā</s>' — and two [additional mantras].

children.text: [Colophon:]
children.translated_text: [Colophon:]

children.text:
háriḥ om
tatth sat
śrī śrīnivāsārpaṇam astu
children.translated_text: <s>Hariḥ Oṃ Tat Sat</s>. May this be an offering to <s>Śrī Śrīnivāsa</s>.

children.text:
Śrī Śrī Śrī-nivāsāya namaḥ
Śrī-vaikhānasa-mantra-praśnāṣṭake
aṣṭama-praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to Śrī Śrī <s>Śrīnivāsa</s>. In the collection of eight <s>praśnas</s> (sections) of the Śrī <s>Vaikhānasa Mantra</s>, the Eighth <s>Praśna</s>.

children.text:
8.1.1.1 tam éka-nemíṃ trí-vŕ̥ttá(g)ṃ ṣoḍaśāntá(g)ṃ śátā́rdhā́ráṃ víṃśátí prátyátárā́bhír áṣṭákaíṣ ṣáḍbhír víśvá-rū́paika-pāśám
trí-mā́rgá-bhédáṃ dví-nímíttaika-mohám
8.1.1.2 prajā́-patiṃ prathamáṃ yajñíyānāṃ devā́nām ágre yajatáṃ yajadhvam
sá no dadātu dráviṇa(g)ṃ suvī́rya(g)ṃ rāyás póṣaṃ víṣyatu nā́bhim asmé
8.1.1.3 raúkmáṃ kūrmáṃ bráhma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.1.4 tam eka-nemím gájáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.1.5 śatá-dhāra(g)ṃ hiraṇmáyam gárúḍáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.1.6 brahmā́ devā́nām bráhmaṇa imáṃ bráhmá-máṇíṃ bráhma-sthāne 'hám prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
children.translated_text: (8.1.1.1) That [wheel] of one felly, three turnings, sixteen ends, fifty spokes, with twenty counter-spokes, in groups of eight and six, of universal form, with one noose — of three-path division, two-cause, one delusion. (8.1.1.2) Worship <s>Prajāpati</s>, the first of the sacrificial ones, the worshipful at the forefront of the gods — may he give us wealth, good heroism; may he release to us the increase of riches, [opening] the navel. (8.1.1.3) I install the golden <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise) at the station of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.1.4) 'That one-fellied...' — I install the elephant, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.1.5) 'The hundred-streamed...' — I install the golden <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.1.6) '<s>Brahmā</s>, [lord] of the gods, by <s>Brahman</s>...' — I install this <s>Brahma</s>-gem at the station of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.

children.text:
8.1.2.1 índraṃ práṇayantaṃ índrā́yemáṃ vájrá-máṇím índra-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.2.2 agnā́v agníś carati práviṣṭa ŕ̥ṣīṇāṃ putró adhirājá eṣáḥ
sāhākŕ̥tya bráhmaṇā te juhomi[*768] mā́ devā́nāṃ mithuyā́ kar bhāgadhéyam
8.1.2.3 ágnaya imáṃ maúktíkám ágni-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.2.4 yamó dādhāra yamā́yemáṃ vaíḍū́ryá-máṇíṃ yáma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.2.5 vásavaḥ prathamáḥ nírr̥taya imáṃ śáṅkhá-jáṃ nírŕ̥ti-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
[*768] Text: jahomi
children.translated_text: (8.1.2.1) '<s>Indra</s>, the leader...' — I install this <s>vajra</s> (diamond)-gem for <s>Indra</s> at the station of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.2.2) <s>Agni</s> entered into <s>Agni</s> moves within — he is the son of the <s>Ṛṣis</s>, the sovereign here; having accomplished with the <s>Brahman</s>, I offer to you — do not make the portion of the gods go astray. (8.1.2.3) I install this pearl for <s>Agni</s> at the station of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.2.4) '<s>Yama</s> upheld...' — I install this <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl/lapis lazuli)-gem for <s>Yama</s> at the station of <s>Yama</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.2.5) 'The <s>Vasus</s>, the foremost...' — I install this conch-born [gem] for <s>Nirr̥ti</s> at the station of <s>Nirr̥ti</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. [Editorial note: Text reads 'jahomi', corrected to 'juhomi'.]

children.text:
8.1.3.1 yé te śatám váruṇāyemáṃ spháṭíká-máṇíṃ várúṇa-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.3.2 marútaḥ paramātmā́ vā́yava imáṃ púṣyá-kā́ntá-máṇíṃ vā́yu-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.3.3 sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānam sómā́yemáṃ cándrá-kā́ntá-máṇíṃ sóma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.3.4 ī́śānas sárva-lokānā́m ī́śā́nā́yemáṃ nī́lá-máṇím ī́śā́na-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.3.5 śáṃ no nídhattām vā́sukaya imám ámŕ̥tā́śmáká-máṇíṃ vā́súki-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námáḥ
children.translated_text: (8.1.3.1) 'Those hundred of yours, O <s>Varuṇa</s>...' — I install this crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>)-gem for <s>Varuṇa</s> at the station of <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.3.2) 'The <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Paramātman</s>...' — I install this <s>puṣyakānta</s> (topaz)-gem for <s>Vāyu</s> at the station of <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.3.3) '<s>Soma</s> the king...' — I install this <s>candrakānta</s> (moonstone)-gem for <s>Soma</s> at the station of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.3.4) '<s>Īśāna</s>, [lord] of all worlds...' — I install this blue (<s>nīla</s>)-gem for <s>Īśāna</s> at the station of <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.3.5) 'May he bestow welfare, <s>Vāsuki</s>...' — I install this <s>amr̥tāśmaka</s> (amethyst)-gem for <s>Vāsuki</s> at the station of <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.

children.text:
8.1.4.1 dhātā́ dhātr̥ṇā́ṃ bhúvanasya yás patir devá(g)ṃ savitā́ram[*769] abhimātiṣā́ham
imáṃ yajñám aśvínobhā́ bŕ̥haspátir devā́ḥ pāntu yájamānaṃ nyarthā́t
8.1.4.2 sā́dhyébhyá ímáṃ lóhítā́śmáká-máṇíṃ sā́dhya-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.4.3 víśve-devásya víśvébhyó dévébhyá ímám útpálá-máṇíṃ víśvé-déva-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.4.4 ádhi brahmā́ yatatām eṣá devó divás-pátyāṃ vādhi marúto vóbhayeṣā́m
8.1.4.5 tápo-yogī́ yogá ekás svādhiṣṭhā́ ninīhi víśvaṃ bhúvanasya bhū́yaḥ
8.1.4.6 síddhébhyá ímáṃ právā́lá[*770]-máṇíṃ síddha-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.4.7 ímā́ṃ mūrdhanyā́ máma vāṇy asū́nāṃ páter indriyā́ṇāṃ máteḥ priyā́ṇām
vā́co rucīnā́m[*771] právarāya gā́yan nídhiṃ nídadhyan prajáyā astu bhū́tyai
[*769] RV: trātāram; TS, VMP: savitā́ram
[*770] Text: právā́ḷá
[*771] 1926, '46, '84 editions: r̥cīnā́m
children.translated_text: (8.1.4.1) <s>Dhātr̥</s>, the upholder of upholders, lord of the world — the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, the overcomer of foes — may the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Br̥haspati</s>, and the gods protect this sacrifice and the sacrificer from harm. (8.1.4.2) I install this red (<s>lohitāśmaka</s>)-gem for the <s>Sādhyas</s> at the station of the <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.4.3) '[By the power] of the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, for all the gods...' — I install this <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus)-gem for the <s>Viśvedevas</s> at the station of the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.4.4) May <s>Brahmā</s> exert himself in this; the god [is lord] of heaven — or may the <s>Maruts</s> [exert themselves] over both. (8.1.4.5) The one <s>yoga</s> practitioner of austerity and <s>yoga</s>, self-established — lead the whole world of beings again! (8.1.4.6) I install this coral (<s>pravāla</s>)-gem for the <s>Siddhas</s> at the station of the <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.4.7) This head-[gem] — of my speech, of the vital airs, the lord of the senses, of thought, of the beloved — singing for the best of the voices' splendors, placing the treasure — may there be progeny and prosperity! [Editorial notes: variant readings from Ṛg Veda and Taittirīya Saṃhitā.]

children.text:
8.1.5.1 gándhárvébhyá ímā́ṃ mánáś-śílā́ṃ gándhárva-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.5.2 apsarássu yó gandhó gandharvéṣu ca yád yáśaḥ
daívo yó mānuṣó gandhás sá mā gandhás surabhír juṣatām
8.1.5.3 ápsáróbhyá ímáṃ śúktí-jám ápsára-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.5.4 yáṅ kādraveyā́[*772] ádhigās samū́he śérate vīrā́s tásya páribarhi víśvam
táṃ vāsuke bhūta-sáhasra-mūrte túbhyaṃ námaḥ pratháye bhū́taye tvā
8.1.5.5 nā́gébhyá ímáṃ vímálá-máṇíṃ nā́ga-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.5.6 aryamṇáḥ kumbhī́ śátruḥ pātra-pāṇír nipuṇáḥ áryámṇá ímáṃ kúrvíndám áryáma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.5.7 índraṃ práṇayantam índrā́yemáṃ gaíríkám índra-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
[*772] 1926 edition: kādraveyā́; 1946, '84 eds.: kārdraveyā́
children.translated_text: (8.1.5.1) I install this mind-stone (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) for the <s>Gandharvas</s> at the station of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.5.2) The fragrance that is among the <s>Apsarases</s>, and the glory among the <s>Gandharvas</s> — the divine and human fragrance — may that sweet fragrance delight me. (8.1.5.3) I install this pearl-shell-born [gem] for the <s>Apsarases</s> at the station of the <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.5.4) '[O you] whom the <s>Kādraveyās</s> (serpent-sons of <s>Kadrū</s>) attend in assembly — where the heroes recline, whose enclosure is the whole [universe] — to you, <s>Vāsuki</s>, of thousand-fold form among beings, obeisance to you — I spread forth for prosperity.' (8.1.5.5) I install this pure (<s>vimala</s>)-gem for the <s>Nāgas</s> at the station of the <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.5.6) '<s>Aryaman</s>'s vessel, the foe, with cup in hand, the skillful one...' — I install this <s>kurvinda</s> (corundum) for <s>Aryaman</s> at the station of <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.5.7) '<s>Indra</s>, the leader...' — I install this rock-mineral (<s>gairika</s>) for <s>Indra</s> at the station of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. [Editorial note: variant readings across editions.]

children.text:
8.1.6.1 agnā́v agníḥ ágnaya imáṃ hárítā́lákám[*773] ágni-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.6.2 yamó dādhāra yámā́yemā́ṃ mánáś-śílā́ṃ yáma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.6.3 vásavaḥ prathamáḥ nírr̥taya imám áṃjánáṃ nírŕ̥ti-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.6.4 yé te śatáṃ váruṇāyemáṃ kā́sī́sáṃ várúṇa-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.6.5 marútaḥ paramātmā́ vā́yava imáṃ pā́rádáṃ vā́yu-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
[*773] Text: hárítā́ḷákám
children.translated_text: (8.1.6.1) '<s>Agni</s> within <s>Agni</s>...' — I install this orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) for <s>Agni</s> at the station of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.6.2) '<s>Yama</s> upheld...' — I install this mind-stone (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) for <s>Yama</s> at the station of <s>Yama</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.6.3) 'The <s>Vasus</s>, the foremost...' — I install this collyrium (<s>añjana</s>) for <s>Nirr̥ti</s> at the station of <s>Nirr̥ti</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.6.4) 'Those hundred of yours, O <s>Varuṇa</s>...' — I install this green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>) for <s>Varuṇa</s> at the station of <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.6.5) 'The <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Paramātman</s>...' — I install this mercury (<s>pārada</s>) for <s>Vāyu</s> at the station of <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.

children.text:
8.1.7.1 sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānam sómā́yemáṃ saúrā́ṣṭrá(g)ṃ sóma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.7.2 ī́śānas sárva-lokānā́m ī́śā́nā́yemáṃ gó-rócánám ī́śā́na-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.7.3 brahmā́ devā́nāṃ padavī́ḥ kavīnā́m ŕ̥ṣir víprāṇāṃ mahiṣó mr̥gā́ṇām
śyenó gŕ̥ddhrāṇā(g)ṃ[*774] svádhitir vánānā(g)ṃ sómaḥ pavítram áty eti rébhán[*775]
8.1.7.4 bráhmáṇá ímā́ní sárvá-gándhā́ní bráhma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.7.5 índraṃ práṇayantam índrā́yémā́ní[*776] ṣáṣtíkā́n vrī́hī́nī́ndra-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpáyāmy óṃ námaḥ
[*774] RV: gŕ̥dhrāṇā(g)ṃ
[*775] Text: rébhánn
[*776] Text: índā́yémā́ní
children.translated_text: (8.1.7.1) '<s>Soma</s> the king...' — I install this <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> [mineral] for <s>Soma</s> at the station of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.7.2) '<s>Īśāna</s>, [lord] of all worlds...' — I install this <s>gorocana</s> (ox-gallstone pigment) for <s>Īśāna</s> at the station of <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.7.3) <s>Brahmā</s> [is] the path of the gods, the seer of the wise, the mighty buffalo among beasts, the hawk among vultures, the axe among forests — <s>Soma</s>, purifying, passes beyond, singing. (8.1.7.4) I install all these fragrances for <s>Brahman</s> at the station of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.7.5) '<s>Indra</s>, the leader...' — I install these sixty-day rice grains for <s>Indra</s> at the station of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. [Editorial note: variant readings across editions.]

children.text:
8.1.8.1 agnā́v agníḥ ágnaya imaú kúlúddhá-mā́ṣā́v[*777] ágni-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.8.2 yamó dādhāra yamā́yemaú gó-dhū́má-múdgaú yáma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.8.3 vásavaḥ prathamáḥ nírr̥taya imau tila-tilvau nirr̥ti-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.8.4 yé té śatám váruṇāyemaú vaṃśá-yávaú[*778] várúṇa-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.8.5 marútaḥ paramātmā́ vā́yava imaú nī́vā́rá-príyā́ṃgū́ vā́yu-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
[*777] Text: kúḷúddhámā́ṣā́v
[*778] 1946 edition: yavá-vaṃśá-yávaú
children.translated_text: (8.1.8.1) '<s>Agni</s> within <s>Agni</s>...' — I install these hulled black beans (<s>kuluddha-māṣa</s>) for <s>Agni</s> at the station of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.8.2) '<s>Yama</s> upheld...' — I install these cow-wheat and mung beans (<s>godhūma-mudga</s>) for <s>Yama</s> at the station of <s>Yama</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.8.3) 'The <s>Vasus</s>, the foremost...' — I install these sesame and sesame-seeds (<s>tila-tilva</s>) for <s>Nirr̥ti</s> at the station of <s>Nirr̥ti</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.8.4) 'Those hundred of yours, O <s>Varuṇa</s>...' — I install these bamboo-barley (<s>vaṃśa-yava</s>) for <s>Varuṇa</s> at the station of <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.8.5) 'The <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Paramātman</s>...' — I install these wild rice and millet (<s>nīvāra-priyaṅgu</s>) for <s>Vāyu</s> at the station of <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.

children.text:
8.1.9.1 sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānam sómā́yemaú gódhū́má-yávaú sóma-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.9.2 ī́śānas sárva-lokānā́m ī́śā́náyémā́ní sárvá-bī́jā́nī́śā́na-sthāne 'háṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.9.3 bhūyá ā́tma-vr̥tyā́ bála-tejo-jananyā́ devópavāhyā́ mánasā yayā́sánn
dākṣāyaṇyā́ dhanyaí[*779] yajeya[*780]
8.1.9.4 śrī́vátthsáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy oṃ námaḥ
8.1.9.5 námas sulomá sulomí bhuví bhuvó cittála[*781] gúhala[*782] dóṇīyat
8.1.9.6 pū́rṇá-kumbhaṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.9.7 sa eko bhū́d divā́ni śaṃ nas sáñcāri bhavódbhavaḥ
sraṣṭús sr̥ṣṭeś ca sáñcitaḥ
[*779] Text: thanyaí
[*780] cf. VMP 6.34.4: yajeya(gg)ṃ
[*781] Text: cittáḷa
[*782] Text: gúhaḷa
children.translated_text: (8.1.9.1) '<s>Soma</s> the king...' — I install these wheat and barley (<s>godhūma-yava</s>) for <s>Soma</s> at the station of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.9.2) '<s>Īśāna</s>, [lord] of all worlds...' — I install all these seeds for <s>Īśāna</s> at the station of <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.9.3) Again, by self-sustenance, generating strength and splendor, to be offered to the gods, with the mind by which they went — to the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, the fortunate one, I shall worship. (8.1.9.4) I install the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> [emblem], <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.9.5) Obeisance, O fair-haired one, the fair-haired on earth, of the earth — <s>cittala</s>, <s>guhala</s>, <s>doṇīyat</s> [ritual syllables]. (8.1.9.6) I install the full water-pot (<s>pūrṇa-kumbha</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>. (8.1.9.7) He, the one, became the sky — auspiciousness to us — the wanderer, born of becoming, accumulated by the creator of creation. [Editorial notes: variant readings across editions.]

children.text:
8.1.10.1 bhérī́ṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.10.2 devásya tvā ā́dárśáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.10.3 áto devā́ mátsyá-yúgmáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.10.4 kṣmā́m ekā́ṃ sálilāvasannā́ṃ śrutvā́ svanantī́m ánu supátantīm
svayam bhūtvā́ varāhó vára újjahāra tásmai devā́ya súkr̥tāya pitre
8.1.10.5 áṅkúśáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.10.6 tán mā yaśo 'gré śáṅkáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
children.translated_text: (8.1.10.1) 'I install the drum (<s>bherī</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.10.2) 'Of the god — I install your mirror (<s>ādarśa</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.10.3) '<s>Ato devā</s>... I install the fish-pair (<s>matsya-yugma</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.10.4) 'Having heard the one earth sunk in the waters, resounding, flying forth well — having himself become <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar), the most excellent one raised her up. To that god, the virtuous father.' (8.1.10.5) 'I install the goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.10.6) 'May that glory [be ours]... I install the conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.'

children.text:
8.1.11.1 brahmā́ devā́nām ā́vártáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óm námaḥ
8.1.11.2 bhū́mān anto 'gré gádā́-cákrā́sí-śárā́n prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.11.3 tán mā yaśo 'gré śáṅkhá-śā́rṅgá-khéṭákā́n prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.11.4 bráhmá[*783] bráhmāntarātmā́ bráhmá-pū́tāntarātmā́ bráhmaṇi bráhma-niṣṭhó bráhma-gupto gupto 'ham asmi
8.1.11.5 sruva-kamaṇḍalu-tulā-toda-yuga-lāṅgalādi-varṇa-cihnāni prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
[*783] 1946 edition: bráhmá; 1984 edition: bráhmā́
children.translated_text: (8.1.11.1) '<s>Brahmā</s>, [first] of the gods — I install the whirl (<s>āvarta</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.11.2) 'Abundant, at the end and beginning — I install the mace (<s>gadā</s>), discus (<s>cakra</s>), sword (<s>asi</s>), and arrows (<s>śara</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.11.3) 'May that glory [be ours]... I install the conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), bow (<s>Śārṅga</s>), and shield (<s>kheṭaka</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.11.4) '<s>Brahman</s>, the inner self of <s>Brahman</s>, the inner self purified by <s>Brahman</s>, established in <s>Brahman</s>, protected by <s>Brahman</s> — I am protected.' (8.1.11.5) 'I install the sacrificial ladle (<s>sruva</s>), water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>), balance (<s>tulā</s>), goad (<s>toda</s>), yoke (<s>yuga</s>), plough (<s>lāṅgala</s>), and other emblematic marks (<s>varṇa-cihna</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.'

children.text:
8.1.12.1 yé te śatám méghá-vídyúl-lā́ṃchánáṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.12.2 śriyé jātáḥ śrī́-rū́páṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.12.3 medínī devī́ háríṇī́-rū́páṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námaḥ
8.1.12.4 áto devā́
8.1.12.5 óṃ kánikradaj januṣam
8.1.12.6 prá tád víṣṇuḥ
8.1.12.7 víṣṇór nú kam ā́ tvāhārṣam ékākṣara(g)ṃ sahásra-śīrṣā púruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: (8.1.12.1) 'Your hundred... I install the cloud-lightning mark (<s>megha-vidyul-lāñchana</s>), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.12.2) 'Born for glory (<s>Śrī</s>)... I install the form of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.12.3) '<s>Medinī</s> the goddess... I install the form of <s>Hariṇī</s> (the golden one), <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.12.4) '<s>Ato devā</s>...' (8.1.12.5) '<s>Oṃ</s>, <s>kanikradaj januṣam</s>...' (8.1.12.6) '<s>Pra tad Viṣṇuḥ</s>...' (8.1.12.7) '<s>Viṣṇor nu kam</s>... I have brought you here. The single syllable (<s>ekākṣara</s>). The thousand-headed <s>Puruṣa</s>.'

children.text:
8.1.13.1 víṣṇor nú kam áto devā́ idáṃ víṣṇus trī́ṇi padā́ víṣṇoḥ kármāṇi tád víṣṇoḥ paramáṃ tád víprāsaḥ
8.1.13.2 súvar bhúvar bhū́ḥ
8.1.13.3 yáṃ áṃ[*784] óṃ
8.1.13.4 ékākṣaram aṃ ām
8.1.13.5 ā́tmātmā páramāntarātmā́
8.1.13.6 idáṃ víṣṇuḥ
8.1.13.7 ā́yā́tú bhágávā́n
8.1.13.8 víṣṇúm ā́vāhayāmi
8.1.13.9 śrī́ṃ óm
8.1.13.10 śriyé jātáḥ ā́yā́tú bhágávátī́
8.1.13.11 śríyam ā́vāhayāmi laṃ om
8.1.13.12 medínī devī́
8.1.13.13 ā́yā́tú bhágávátī́ háríṇīm ā́vāhayāmi
[*784] 1946 edition: āṃ
children.translated_text: (8.1.13.1) '<s>Viṣṇor nu kam</s>; <s>ato devā</s>; this <s>Viṣṇu</s>; three steps; the deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; that supreme [abode] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; that the inspired ones...' (8.1.13.2) '<s>Suvar</s>, <s>Bhuvar</s>, <s>Bhūḥ</s>.' (8.1.13.3) '<s>Yaṃ</s>, <s>Aṃ</s>, <s>Oṃ</s>.' (8.1.13.4) 'The single syllable: <s>Aṃ</s>, <s>Ām</s>.' (8.1.13.5) 'The Self, the Self, the Supreme Inner Self.' (8.1.13.6) 'This <s>Viṣṇu</s>...' (8.1.13.7) 'May the Blessed Lord come.' (8.1.13.8) 'I invoke <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' (8.1.13.9) '<s>Śrīṃ Oṃ</s>.' (8.1.13.10) 'Born for glory... May the Blessed Goddess come.' (8.1.13.11) 'I invoke <s>Śrī</s>. <s>Laṃ Oṃ</s>.' (8.1.13.12) '<s>Medinī</s> the goddess...' (8.1.13.13) 'May the Blessed Goddess come. I invoke <s>Hariṇī</s>.'

children.text: 8.0.1 brahmá devā́nāṃ námaḥ prátiṣṭhapáyāmy óṃ námo 'stu bhū́tyai práṇayantaṃ marútaḥ paramātmā́ prátiṣṭhāpayāmy óṃ námo námas sáñcāri bhavódbhavas tán mā yaśo 'gré námaḥ púruṣa ó(g)ṃ saptá ca
children.translated_text: (8.0.1) [Rubric:] '<s>Brahmā</s>, of the gods, <s>namaḥ</s>; I install, <s>Oṃ namo</s> 'stu; for prosperity; directing, the <s>Maruts</s>; the Supreme Self; I install, <s>Oṃ namo namaḥ</s>; the wandering one, born of existence; may that glory; <s>namaḥ</s>; <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Oṃ</s>' — and seven [mantras].

children.text:
8.1.14.1 úd vayáṃ támasa úd u tyáṃ jātá-vedaśam
8.1.14.2 prá tád víṣṇuḥ
8.1.14.3 vímā́naṃ prápadye
8.1.14.4 víṣṇu-mayaṃ prápadye
8.1.14.5 dévāvāsaṃ prápadye
8.1.14.6 vaíkuṇṭhodbhavaṃ prápadye
8.1.14.7 máṇíkaṃ prápadye
8.1.14.8 máhā́-bálaṃ prápadye
8.1.14.9 vímálaṃ prápadye
8.1.14.10 dvā́ra-pālakaṃ prápadye
children.translated_text: (8.1.14.1) 'We rise from the darkness...' (8.1.14.2) '<s>Ud u tyaṃ Jātavedasam</s>...' (8.1.14.2) '<s>Pra tad Viṣṇuḥ</s>...' (8.1.14.3) 'I take refuge in the celestial vehicle (<s>vimāna</s>).' (8.1.14.4) 'I take refuge in that which is made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' (8.1.14.5) 'I take refuge in the abode of the gods (<s>devāvāsa</s>).' (8.1.14.6) 'I take refuge in that born of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.' (8.1.14.7) 'I take refuge in the jewel (<s>maṇika</s>).' (8.1.14.8) 'I take refuge in the great strength (<s>mahā-bala</s>).' (8.1.14.9) 'I take refuge in the pure one (<s>vimala</s>).' (8.1.14.10) 'I take refuge in the door-guardian (<s>dvāra-pālaka</s>).'

children.text:
8.1.15.1 nírasta(g)ṃ rákṣo nírasto 'ghá-śá(g)ṃso nírastā árātayaḥ
8.1.15.2 sá-sómā devā́ rakṣadhvam
8.1.15.3 híraṇya-pā́ṇím ūtáye savitā́ram úpa hvaye
sá céttā devátā padám
8.1.15.4 diváṃ vívr̥ṇotu diví svargáṃ pihita-dvāráṃ vívr̥notu
8.1.15.5 dívy antárikṣe devátānā(g)ṃ sāpsaró-gaṇam abhídarśayatām
8.1.15.6 bhúvaṅgāya námaḥ
8.1.15.7 áto devā́ idáṃ víṣṇus trī́ṇi padā́ víṣṇoḥ kármāṇi tád víṣṇoḥ paramáṃ padá(g)ṃ tad víprāsaḥ
8.1.15.8 úddīpyasva jātavedo 'paghnáṃ nírr̥tiṃ máma
paśū́(g)ṃś ca máhyam ā́vaha jī́vanañ ca díśodiśa
children.translated_text: (8.1.15.1) 'Cast away is the demon (<s>rakṣas</s>), cast away is the evil-speaker, cast away are the enemies.' (8.1.15.2) 'O gods with <s>Soma</s>, protect us.' (8.1.15.3) 'I call upon <s>Savitṛ</s>, the golden-handed one, for protection. He is the perceiver of the divine station.' (8.1.15.4) 'May he open heaven; may he open in heaven the celestial realm whose door is closed.' (8.1.15.5) 'In the divine atmosphere, may they reveal the host of <s>Apsaras</s> among the gods.' (8.1.15.6) 'To the serpent (<s>Bhujaṅga</s>), <s>namaḥ</s>.' (8.1.15.7) '<s>Ato devā</s>; this <s>Viṣṇu</s>; three steps; the deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; that the inspired ones...' (8.1.15.8) 'Blaze forth, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, destroying my <s>Nirṛti</s> (misfortune). Bring me cattle and livelihood, and grant life in every direction.'

children.text:
8.1.16.1 śā́myantú ghorāṇi
8.1.16.2 śā́myantú pāpāni
8.1.16.3 śā́myantú ītayaḥ
8.1.16.4 bhágávató bálena bhagavató vī́ryeṇa bhagavatás téjasā[*785] bhagavatáḥ kármaṇā
8.1.16.5 bhágávatā́nugr̥hīto bhagavatā́nuddhyāto bhagavad dhyā́tvā[*786] bhagavat-kárma kariṣyāmi tád bhagavā́n ánumanyatām
8.1.16.6 nárya-prajā́ṃ me gopāya
8.1.16.7 amr̥tatvā́ya jīváse
jātā́ṃ janiṣyámāṇāñ ca
amŕ̥te satyé prátiṣṭhitām
8.1.16.8 átharva pitúṃ me gopāya
rásam ánnam ihā́yuṣe[*787]
[*785] Text: tséjasā
[*786] 1984 edition: bhagavaṃ ddhyā́tvā; 1926, 1946 eds.: bhagavad dhyā́tvā
[*787] VMP divides this verse making the second line the first line of chapter 17. The numbering is adjusted so that the complete verse comes at the end of chapter 16.
children.translated_text: (8.1.16.1) 'May the terrible things be pacified.' (8.1.16.2) 'May the sins be pacified.' (8.1.16.3) 'May the calamities be pacified.' (8.1.16.4) 'By the strength of the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavat</s>), by the valor of the Blessed One, by the radiance of the Blessed One, by the action of the Blessed One.' (8.1.16.5) 'Favored by the Blessed One, contemplated by the Blessed One, having meditated on the Blessed One — I shall perform the work of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One approve of that.' (8.1.16.6) 'Protect for me my human progeny.' (8.1.16.7) 'For the sake of immortality, for living — [protect] the born and those yet to be born, established in the immortal and the true.' (8.1.16.8) 'O <s>Atharvan</s>, protect for me my nourishment — the essence, the food, here for [this] lifespan.'

children.text:
8.1.17.1 ádabdhāyó 'śītano
8.1.17.2 áviṣan naḥ pitúṃ kr̥ṇu
8.1.17.3 śá(gg)ṃsya paśū́n me gopāya
8.1.17.4 dvi-pā́do yé cátuṣ-padaḥ
aṣṭā́ śaphāś ca yá ihā́gne ye caika-śaphā āśu-gā́ḥ[*788]
8.1.17.5 sá-pratha sabhā́ṃ me gopāya
8.1.17.6 yé ca sábhyās sábhā-sádaḥ
tā́n indriyā́vataḥ kuru
[*788] 1946 edition: aśu-gā́ḥ
children.translated_text: (8.1.17.1) 'O undecaying, cool one...' (8.1.17.2) 'Without poison, provide nourishment for us.' (8.1.17.3) 'O praiseworthy one, protect for me my cattle.' (8.1.17.4) 'The two-footed and the four-footed, the eight-hoofed and those here, O <s>Agni</s>, and the single-hoofed swift ones.' (8.1.17.5) 'O spacious one, protect for me my assembly (<s>sabhā</s>).' (8.1.17.6) 'Those who are courtiers and assembly-members — make them endowed with power.'

children.text:
8.1.18.1 sárvam ā́yur úpāsatām
8.1.18.2 áhe budhniya mántram me gopāya
yám ŕ̥ṣayas traividā́ vidúḥ
ŕ̥cas sāmāni yájū́(g)ṃṣi
8.1.18.3 sā́ hí[*789] śrī́r amŕ̥tā satā́m
8.1.18.4 mā́ no hi(g)ṃsīj jātavedo gā́m áśvaṃ púruṣaṃ jágat
ábibhrad ágna ā́gahi śriyā́ mā páripātaya
8.1.18.5 samrā́jaṃ ca virā́jaṃ cābhi śrī́r yā́ ca no gr̥hé
lakṣmī́ rāṣṭrásya yā́ múkhe táyā
mā sá(g)ṃ sr̥jāmasi
[*789] VMP text: hiś; TB: hi
children.translated_text: (8.1.18.1) 'May they attend upon the full lifespan.' (8.1.18.2) 'O <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> (Serpent of the Deep), protect for me my <s>mantra</s> — which the thrice-knowing <s>Ṛṣis</s> know: the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, the <s>Sāman</s> chants, and the <s>Yajus</s> formulas.' (8.1.18.3) 'For she is <s>Śrī</s>, the immortal one of the virtuous.' (8.1.18.4) 'Do not harm us, O <s>Jātavedas</s> — the cow, the horse, the man, the world. Come bearing [blessings], O <s>Agni</s>; protect me all around with prosperity.' (8.1.18.5) 'The sovereign and the shining one, and the <s>Śrī</s> that is in our house — <s>Lakṣmī</s> who is at the face of the kingdom — with her may we be united.'

children.text:
8.1.19.1 índrasya tvā́ vájreṇābhy úpa viśāmi
váha kāle váha śríyaṃ mābhivaha[*790]
8.1.19.2 áśvo 'si háyo 'sy áto 'si náro 'sy árvāsi sáptir asi
vā́jy asi vŕ̥ṣāsi nr̥máṇā asi yáyur nā́māsy ādityā́nāṃ pátvā́nvihi
8.1.19.3 ā́-go-dā́nāt páṭhed idám
8.1.19.4 devásya tvā bráhma jajñāná(g)ṃ
8.1.19.5 híraṇya-garbháḥ
8.1.19.6 bhū́ḥ prápadye bhúvaḥ prápadye súvaḥ prápadye bhū́r bhúvas súvaḥ prápadye virā́jamānaṃ tám ajaṃ prápadye
8.1.19.7 téjo-mayaṃ téjasām ápy agámya(g)ṃ sárvātmā́naṃ támasaḥ pā́rabhūtaṃ bhūtyā́ viśváṃ pāti yás táṃ prápadye
8.1.19.8 víṣṇuṃ prápadye
8.1.19.9 púrúṣaṃ prápadye
[*790] Text: mābhīrvaha
children.translated_text: (8.1.19.1) 'By the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) of <s>Indra</s>, I approach and sit near you. Carry in due time, carry prosperity; carry it to me.' (8.1.19.2) 'You are a horse (<s>aśva</s>), you are a steed (<s>haya</s>), you are [another] horse (<s>ata</s>), you are a man (<s>nara</s>), you are a racer (<s>arvan</s>), you are a swift one (<s>sapti</s>), you are a prize-winner (<s>vājin</s>), you are a bull (<s>vṛṣan</s>), you are delighting in men (<s>nṛmaṇas</s>), <s>Yayu</s> is your name — follow the path of the <s>Ādityas</s>.' (8.1.19.3) 'One should recite this up to the giving of cows (<s>go-dāna</s>).' (8.1.19.4) 'Of the god — <s>Brahman</s> was born...' (8.1.19.5) '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>...' (8.1.19.6) 'I take refuge in <s>Bhūḥ</s>; I take refuge in <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>; I take refuge in <s>Suvaḥ</s>; I take refuge in <s>Bhūr Bhuvas Suvaḥ</s>; I take refuge in the shining, unborn one.' (8.1.19.7) 'He who is made of radiance, having reached the radiance of radiances, the Self of all, who has transcended darkness — who protects the universe with prosperity — I take refuge in him.' (8.1.19.8) 'I take refuge in <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' (8.1.19.9) 'I take refuge in <s>Puruṣa</s>.'

children.text:
8.1.20.1 sátyaṃ prápadye
8.1.20.2 ácyútaṃ prápadye
8.1.20.3 ánírúddhaṃ prápadye
8.1.20.4 váraṃ raṃha ā́sthāsye gā́rudaṃ raṃhaṃ ā́sthāsye gā́rútmaṃtaṃ ráṃha ā́sthāsye
8.1.20.5 sárvaṃ sarvaṃ ráṃho vaiṣṇavám aham ā́sthāsye
8.1.20.6 bhū́r asi bhū́ḥ prátiṣṭhityai
8.1.20.7 bhúvo 'si bhúvaḥ prátiṣṭhityai
8.1.20.8 súvar asi súvaḥ prátiṣṭhityai
8.1.20.9 bhū́r bhúvas súvar asi súvaḥ prátiṣṭhityai
8.1.20.10 sānandás sárveṣām antarātmā́ bhava
children.translated_text: (8.1.20.1) 'I take refuge in <s>Satya</s> (Truth).' (8.1.20.2) 'I take refuge in <s>Acyuta</s> (the Unfallen).' (8.1.20.3) 'I take refuge in <s>Aniruddha</s> (the Unobstructed).' (8.1.20.4) 'I shall mount the best speed; I shall mount the speed of <s>Garuḍa</s>; I shall mount the speed of <s>Garutmat</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>).' (8.1.20.5) 'I shall mount all, all the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> speed.' (8.1.20.6) 'You are <s>Bhūḥ</s> — for the establishment of <s>Bhūḥ</s>.' (8.1.20.7) 'You are <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> — for the establishment of <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>.' (8.1.20.8) 'You are <s>Suvaḥ</s> — for the establishment of <s>Suvaḥ</s>.' (8.1.20.9) 'You are <s>Bhūr Bhuvas Suvaḥ</s> — for the establishment of <s>Suvaḥ</s>.' (8.1.20.10) 'Be the blissful inner self of all.'

children.text:
8.1.21.1 pūtáḥ pū́tāntarātmā́ bhava
8.1.21.2 puṇyáḥ púṇyāntarātmā́ bhava
8.1.21.3 brahmá bráhmāntarātmā́ bhava
8.1.21.4 víṣṇúṃ prátiṣṭhāpayāmí
8.1.21.5 ávadhūta(g)ṃ rákṣó 'vadhūtā árātayaḥ
8.1.21.6 ávadhūtas so 'stu yo 'smān dveṣṭi yáñ ca vayáṃ dviṣmáḥ
8.1.21.7 ā́śā́sú sáptásv ápí kañja-rekhā ā́pas samagrā́s samudā́vahāmi
8.1.21.8 sómā́gní-sū́ryā́mŕ̥tá-puṣkarīṇā́m āpas samāvā́hya púras-kariṣye
8.1.21.9 sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānaṃ váruṇam agním anvā́rabhāmahe
ādityā́n víṣṇu(g)ṃ sū́ryaṃ brahmā́ṇaṃ ca bŕ̥haspátim
children.translated_text: (8.1.21.1) 'Be pure, be the pure inner self.' (8.1.21.2) 'Be meritorious, be the meritorious inner self.' (8.1.21.3) 'Be <s>Brahman</s>, be the inner self of <s>Brahman</s>.' (8.1.21.4) 'I install <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' (8.1.21.5) 'Shaken off is the demon (<s>rakṣas</s>), shaken off are the enemies.' (8.1.21.6) 'May he be shaken off who hates us, and whom we hate.' (8.1.21.7) 'In the seven directions, with lotus-lines, I gather together all the waters.' (8.1.21.8) 'Having gathered the waters of the <s>Soma</s>-pool, <s>Agni</s>-pool, <s>Sūrya</s>-pool, and <s>Amṛta</s>-pool (<s>puṣkariṇī</s>), I shall make [them] the foremost.' (8.1.21.9) 'We invoke King <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.'

children.text:
8.1.22.1 ā́ mā vā́jasya śúcī vo havyā́
8.1.22.2 duhatā́n dívam índras savitemā́ṃ duhatā́ṃ medínīm
8.1.22.3 tád ubháyaṃ prajānā́ṃ nírītaye nírudvegāya
8.1.22.4 jāhnavī́ṃ loka-pāvánīm
8.1.22.5 imáṃ me gaṅge yamune sarasvati śútudri stómá(g)ṃ sacatā páruṣṇíyā́
asikniyā́ marudvr̥dhe vitástayā́rjīkīye śr̥ṇuhyā́ suṣómayā
8.1.22.6 ā́dyam abhígr̥hṇāmi śrīman-nārāyaṇa-caraṇau śaraṇaṃ prapadye śrī́máté nā́rāyaṇāya námaḥ
8.1.22.7 tátth savitúr váreṇyam
children.translated_text:
Bring me the pure oblations of <s>vāja</s> (nourishment)!
May <s>Indra</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s> milk heaven; may they milk this earth;
that is for the benefit of both [classes of] offspring, for freedom from distress, for freedom from agitation.
To <s>Jāhnavī</s> (the Ganges), the purifier of the world.
O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O <s>Yamunā</s>, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, O <s>Śutudri</s>, attend to this hymn of praise, O <s>Paruṣṇī</s>,
O <s>Asiknī</s>, O <s>Marudvṛdhā</s>, O <s>Vitastā</s>, O <s>Ārjīkīyā</s>, hear, O <s>Suṣomā</s>!
First I take hold [of the offering]; I take refuge at the feet of <s>Śrīman Nārāyaṇa</s>; homage to the glorious <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!
That of <s>Savitṛ</s>, the most excellent —

children.text:
8.1.23.1 arvā́ñcam índram
8.1.23.2 svastí no mimītāṃ kánikradaj janúṣam
8.1.23.3 sóma(g)ṃ rā́jānam ídam ā́paś śivā́ḥ
8.1.23.4 bhágávató balena
8.1.23.5 náśyanti jágatām ītáyo nírastaḥ parāvásus[*791] saha pāpmánā
8.1.23.6 ahám evédáṃ kariṣyāmi vibhóḥ kartúṃ nidhāsyati
8.1.23.7 káriṣyāmy átra yát kíñcit[*792] tán me devó ínumanyatām
8.1.23.8 pūtás tasya
8.1.23.9 óṃ bhū́r bhúvas súvaḥ
8.1.23.10 nārāyaṇā́ya
[*791] According to MW, p. 590, parāvásu is a name “of a Gandharva (associated with Viśvavasu)”.
[*792] 1984 edition: yátíñcat; 1946 edition: yátíñcit
children.translated_text:
<s>Indra</s>, turned toward us;
may he who neighs at birth measure out well-being for us;
King <s>Soma</s>, these auspicious waters;
by the power of the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavat</s>),
the afflictions of the world perish; <s>Parāvasu</s> is cast out together with sin.
I myself shall do this; the all-pervading one will set it in place.
Whatever I shall do here, may the <s>deva</s> (god) approve of that for me.
Purified is his.
<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvaḥ</s> (earth, atmosphere, heaven)!
To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!

children.text:
8.1.24.1 óṃ víṣṇave námaḥ
8.1.24.2 óṃ púruṣāya námaḥ
8.1.24.3 óṃ satyā́ya námaḥ
8.1.24.4 óṃ ácyutāya námaḥ
8.1.24.5 oṃ áníruddhāya námaḥ
8.1.24.6 udyántaṃ vā́vā́dityám agnír ánusamā́rohati
8.1.24.7 tásmād dhūmá evā́gnér dívā dadr̥śe
8.1.24.8 bhū́r anílayā bhū́tayā bhū́tayā páriṣiñcāmi bhúvas suṣumnáyā prāṇávatyā páriṣiñcāmi svár amŕ̥távatyā jyótiṣmatyā ca páriṣiñcāmi
8.1.24.9 tā́(g)ṃ savitúr váreṇyasya citrā́m aháṃ[*793] vr̥ṇe sumatíṃ viśvá-janyāṃ yā́m asya káṇvo áduhat[*794] prápīnā(g)ṃ sahásra-dhārāṃ páyasā mahī́ṃ gā́m
8.1.24.10 ā́gneyó yásmāt praíṣām adhīśáḥ
[*793] 1984 edition: ahaṃ; 1946 edition: āhaṃ
[*794] Text: ā́duhat
children.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Cosmic Person)!
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Satya</s> (Truth)!
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable)!
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Aniruddha</s> (the Irresistible)!
<s>Agni</s> (Fire) follows the rising sun (<s>Āditya</s>).
Therefore only the smoke of <s>Agni</s> is seen during the day.
<s>Bhūḥ</s> — with the unstirring one, with prosperity, with prosperity, I sprinkle; <s>bhuvaḥ</s> — with <s>Suṣumṇā</s>, with <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), I sprinkle; <s>svaḥ</s> — with the immortal one, with the luminous one, I sprinkle.
That splendid [gift] of excellent <s>Savitṛ</s>, I choose — the universal benevolence, which <s>Kaṇva</s> milked for him, the great cow, swollen, of a thousand streams, [flowing] with milk.
Because of <s>Agni</s>, since he is the lord of commands.

children.text:
8.1.25.1 víṣvak-senaṃ prápadye
8.1.25.2 śā́ntaṃ prápadye
8.1.25.3 háraṃ prápadye
8.1.25.4 ámítaṃ prápadye
8.1.25.5 sū́travatīṃ prápadye
8.1.25.6 jayā́ṃ prápadye
8.1.25.7 mā́rkaṇḍeyāya námaḥ
8.1.25.8 bhr̥gáve námaḥ
8.1.25.9 bráhmaṇe námaḥ
8.1.25.10 śáṅkarāya námaḥ
8.1.26.1 sū́ryā́ya námaḥ
8.1.26.2 sómā́ya námaḥ
8.1.26.3 áṅgārakāya námaḥ
8.1.26.4 saúmyā́ya námaḥ
8.1.26.5 bŕ̥haspátaye námaḥ
8.1.26.6 bhā́rgavāya námaḥ
8.1.26.7 sauráye námaḥ
8.1.26.8 rā́have námaḥ
8.1.26.9 kétáve námaḥ
8.1.26.10 dhā́tre námaḥ
children.translated_text:
I take refuge in <s>Viṣvaksena</s> (the All-pervading)!
I take refuge in the Peaceful One (<s>Śānta</s>)!
I take refuge in <s>Hara</s> (the Remover)!
I take refuge in the Boundless One (<s>Amita</s>)!
I take refuge in <s>Sūtravatī</s> (the Thread-bearer)!
I take refuge in <s>Jayā</s> (Victory)!
Homage to <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>!
Homage to <s>Bhṛgu</s>!
Homage to <s>Brahman</s>!
Homage to <s>Śaṅkara</s>!
Homage to <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun)!
Homage to <s>Soma</s> (the Moon)!
Homage to <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars)!
Homage to <s>Saumya</s> (Mercury)!
Homage to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter)!
Homage to <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus)!
Homage to <s>Sauri</s> (Saturn)!
Homage to <s>Rāhu</s>!
Homage to <s>Ketu</s>!
Homage to <s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator)!

children.text:
8.1.27.1 vídhā́tre námaḥ
8.1.27.2 bhúvaṅgāya námaḥ
8.1.27.3 pátáṅgāya námaḥ
8.1.27.4 pátírā́ya námaḥ
8.1.27.5 váráṇā́ya námaḥ
8.1.27.6 dharmā́ya námaḥ
8.1.27.7 jñā́nā́ya námaḥ
8.1.27.8 aiśvaryā́ya námaḥ
8.1.27.9 gájá-lakṣmyai námaḥ
8.1.27.10 maṇikā́ya námaḥ
children.translated_text:
Homage to <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Ordainer)!
Homage to <s>Bhuvaṅga</s> (the Serpent)!
Homage to <s>Pataṅga</s> (the Bird/Sun)!
Homage to <s>Patīra</s>!
Homage to <s>Varaṇa</s>!
Homage to <s>Dharma</s> (Righteousness)!
Homage to <s>Jñāna</s> (Knowledge)!
Homage to <s>Aiśvarya</s> (Sovereignty)!
Homage to <s>Gaja-Lakṣmī</s> (Elephant-<s>Lakṣmī</s>)!
Homage to <s>Maṇika</s>!

children.text:
8.1.28.1 sandhyā́yai námaḥ
8.1.28.2 nyakṣyā́ya námaḥ
8.1.28.3 indrā́ya námaḥ
8.1.28.4 tā́pasāya námaḥ
8.1.28.5 siddhidā́ya námaḥ
8.1.28.6 kíṣkindhāya námaḥ
8.1.28.7 tīrthā́ya námaḥ
8.1.28.8 nā́ga-rājāya námaḥ
8.1.28.9 gaṇeśā́ya námaḥ
8.1.28.10 śáṅkha-nidhaye námaḥ
children.translated_text:
Homage to <s>Sandhyā</s> (Twilight)!
Homage to <s>Nyakṣya</s>!
Homage to <s>Indra</s>!
Homage to the Ascetic (<s>Tāpasa</s>)!
Homage to the Bestower of <s>Siddhi</s> (Perfection)!
Homage to <s>Kiṣkindha</s>!
Homage to <s>Tīrtha</s> (the Sacred Ford)!
Homage to <s>Nāga-rāja</s> (the Serpent King)!
Homage to <s>Gaṇeśa</s> (Lord of the Hosts)!
Homage to <s>Śaṅkha-nidhi</s> (the Conch Treasure)!

children.text:
8.1.29.1 pádma-nidhaye námaḥ
8.1.29.2 tuhiṇā́ya námaḥ
8.1.29.3 balindā́ya námaḥ
8.1.29.4 khaḍgā́ya námaḥ
8.1.29.5 śārṅgā́ya námaḥ
8.1.29.6 śáṅkha-cūliṇe[*795] námaḥ
8.1.29.7 cákra-cūliṇe[*796] námaḥ
8.1.29.8 caṇḍā́ya námaḥ
8.1.29.9 prácaṇḍāya námaḥ
8.1.29.10 śrī-bhūtā́ya námaḥ
[*795] Text: cūḷiṇe
[*796] Text: cūḷiṇe
children.translated_text:
Homage to <s>Padma-nidhi</s> (the Lotus Treasure)!
Homage to <s>Tuhiṇa</s> (the Cold One/Snow)!
Homage to <s>Balinda</s>!
Homage to <s>Khaḍga</s> (the Sword)!
Homage to <s>Śārṅga</s> (the Bow)!
Homage to <s>Śaṅkha-cūlin</s> (the Conch-crested One)!
Homage to <s>Cakra-cūlin</s> (the Discus-crested One)!
Homage to <s>Caṇḍa</s> (the Fierce One)!
Homage to <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> (the Exceedingly Fierce One)!
Homage to <s>Śrī-bhūta</s> (the Auspicious Being)!

children.text:

children.translated_text: (8.1.41.1) <s>Agni</s>, most devoted to purity, pure, the inspired poet, pure, the seer — pure, he shines when offered into; O <s>Agni</s>, your pure [flames] rise up — your bright lights, your rays, blaze forth. (8.1.41.2) 'That excellent [glory] of <s>Savitṛ</s>...' [<s>Gāyatrī</s> incipit]. (8.1.41.3) 'In the seven streams...' (8.1.41.4) 'These waters, auspicious...' (8.1.41.5) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>...' (8.1.41.6) 'I take refuge in <s>Bhūḥ</s> (Earth)...' (8.1.41.7) 'For the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, whose refuge is <s>Acyuta</s> (the Unfallen), firmly established in intense austerity, the seer of <s>Brahman</s>.' [Editorial note: VMP divides the verse, placing the second line at the start of chapter 42.]

children.text:
8.1.42.1 dhanur-dharā́yai[*801] vidmáhe sarva-siddhyaí ca dhīmahi
tán no dharā pracodáyāt

8.1.42.3 bhū́r bhúvas súvar óm

[*801] 1946 edition: -tharāyai; 1984 edition: -tharāya
children.translated_text: (8.1.42.1) We know [you who hold] the bow (<s>Dhanuṣ-dharā</s>); we meditate upon [you] for the attainment of all perfections (<s>sarva-siddhi</s>) — may that Supporter (<s>Dharā</s>) inspire us. (8.1.42.2) To [her who is] the remover of all beings [i.e., all evil], <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! (8.1.42.3) <s>Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Suvaḥ Oṃ</s>. (8.1.42.4) Obeisance to the supporting power (<s>Ādhāra-śakti</s>). (8.1.42.5) Obeisance to the endless seat (<s>Anantāsana</s>). (8.1.42.6) Obeisance to the tortoise seat (<s>Kūrmāsana</s>). (8.1.42.7) Obeisance to the pure seat (<s>Vimalāsana</s>). (8.1.42.8) Obeisance to the lotus seat (<s>Padmāsana</s>). [Editorial note: variant readings across editions.]

8.1.44.6 ó(g)ṃ satyám
8.1.44.7 óṃ táth savitúr váreṇyaṃ bhárgo devásya dhīmahi
dhíyo yó naḥ pracodáyāt
8.1.44.8 óm ā́po jyótī ráso 'mŕ̥taṃ bráhma bhū́r bhúvas súvar óm
8.1.44.9 bhū́mer vítanván prátaran prakāmáḥ pópūyamānáḥ páñcabhis svá-guṇaiḥ prasannais sárvāṇi mā́n dhārayiṣyasi svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.44.1) <s>Oṃ Bhuvaḥ</s>! (8.1.44.2) <s>Oṃ Suvaḥ</s>! (8.1.44.3) <s>Oṃ Mahaḥ</s>! (8.1.44.4) <s>Oṃ Janaḥ</s>! (8.1.44.5) <s>Oṃ Tapaḥ</s>! (8.1.44.6) <s>Oṃ Satyam</s>! (8.1.44.7) <s>Oṃ</s> — we meditate upon that excellent glory of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>; may he inspire our intellects [<s>Gāyatrī mantra</s>]. (8.1.44.8) <s>Oṃ</s> — waters, light, essence, immortality, <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Suvaḥ Oṃ</s>! (8.1.44.9) Extending the crevices of the earth, the principal one, growing ever greater, with five serene qualities of his own — you shall support all of me, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
8.1.45.1 pŕ̥thivyaí húṃ phaṭ svāhā́
8.1.45.2 apsú pr̥thívī́ṃ právílāpayāmí
8.1.45.3 aniruddha-mūrtíṃ dhyā́yā́mi
8.1.45.4 tváṃ jī́vas tvám ā́pas sárveṣāṃ janitā́ tvam ā́hāraḥ
tváṃ víṣṇo śramā́pánudāya cátur-guṇāya svā́hā
8.1.45.5 amr̥tā́ya húṃ phaṭ svāhā́
8.1.45.6 agnā́v apáh právílāpayāmi
8.1.45.7 acyuta-mūrtíṃ dhyāyāmi
8.1.45.8 tvám agne trí-guṇo variṣṭháḥ páraṃ brahma páraṃ jyótiḥ
sárveṣāṃ tváṃ pā́lanāya hutám amŕ̥táṃ vahiṣyase svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.45.1) To <s>Pr̥thivī</s> (Earth), <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! (8.1.45.2) I dissolve the earth into the waters. (8.1.45.3) I meditate upon the <s>Aniruddha</s> (Unobstructed) form [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. (8.1.45.4) You are the life-force (<s>jīva</s>), you are the waters — the begetter of all, you are nourishment; O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, fourfold, for the removal of fatigue, <s>svāhā</s>! (8.1.45.5) To the immortal (<s>Amr̥ta</s>), <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! (8.1.45.6) I dissolve the waters into fire. (8.1.45.7) I meditate upon the <s>Acyuta</s> (Unfailing) form [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. (8.1.45.8) You are <s>Agni</s> (fire), threefold, the greatest, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme light — for the protection of all, you shall carry the offered immortal [substance], <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
8.1.46.1 agnáyé húṃ phaṭ svāhā́
8.1.46.2 vāyā́v agníṃ právílāpayāmí
8.1.46.3 satya-mūrtíṃ dhyāyāmí
8.1.46.4 yó vā vā́yur dví-guṇo 'ntarātmā́ sárveṣām antáś caratīhá víṣṇo
sa tvaṃ devā́n manuṣyān mr̥tān párisaṃjīvase svā́hā
8.1.46.5 vāyávé húṃ phaṭ svāhā́
8.1.46.6 ā́kā́śé vāyúṃ právílāpayāmí
8.1.46.7 puruṣa-mūrtíṃ dhyāyāmí
8.1.46.8 yó vā gáviṣṭhaḥ páramaḥ pradhānáḥ[*802] padáṃ vā yásya satvám āsīt
yásyopáritvaṃ múnayo 'núpaśyanti tásmai mukhyā́ya víṣṇave svā́hā[*803]
[*802] Text: prathānáḥ
[*803] VMP divides this verse making the second line the first line of chapter 47. The numbering is adjusted so that the complete verse comes at the end of chapter 46.
children.translated_text: (8.1.46.1) To <s>Agni</s>, <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! (8.1.46.2) I dissolve fire into wind. (8.1.46.3) I meditate upon the <s>Satya</s> (Truth) form [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. (8.1.46.4) He who as <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), twofold, is the inner self of all, moving within all here — O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, you who revive the gods, men, and the dead, <s>svāhā</s>!
