To everything, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: 8.0.25 vyānā́ya svā́hā nivekṣyaté svā́hā nipádyamānāya svā́hā suptā́ya svā́hā vīkṣiṣyaté svā́hottíṣṭhate svā́hā caṅkramitā́ya svā́hā karóti tásmai svā́hā catvā́ri ca
children.translated_text: To the diffused breath, <s>svāhā</s>; to the one about to enter, <s>svāhā</s>; to the one lying down, <s>svāhā</s>; to the one who has fallen asleep, <s>svāhā</s>; to the one about to look, <s>svāhā</s>; to the one standing up, <s>svāhā</s>; to the one who has paced about, <s>svāhā</s>; to what he does, <s>svāhā</s> — and [these are] four.

children.text:
8.1.173.1 ā́-go-dā́nāt páṭhed idáṃ brāhmīyáṃ bráhma-nirmitam
sūktáṃ tát pāramātmíkam ātmā́ devā́nām ájaro 'mareśaḥ[*911]
8.1.173.2 sáṃphullāgré puṇḍarīké níviṣṭas tālā́rdhā́yā́mó[*912] rakta-netráḥ
śaṅkhá-spháṭíká-saṅkāśás téṣā́ṃ dévā́nā́m antar āsī́d antarātmā́
8.1.173.3 ajitó devó yakṣā́ṇāṃ vidyā́dharāṇā́ṃ gandharvāṇā́m antarātmā́ brahmaṇaś cāntarātmā́
brāhmīkó raudriká udānakás sa manuṣyā́ṇāṃ raukmó rukmó vā
8.1.173.4 áṅgúṣṭhá-mā́tró hŕ̥dáyé sanniviṣṭás tásthúṣā́m antarātmā́
agnír ā́viṣṭo yád rūpáṃ tásya pravā́ asi sá jīva ity abhíśasyate
[*911] Full verse for pratīka ā-go-dānāt. Note full verse comes after, not before, the pratīka.
[*912] Text: tālā́rthā́yā́mó
children.translated_text: 8.1.173.1 'One should recite up to the cow-gift (<s>go-dāna</s>) this <s>Brāhma</s> [hymn], created by <s>Brahman</s> — that <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) which is of the Supreme Self (<s>Pāramātmika</s>): the Self of the gods, unaging, the lord of the immortals.' 8.1.173.2 'Seated in a fully-blossomed white lotus, of the height of half a palm-tree, red-eyed, resembling conch and crystal — he was the inner Self (<s>antarātman</s>) of those gods.' 8.1.173.3 'The unconquered god — the inner Self of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, the <s>Vidyādharas</s>, the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and also the inner Self of <s>Brahman</s>; of the nature of <s>Brahmā</s>, of <s>Rudra</s>, the upward-breath — he is the golden one of humans, gold itself.' 8.1.173.4 'Of the measure of a thumb, seated in the heart — the inner Self of all that stands; when <s>Agni</s> has entered, that form of which you are the flow — he is called the living one (<s>jīva</s>).'

children.text: 8.0.26 ā́-go-dā́nāt páṭhed aṣṭaú ca
children.translated_text: 8.0.26 [Rubric:] 'One should recite up to the cow-gift...' — and eight [more mantras].

children.text:
8.1.174.1 ómāsaś carṣaṇī-dhr̥to víśve devāsa ā́ gata
dāśvā́ṃso dāśúṣas sutám
8.1.174.2 víśve devā́so aptúras sutám ā́ gaṃta tū́rṇayaḥ
usrā́ iva svásarāṇi
8.1.174.3 víśve devā́so asrídha[*913] éhi māyāso adrúhaḥ
médhaṃ juṣanta váhnayaḥ
8.1.174.4 pāvakā́ nas sárasvatī vā́jebhir vājínīvatī
yajñáṃ vaṣṭu dhiyā́vasuḥ
8.1.174.5 codayitrī́ sūnŕ̥tānāṃ cétantī sumatīnā́m
yajñáṃ dadhe sáraśvatī
8.1.174.6 mahó árṇas sárasvatī prá cetayati ketúnā
dhiyo víśvā ví rājati
[*913] RV: asrídha; MS: asridhā. Note VMP=RV, not MS.
children.translated_text: 8.1.174.1 'Helpers, sustainers of the peoples — O All-Gods, come! [Come,] givers, to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] of the worshipper.' 8.1.174.2 'O All-Gods, active ones, come quickly to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] — like dawns to their stations!' 8.1.174.3 'O All-Gods, unfailing, not deceitful, not injurious — you bearers [of oblation], delight in the sacrifice!' 8.1.174.4 'May purifying <s>Sarasvatī</s>, rich in prizes, abounding in spoils, desire our sacrifice — she who is rich in wisdom!' 8.1.174.5 'The inspirer of true songs, the awakener of good thoughts — <s>Sarasvatī</s> has sustained the sacrifice.' 8.1.174.6 '<s>Sarasvatī</s>, with her beacon, makes the great flood perceive — she illumines all thoughts.'

children.text: 8.0.27 sárasvatī dvé ca
children.translated_text: 8.0.27 [Rubric:] '<s>Sarasvatī</s>...' — and two [more mantras].

children.text:
8.1.175.1 rā́trī vy akhyad āyatī́ purutrā́ devyā 1 'kṣábhiḥ[*914]
víśvā ádhi śríyo 'dhita
8.1.175.2 órv aprā ámartyā niváto devyū1dvátaḥ
jyótiṣā bādhate támaḥ
8.1.175.3 nír u svásāram askr̥toṣásaṃ devyā́yatī́
ápéd u hāsate támaḥ
8.1.175.4 sā́ no adyá yásyā vayáṃ ní te yā́mann ávikṣmahi
vr̥kṣé ná vasatíṃ váyaḥ
8.1.175.5 ní grā́māso avikṣata ní padváṃto ní pakṣíṇaḥ
ní śyenā́saś cid arthínaḥ
[*914] RV: devy 1 kṣabhiḥ; TB: devy akṣabhiḥ
children.translated_text: 8.1.175.1 'The goddess Night (<s>Rātrī</s>) has come, looking out in many directions with her eyes — she has put on all her glories.' 8.1.175.2 'The immortal goddess has filled the wide [space], the depths and the heights — with her light she drives away the darkness.' 8.1.175.3 'The goddess, approaching, has sent away her sister <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) — the darkness too departs.' 8.1.175.4 'May she be favorable to us today — she in whose approach we have found rest, as birds [find rest] in a tree.' 8.1.175.5 'The villages have settled down, the footless creatures and the winged ones, and even the seeking hawks have settled.'

children.text:
8.1.176.1 yāváyā vr̥kyaṃ[*915] 1 vŕ̥kaṃ yaváya stenám ūrmye
áthā nas sutárā bhava
8.1.176.2 úpa mā pépiśat támaḥ kr̥ṣṇáṃ vyaktam asthita
úṣa r̥ṇéva yātaya
8.1.176.3 úpa te gā́[*916] ivā́karaṃ vr̥ṇīṣvá duhitar divaḥ
rā́tri stómaṃ ná jigyúṣe
8.1.176.4[*917] ā́ rātri pā́rthivaṃ rájaḥ pitúr aprāyi[*918] dhā́mabhiḥ
divás sádāṃsi br̥hatī́ ví tiṣṭhasa ā́ tveṣáṃ vartate támaḥ
8.1.176.5 yé te rātrī nr̥cákṣaso yuktā́so[*919] navatír náva
aśī́tis saṃtv[*920] aṣṭā́ utó te sapta sáptatīḥ
8.1.176.6 rā́trīṃ prá padye janánīṃ sarvá-bhūta-nivéśanīm
bhadrā́ṃ bhagávatīṃ kr̥ṣṇā́ṃ viśvásya jagató niśām
8.1.176.7 saṃveśinī́ṃ[*921] saṃyaminī́ṃ[*922] grahá-nakṣatra-mā́linīm
prápanno 'hám śivāṃ rātrī́ṃ bhadré pāram aśī́mahi bhadré pāram aśī́mahy óṃ námaḥ
[*915] Text: vr̥kyāṃ
[*916] VMP: vā́; RV, TB, etc: gā́
[*917] Verses 8.1.176.4-7 correspond to verses 4.2.1-4 of the R̥g Veda Khila, the “Rātrī Khila”. Verses 8.1.176.4-5 also correspond to AV 19.47.1 and 19.47.3 respectively. In Coburn's Devi Māhātmya, p. 265, he says that the sole variant between RVKh and AV is the AV's reading of draṣṭāro for yuktāso. However in Whitney's Atharva Veda Saṃhitā, vol. 2, p. 975, he indicates another variant is AV's reading of santi for santu.
[*918] VMP: pitáraḥ prā́yu; AV, RVKh: pitúr aprāyi
[*919] AV: draṣṭāro
[*920] AV: santi
[*921] RVKh: veśanī́ṃ
[*922] RVKh: saṃyamanī́ṃ
children.translated_text: 8.1.176.1 'Ward off the she-wolf and the wolf; ward off the thief, O Night! Be easy for us to cross!' 8.1.176.2 'The dark-colored darkness has come upon me, clinging closely; O <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), drive it away like debts!' 8.1.176.3 'I have driven [my praises] toward you like cattle, O Daughter of Heaven — accept this hymn, O Night, as [you accept praise] from one who would conquer!' 8.1.176.4 'O Night, the earthly expanse has been spread by the luminaries of the Father; you stand lofty in the seats of heaven — the fierce darkness rolls forth.' 8.1.176.5 'Your watchers of men, O Night, yoked [to their task] — ninety and nine, eighty also, and your seven and seventy.' 8.1.176.6 'I take refuge in Night, the mother, the one who gives rest to all beings — the auspicious, the blessed, the dark night of all the world.' 8.1.176.7 'She who causes rest, she who controls, adorned with a garland of planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> (stars) — I have surrendered to the auspicious Night; O blessed one, may we cross to the far shore! O blessed one, may we cross to the far shore! <s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>.'

children.text: 8.0.28 arthínas sáptatīś catvā́ri ca
children.translated_text: 8.0.28 [Rubric:] '...the seeking ones... seven and seventy...' — and four [more mantras].

children.text:
8.1.177.1 hiraṇya-garbhá ā́po ha yát prájāpate
8.1.177.2 sá veda putráḥ pitára(g)ṃ sá mātára(g)ṃ sá sūnúr bhuvat sá bhuvat púnar-maghaḥ
sá dyā́m aúrṇod antárikṣa(g)ṃ sá súvas sá víśvā bhúvo abhavat sá ā́ bhavat
8.1.177.3 sá pratnaván návīyasā́gne dyumnéna saṃyátā[*923]
br̥hát tatantha bhānúnā
8.1.177.4 ní kā́vyā vedhásaś[*924] śáśvatas kar háste dádhāno náryā purū́ṇi
agnír bhuvad rayipátī rayīṇā́(g)ṃ satrā́ cakrāṇó amŕ̥tāni víśvā
8.1.177.5 híraṇya-pāṇim ūtáye savitā́ram úpa hvaye sá céttā devátā padám
8.1.177.6 vāmám adyá savitar vāmám u śvó divé-dive vāmám asmábhya(g)ṃ sāvīḥ
vāmásya hí kṣáyasya deva bhū́rer ayā́ dhiyá vāma-bhā́jas syama
8.1.177.7 báḍ itthā́ párvatānāṃ khidráṃ bibharṣi pr̥thiví
prá yā́ bhūmi pravatvati mahnā́ jinóṣi mahini[*925]
[*923] The 1946 and 1984 editions of the VMP text here insert a footnote that reads: údutyáṃ citrám, which is the only part missing in an otherwise continuous quote from TS 2.2.12. Keith's translation for this pratīka (his TS 2.2.12f) is: “The radiant.”
[*924] Text: vethásaś
[*925] VMP divides this verse making the second line the first line of chapter 178. The numbering is adjusted so that the complete verse comes at the end of chapter 177.
children.translated_text: 8.1.177.1 '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>... When the waters... O <s>Prajāpati</s>...' 8.1.177.2 'He knew the father and the mother — that son; he became the creator, he became the re-giver. He covered heaven and the atmosphere, and the sun — he became all beings, he came into being.' 8.1.177.3 'As of old, with new brilliance, O <s>Agni</s>, combined — you have spread far with your radiance.' 8.1.177.4 'Fashioning in his hand the many manly skills of the poets and sages of old — <s>Agni</s> has become the lord of riches, of all riches, having accomplished all immortal deeds.' 8.1.177.5 'I call upon the golden-handed <s>Savitṛ</s> for protection — he is the perceiver of the divine station.' 8.1.177.6 'O <s>Savitṛ</s>, grant us desirable [wealth] today, desirable [wealth] tomorrow, desirable [wealth] day after day! Through your abundant dwelling, O god — by this prayer, may we share in desirable things!' 8.1.177.7 'Indeed thus you bear the cleft of the mountains, O <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth); you who [flow] forward and downward — by your greatness you shake, O Mighty One!'

children.text:
8.1.178.1 stómāsas tvā vicāriṇi práti ṣṭobhanty aktúbhiḥ
prá yā́ vā́jaṃ ná héṣantaṃ perúm ásyasy arjuni
8.1.178.2 r̥dūdáreṇa sákhyā saceya yó mā ná ríṣyed dhary-aśva pītáḥ
ayáṃ yás sómo nyádhāyy asmé tásmā índraṃ pratíram emy áccha
8.1.178.3 ā́pānta-manyus tr̥pála-prabharmā dhúniś śímīvāñ chárumā(g)ṃ r̥jīṣī́
sómo víśvāny atasā́ vánāni nā́rvā́g índraṃ pratimā́nāni debhuḥ
8.1.178.4 prá suvānás sóma r̥ta-yúś ciketéndrāya bráhma jamádagnir árcann
vŕ̥ṣāyantā́si śávasas turásyā́ntár yaccha gr̥ṇaté dhartráṃ dŕ̥(g)ṃha
8.1.178.5 sa-bā́dhas te mádaṃ ca śuṣmayáṃ ca bráhma náro brahma-kŕ̥tas saparyan
arkó vā yát turáte sóma-cakṣās tátréd índro dadhate pr̥tsú[*926] turyā́m[*927]
[*926] Text: pr̥thsú
[*927] VMP divides this verse making the second line the first line of chapter 179. The numbering is adjusted so that the complete verse comes at the end of chapter 178.
children.translated_text: 8.1.178.1 'The hymns of praise, O wandering one, sound forth to you at their times; you who set in motion the prize like a neighing [horse] — the silvery one.' 8.1.178.2 'May I be united in friendship with [him] of gentle womb — who, when drunk, would not harm me, O Lord of Bay Horses! This <s>Soma</s> which has been placed within us — for that I go eagerly toward <s>Indra</s>.' 8.1.178.3 'With fury satiated, of triple strength, roaring, of measured beauty, of victorious juices — <s>Soma</s> [presses through] all the woven [strainer-cloths] of the forest; no [counter-]measures have hindered <s>Indra</s>.' 8.1.178.4 'O <s>Soma</s>, being pressed, you perceive the cosmic order; <s>Jamadagni</s>, praising, composes the <s>brahman</s> (prayer) for <s>Indra</s>. You are eager with power, striving onward — bestow a hold upon the singer, make it firm!' 8.1.178.5 'With struggle — your exhilaration and fury; the men who have performed the <s>brahman</s> [honor] the <s>brahman</s>, attending [it]. When either the hymn or the Soma-seer hastens, there <s>Indra</s> wins the fourth [portion] in the battles.'

children.text:
8.1.179.1 váṣaṭ te viṣṇav āsá ā́ kr̥ṇomi tán me juṣasva śipi-viṣṭa havyám
várdhantu tvā suṣṭutáyo gíro me yūyáṃ pāta svastíbhis sádā naḥ
8.1.179.2 prá tát te adyá śipi-viṣṭa nā́māryáś śa(g)ṃsāmi vayúnāni vidvā́n
táṃ tvā gr̥ṇāmi tavásam átavīyān kṣáyantam asyá rájasaḥ parāké
8.1.179.3 kím ít te viṣṇo paricákṣyaṃ bhūt prá yád vavakṣé śipi-viṣṭó asmi
mā́ várpo asmád ápa gūha etád yád anyá-rūpas samithé babhū́tha
8.1.179.4 ágne dā́ daśúṣe rayíṃ vīrávantaṃ párīṇasaṃ śiśīhí nas sūnumátaḥ
8.1.179.5 dā́ no agne śatíno dā́s sahasríṇo duró ná vā́ja(gg)ṃ śrútyā ápā vr̥dhi
prā́cī dyā́vā-pr̥thivī́ bráhmaṇā kr̥dhi súvarṇá śukrám uṣáso ví didyutuḥ
children.translated_text: 8.1.179.1 'Hail (<s>vaṣaṭ</s>) to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s> — I make [an offering] at [your] seat; accept from me this oblation, O <s>Śipivista</s> (the Radiant One)! May the praises, the hymns, increase you — protect us always with blessings!' 8.1.179.2 'I shall proclaim today your name, O <s>Śipivista</s>, the noble [name]; knowing [your] courses, I praise you, the mighty one, mightier [than all] — you who dwell in the far distance of this realm.' 8.1.179.3 'What is to be seen of you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>? For you have declared: "I am <s>Śipivista</s>." Do not hide this form from us — [the form] in which you appeared of another appearance in battle.' 8.1.179.4 'O <s>Agni</s>, give to the worshipper wealth abounding in heroes, bestowing abundance! Sharpen us as ones having sons.' 8.1.179.5 'Give us, O <s>Agni</s>, [wealth] hundredfold, give [it] thousandfold! Open for us prizes, as a door [opens] to fame! Make heaven and earth advance by the sacred word (<s>brahman</s>)! The golden, the bright — the dawns have shone forth.'

children.text:
8.1.180.1 agnír dā dráviṇaṃ vīrá-peśā agnír ŕ̥ṣiṃ yás sahásrā sanóti
agnír diví havyám ā́ ta tanāgnér dhā́māni víbhr̥tā purutrā́
8.1.180.2 mā́ no márdhīr ā́ tū́ bhara
8.1.180.3 ghr̥táṃ ná pūtáṃ tanū́r arepā́ś śúci híraṇyam tát te rukmó ná rocata svadhāvaḥ
8.1.180.4 ubhé suścandra sarpíṣo dárvī śrīṇīṣa āsáni
utó na útpupūryā ukthéṣu śávásás páta íṣa(gg)ṃ stotŕ̥bhya ā́ bhara
8.1.180.5 vā́yo śatá(g)ṃ hárīṇāṃ yuvásva póṣyāṇām utá vā te sahasríṇo rátha ā́ yātu pā́jasā
8.1.180.6 prá yā́bhir yā́si dāśvā́(g)ṃsam ácchā niyúdbhir vāyav iṣṭáye duroṇé
ní no rayí(g)ṃ subhójasaṃ yuvehá ní vīrávad gávyam áśviyaṃ ca rā́dhaḥ
8.1.180.7 revátīr nas sadha-mā́da índre santu tuví-vājāḥ kṣumánto yā́bhir mádema
8.1.180.8 revā́(g)ṃ íd revátas stotā́ syā́t tvā́vato maghónaḥ préd u harivas śrutásya
children.translated_text: (8.1.180.1) '<s>Agni</s> gives wealth, adorned with heroes; <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Ṛṣi</s> who wins thousands. <s>Agni</s> [extends] the oblation in heaven for you — the abodes of <s>Agni</s> are distributed in many places.' (8.1.180.2) 'Do not neglect us; bring [it] here.' (8.1.180.3) 'Like purified ghee, the body without blemish, pure gold — that [splendor] of yours shines like a golden ornament, O self-empowered one.' (8.1.180.4) 'O beautiful one, may you mix the two ladles of ghee at the [altar] seat. Fill us up too. O lord of strength, bring nourishment for the praisers in the hymns.' (8.1.180.5) 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, yoke a hundred of your tawny steeds, your nourishing ones; or may your chariot of a thousand come with splendor.' (8.1.180.6) 'With those [mares] by which you go forth toward the worshipper, with your teams, O <s>Vāyu</s>, for the sacrifice in the dwelling — join to us here wealth of good nourishment, and heroic, cow-rich, and horse-rich bounty.' (8.1.180.7) 'May our rich praises in <s>Indra</s> be powerful, of abundant prizes, with nourishment — by which we may rejoice.' (8.1.180.8) 'Indeed, a rich praiser of the rich one may he be — of one so great a patron. Come forth indeed, O tawny-horsed one, of the renowned.'

children.text: 8.0.29 pŕ̥thívís sápáryán vídidyutuś ca rā́dháś catvā́ri ca
children.translated_text: (8.0.29) [Rubric:] '...worshipping the earth; ...the flashing and the bounty' — and four [mantras].

children.text:
8.1.181.1 viśva-jíte dhana-jíte svar-jíte satrā-jíte nr̥-jíta urvarā-jíte
aśva-jíte go-jíte ab-jíte bharéndrāya sómaṃ yajatā́ya haryatám
8.1.181.2 abhibhúve 'bhibhaṃgā́ya vanvaté 'ṣālhāya sáhamānāya vedháse
tuvigráye váhnaye duṣṭárītave satrā-sā́he náma índrāya vocata
8.1.181.3 satrā-sāhó jana-bhakṣó janaṃ-saháś cyavano yudhmó ánu jóṣam ukṣitáḥ vr̥taṃ-cayás sáhurir vikṣvāritá[*928] índrasya vocaṃ prá kr̥tā́ni vīryā
8.1.181.4 anānudó vr̥ṣabhó dódhato vadhó gaṃbhīrá r̥ṣvó ásamaṣṭa-kāvyaḥ
radhra-codáś śnáthano vīlitás pr̥thúr índras suyajñá uṣásas svar janat
8.1.181.5 yajñéna gātúm aptúro vividrire dhíyo hinvānā́ uśíjo manīṣíṇaḥ
abhisvárā niṣádā gā́ avasyáva índre hinvānā́ dráviṇāny āśata
[*928] Text: ikṣvāritá
children.translated_text: (8.1.181.1) 'To the all-conquering, wealth-conquering, heaven-conquering, ever-conquering, man-conquering, field-conquering, horse-conquering, cow-conquering, water-conquering one — bring the beloved <s>Soma</s> for <s>Indra</s>, the adorable.' (8.1.181.2) 'To the overpowering, the overwhelming, the winning, the unconquered, the victorious, the wise, the greatly devouring, the conveyor, the irresistible, the ever-conquering — speak obeisance to <s>Indra</s>.' (8.1.181.3) 'The ever-conquering, the people's nourisher, the overcomer of men, the shaker, the warrior, pleased at will, the breaker of obstructions, the enduring, stirred among the people — I shall declare the accomplished heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>.' (8.1.181.4) 'The unyielding bull, the weapon of the furious, deep, lofty, of unsurpassed poetic wisdom, the prodder of the weak, the striker, the broad, the firm — <s>Indra</s>, well-worshipped, generated the heavenly light from <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn).' (8.1.181.5) 'By sacrifice the zealous ones found the pathway, the eager sages urging [their] thoughts. The resonant ones, sitting down, seeking help for the cows — impelling [offerings] in <s>Indra</s>, they obtained riches.'

children.text:
8.1.182.1 índra śréṣṭhāni dráviṇāni dhéhi cíttiṃ dákṣasya subhagatvám asmé
póṣaṃ rayīṇā́m áriṣṭiṃ tanū́nāṃ svādmā́naṃ vācás sudinatvám áhnām
8.1.182.2 trí-kadrukeṣu mahiṣó yávāśiraṃ tuvi-śúṣmas
tr̥pátsómam apibad víṣṇunā sutáṃ yáthā́vaśat
sá īṃ mamāda máhi kárma kártave mahā́m urúṃ
saínaṃ saścad devó deváṃ satyám índraṃ satyá índuḥ
8.1.182.3 ádha tvíṣīmāṃ[*929] abhyójasā kríviṃ yudhā́bhavad
ā́ ródasī apr̥ṇad asya majmánā prá vāvr̥dhe
ádhattānyáṃ jaṭháre prém aricyata
saínaṃ saścad devó devám satyám índraṃ[*930] satyá índuḥ
8.1.182.4 sākáṃ jātáḥ krátunā sākám ójasā vavakṣitha
sākáṃ vr̥ddhó vīryais sāsahír mŕ̥dho vícarṣaṇiḥ
dā́tā rā́dhas stuvaté kā́myaṃ vásu saínaṃ sáścad devó devám satyám índraṃ[*931] satyá índuḥ
8.1.182.5 táva tyán náryaṃ[*932] nr̥tó 'pa indra prathamáṃ pūrvyáṃ diví pravā́cyaṃ kr̥tám
yád devásya śávasā prā́riṇā ásuṃ riṇáṃn apáḥ
bhuvad víśvam abhy ā́devam ójasā vidā́d ū́rjaṃ śatá-kratu vidā́d íṣam
[*929] Text: tvíṣīṃmāṃ
[*930] VMP omits saścad devó devám satyám índraṃ, which is in RV, and has = in its place in the text.
[*931] VMP omits devó devám satyám índraṃ, which is in RV, and has = in its place in the text.
[*932] Text: nárya
children.translated_text: (8.1.182.1) 'O <s>Indra</s>, bestow the best riches, wisdom, skill, good fortune upon us, increase of wealth, safety of bodies, sweetness of speech, and good days for our days.' (8.1.182.2) 'In the three <s>Trikadru</s> [cups], the great bull, mingled with barley, of mighty blowing — he drank the <s>Soma</s> pressed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as he wished, in a mighty, wide [draught], to perform the great deed. That god follows the god — the true <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop) [follows] the true <s>Indra</s>.' (8.1.182.3) 'Then with his vehemence and power he overcame the enemy <s>Krivi</s> in battle. He filled both heaven and earth with his might; he increased. He placed another in the belly and overflowed. That god follows the god — the true <s>Indu</s> [follows] the true <s>Indra</s>.' (8.1.182.4) 'Born together with resolve, together with strength, you have grown; together increased with heroic powers, you conquer enemies, O all-seeing one. The giver of desired wealth to the praiser — that god follows the god, the true <s>Indu</s> the true <s>Indra</s>.' (8.1.182.5) 'Your heroic [deed], O hero among heroes, O <s>Indra</s> — the first, the ancient, the praiseworthy deed in heaven: that by the power of the god you released the breath of life, releasing the waters. The whole universe came under divine power — the hundred-powered one found strength, found nourishment.'

children.text: 8.0.30 dráviṇāny āśatāpá ékañ ca
children.translated_text: (8.0.30) [Rubric:] '...they obtained riches; ...the waters' — and one [mantra].

children.text:
8.1.183.1 víṣṇave svā́hā
8.1.183.2 víṣṇave svastí-dā́ya svā́hā
8.1.183.3 víṣṇave sárvaṃ-dharāya svā́hā
8.1.183.4 víṣṇave sarva-goptré svā́hā
8.1.183.5 víṣṇave sarvā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.183.6 víṣṇave sarva-devā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.183.7 víṣṇave sarva-vedā́tmane svāhā
8.1.183.8 víṣṇave sarva-munī́nā́m ā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.183.9 víṣṇave yóga-sandhāraṇāya svā́hā
8.1.183.10 víṣṇave sárva-pratiṣṭhāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.183.1) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.2) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the bestower of well-being, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.3) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the upholder of all, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.4) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the protector of all, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.5) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the Self of all, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.6) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the Self of all gods, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.7) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the Self of all <s>Vedas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.8) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the Self of all sages (<s>munis</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.9) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the sustainer of <s>Yoga</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.183.10) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s> the foundation of all, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
8.1.184.1 nārāyaṇā́ya svā́hā
8.1.184.2 nārāyaṇā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.184.3 nārāyaṇā́ya sárva-devātmane svā́hā
8.1.184.4 nārāyaṇā́yéndra-rūpāya svā́hā
8.1.184.5 nārāyaṇā́ya sáṃyámánā́dhípátaye svā́hā
8.1.184.6 nārāyaṇā́ya sámbhógá-pátaye svā́hā
8.1.184.7 nārāyaṇā́ya sárva-tr̥pti-pradāya svā́hā
8.1.184.8 nārāyaṇā́yānántā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.184.9 nārāyaṇā́ya brahméśā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.184.10 nārāyaṇā́ya prajā́-pátaye svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.184.1) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.2) 'To the Self that is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.3) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Self of all gods, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.4) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in the form of <s>Indra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.5) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord of restraint (<s>Saṃyamana</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.6) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord of enjoyment (<s>Sambhoga</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.7) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the bestower of all satisfaction, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.8) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose self is <s>Ananta</s> (the Infinite), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.9) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose self is <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Īśa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.184.10) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Lord of Creatures (<s>Prajāpati</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
8.1.185.1 nārāyaṇā́yānántaśayanāya svā́hā
8.1.185.2 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya svā́hā
8.1.185.3 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya tri-dáśā́dhipataye svā́hā
8.1.185.4 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya vaṭā́kṣá-vā́sine svā́hā
8.1.185.5 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya pādā́rciṣe svā́hā
8.1.185.6 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya bālá-rū́piṇe svā́hā
8.1.185.7 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya māyā́-rū́piṇe svā́hā
8.1.185.8 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya prabódhine svā́hā
8.1.185.9 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya sárvādhiṣṭhānāya svā́hā
8.1.185.10 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya sárva-pravaraṇāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.185.1) 'To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> reclining on <s>Ananta</s> (the Infinite Serpent), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.2) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s> (the Meritorious <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.3) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord of the thirty gods, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.4) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s>, dwelling at the banyan tree's eye (<s>Vaṭākṣa-vāsin</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.5) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose feet are radiant (<s>Pādārci</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.6) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s> in the form of a child (<s>Bāla-rūpin</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.7) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s> in the form of <s>Māyā</s> (divine illusion), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.8) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Awakener (<s>Prabodhin</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.9) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s>, the substratum of all (<s>Sarvādhiṣṭhāna</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.185.10) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s>, the choice of all (<s>Sarva-pravaraṇa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
8.1.186.1 puṇya-nārāyaṇā́ya mū́rdhni sthānāya svā́hā
8.1.186.2 bā́lāya svā́hā
8.1.186.3 bā́lāya váṭa-patra-śā́yíne svā́hā
8.1.186.4 satyā́ya svā́hā
8.1.186.5 satya-niṣṭhā́ya svā́hā
8.1.186.6 satyā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.186.7 satya-nityā́ya svā́hā
8.1.186.8 sárvé tvá(g)ṃ hí satyé satyáṃ prátiṣṭhāya svā́hā
8.1.186.9 satyā́ya sárva-loka-pravartine svā́hā
8.1.186.10 satyātma-devā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.186.1) 'To <s>Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa</s>, stationed at the crown of the head, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.2) 'To the Child (<s>Bāla</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.3) 'To the Child who reclines on the banyan leaf (<s>Vaṭa-patra-śāyin</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.4) 'To <s>Satya</s> (Truth), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.5) 'To the one established in truth (<s>Satya-niṣṭha</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.6) 'To the Self of truth (<s>Satyātman</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.7) 'To the one who is eternally true (<s>Satya-nitya</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.8) 'You are all; indeed in truth, established in truth, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.9) 'To <s>Satya</s>, the one who sets all worlds in motion (<s>Sarva-loka-pravartin</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.186.10) 'To the god whose self is truth (<s>Satyātma-deva</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
8.1.187.1 satya-modā́ya svā́hā
8.1.187.2 satya-sopānakā́ya svā́hā
8.1.187.3 tvá(g)ṃ hí satyā́tmánth sátya-niṣṭhódbhavā́ya svā́hā
8.1.187.4 puruṣāya svā́hā
8.1.187.5 puruṣa-sa(gg)ṃstutā́ya svā́hā
8.1.187.6 puruṣa-samadhītā́ya svā́hā
8.1.187.7 puruṣa-niṣṭhā́ya svā́hā
8.1.187.8 puruṣā́tmáne svā́hā
8.1.187.9 puruṣa-puruṣā́ya svā́hā
8.1.187.10 puruṣā́ya jágan-mitrāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.187.1) 'To the one whose delight is truth (<s>Satya-moda</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.2) 'To the one who is the stairway of truth (<s>Satya-sopānaka</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.3) 'You indeed are the Self of truth — to the one born from establishment in truth (<s>Satya-niṣṭhodbhava</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.4) 'To <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.5) 'To the one praised as <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Puruṣa-saṃstuta</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.6) 'To the one studied as <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Puruṣa-samadhīta</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.7) 'To the one established in <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Puruṣa-niṣṭha</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.8) 'To the Self of <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Puruṣātman</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.9) 'To the <s>Puruṣa</s> of <s>Puruṣas</s> (<s>Puruṣa-puruṣa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.187.10) 'To <s>Puruṣa</s>, the friend of the world (<s>Jagan-mitra</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
8.1.188.1 puruṣā́ya jágad-ādhārāya svā́hā
8.1.188.2 puruṣā́ya jágat-pravartine svā́hā
8.1.188.3 puruṣā́ya jágad-dhetave svā́hā
8.1.188.4 víṣṇu-krīḍā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.188.5 bhūmi-saṅkrīḍā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.188.6 jagan-modā́ya svā́hā
8.1.188.7 jagad-dhitā́ya svā́hā
8.1.188.8 nikhuryapā́ya[*933] svā́hā
8.1.188.9 kā́ya svā́hā
8.1.188.10 kásmai svā́hā
[*933] According to MW, p. 545, nikhuryapa = Name of Viṣṇu in TS.
children.translated_text: (8.1.188.1) 'To <s>Puruṣa</s>, the support of the world (<s>Jagad-ādhāra</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.2) 'To <s>Puruṣa</s>, the one who sets the world in motion (<s>Jagat-pravartin</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.3) 'To <s>Puruṣa</s>, the cause of the world (<s>Jagad-dhetu</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.4) 'To the one whose self is the play of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu-krīḍātman</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.5) 'To the one whose self is the play of the earth (<s>Bhūmi-saṅkrīḍātman</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.6) 'To the delight of the world (<s>Jagan-moda</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.7) 'To the benefactor of the world (<s>Jagad-dhita</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.8) 'To <s>Nikhuryapa</s> (a name of <s>Viṣṇu</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.9) 'To the "Who?" (<s>Ka</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.188.10) 'To the "For whom?" (<s>Kasmai</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text:
8.1.189.1 kátamásmai svā́hā
8.1.189.2 sárvasmai svā́hā
8.1.189.3 víṣṇave svā́hā
8.1.189.4 víṣṇave mantra-sandruhaṇā́ya svā́hā
8.1.189.5 dhruvarūpíṇe svā́hā
8.1.189.6 saṃvr̥tā́tmane svā́hā
8.1.189.7 saṃprīti-karā́ya svā́hā
8.1.189.8 sarva-śubhá-pradā́ya svā́hā
8.1.189.9 aśubha-nāśā́ya svā́hā
8.1.189.10 śubha-saṃbarhaṇā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: (8.1.189.1) 'To the "To which one?" (<s>Katamasmai</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.2) 'To the All (<s>Sarvasmai</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.3) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.4) 'To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the one who binds the <s>mantras</s> together (<s>Mantra-sandruhaṇa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.5) 'To the one of steadfast form (<s>Dhruva-rūpin</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.6) 'To the one whose self is enclosed (<s>Saṃvṛtātman</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.7) 'To the one who brings perfect delight (<s>Saṃprīti-kara</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.8) 'To the bestower of all auspiciousness (<s>Sarva-śubha-prada</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.9) 'To the destroyer of inauspiciousness (<s>Aśubha-nāśa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' (8.1.189.10) 'To the one who gathers all auspiciousness (<s>Śubha-saṃbarhaṇa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.translated_text: To the meritorious one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, powerful and prosperous, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, abounding in victory and prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, generator of desire and bliss, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, all-blissful, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, fully prosperous, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, treasury of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, support of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, abode of boons, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, honored by the worlds, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, the wondrous, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, without beginning or end, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, of immeasurable greatness, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, supremely benevolent, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, foundation of all, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, foundation of all the worlds, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, bringer of auspiciousness to all the worlds, <s>svāhā</s>! To the meritorious one, the Self of all, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
8.0.31 pratiṣṭhā́ya svā́hā
prajā́-pataye svā́hā sárva-praharaṇāya svā́hā satyātma-devā́ya svā́hā jágan-mitrāya svā́hā
kásmai svā́hā śubha-sambarhaṇā́ya svā́hā
lóka-sambhavanā́ya svā́hāṣṭaú ca
children.translated_text: To the established one, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of creatures), <s>svāhā</s>! To the one bearing all weapons, <s>svāhā</s>! To the god whose Self is truth, <s>svāhā</s>! To the friend of the universe, <s>svāhā</s>! To the one [known as] 'Who?', <s>svāhā</s>! To the one who removes auspiciously, <s>svāhā</s>! To the one honored by the worlds, <s>svāhā</s>! — eight [sections].

children.text: Bhágávác-chátā́ṣṭákám
children.translated_text: The Hundred-and-Eight [Names] of the Lord (<s>Bhagavac-chatāṣṭakam</s>)

children.text:
8.2.1.1 nārāyaṇā́ya svā́hā
8.2.1.2 narā́ya svā́hā
8.2.1.3 śaúraye svā́ha
8.2.1.4 cákra-pāṇaye svā́hā
8.2.1.5 janā́rdanā́ya svā́hā
8.2.1.6 vā́sudevāya svā́hā
8.2.1.7 jagad-yónaye svā́hā
8.2.1.8 vāmanā́ya svā́hā
8.2.1.9 jñā́na-pañjarāya svā́hā
8.2.1.10 śrī́-vállabhāya svā́hā
children.translated_text: To <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Nara</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Śauri</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the discus-handed one (<s>Cakrapāṇi</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Janārdana</s> (stirrer of men), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the source of the universe, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Vāmana</s> (the dwarf), <s>svāhā</s>! To the cage of knowledge, <s>svāhā</s>! To the beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
8.2.2.1 jagannāthā́ya svā́hā
8.2.2.2 catúr-mū́rtaye svā́hā
8.2.2.3 catur-bhujā́ya svā́hā
8.2.2.4 gajendra-ghnā́ya svā́hā
8.2.2.5 gajārti-ghnā́ya svā́hā
8.2.2.6 kéśavāya svā́hā
8.2.2.7 kleśa-nāśanā́ya svā́hā
8.2.2.8 kaíṭabhāraye svā́hā
8.2.2.9 avidyā́raye svā́hā
8.2.2.10 kāma-dā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: To the lord of the universe (<s>Jagannātha</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To the four-formed one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the four-armed one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the slayer of the lord of elephants, <s>svāhā</s>! To the destroyer of the elephant's distress, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Keśava</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the destroyer of afflictions, <s>svāhā</s>! To the foe of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the foe of ignorance, <s>svāhā</s>! To the granter of desires, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
8.2.3.1 kamalekṣaṇā́ya svā́hā
8.2.3.2 kaṃsá-śátrave svā́hā
8.2.3.3 ághā́rā́taye svā́hā
8.2.3.4 kākut-sthā́ya svā́hā
8.2.3.5 khaga-vā́hanāya svā́hā
8.2.3.6 nīlāmbhújá-dyutaye svā́hā
8.2.3.7 nityā́ya svā́hā
8.2.3.8 nitya-tr̥ptā́ya svā́hā
8.2.3.9 nirā́śrayā́ya svā́hā
8.2.3.10 nityā́nandā́ya svā́hā
children.translated_text: To the lotus-eyed one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the enemy of <s>Agha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Kākutstha</s> (descendant of Kakutstha), <s>svāhā</s>! To the one whose vehicle is a bird (<s>Garuḍa</s>), <s>svāhā</s>! To the one with the radiance of a blue lotus, <s>svāhā</s>! To the eternal one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the eternally satisfied one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the one without dependence, <s>svāhā</s>! To the eternally blissful one, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
8.2.4.1 surā́dhyakṣā́ya svā́ḥā
8.2.4.2 nirvíkalpāya svā́hā
8.2.4.3 nirañjánā́ya svā́hā
8.2.4.4 brahmaṇyā́ya svā́hā
8.2.4.5 pr̥thivī-nāthā́ya svā́hā
